egSxU75OZ3.one_liner: Neyman-orthogonal learner for conditional geodesic treatment effects on Riemannian manifolds, with pointwise confidence sets.
egSxU75OZ3.problem: Existing Frechet-regression and geodesic causal work does not give Neyman-orthogonal pointwise estimation and inference for covariate-dependent geodesic effects with manifold-valued outcomes from observational data.
egSxU75OZ3.method: They define the conditional geodesic treatment effect through treatment-specific conditional Frechet means and develop the Geodesic Orthogonal learner (GO-learner). A joint error expansion propagates errors in estimating the two means through the logarithm map, with propensity and conditional regression errors entering through products, yielding convergence guarantees and asymptotically valid pointwise confidence sets.
egSxU75OZ3.key_idea: Estimate the effect as a log-map tangent vector between two conditional Frechet means with an orthogonal score, so nuisance errors enter only as products.
egSxU75OZ3.evidence: Convergence and confidence-set theory, plus synthetic experiments on a nonlinear covariance-matrix benchmark (2x2 SPD outcomes, per reviewers) with nuisance misspecification and coverage checks.
egSxU75OZ3.claimed_gains: GO-learner achieves lower average MSE than the competing Frechet-regression estimators for all tested sample sizes n>4000 in the nonlinear covariance-matrix benchmark, and squared Monte Carlo bias is substantially smaller when at least one nuisance class is correctly specified.
egSxU75OZ3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the orthogonal estimator, which jointly accounts for uncertainty in both conditional Frechet means and keeps the familiar nuisance-product error structure, is a coherent and useful methodological extension.
egSxU75OZ3.main_concern: The paper lacks a concrete scientific motivation and any real-data experiment, since evaluation is limited to synthetic 2x2 SPD outcomes with known geometry assumed.

OIB8GJ5llR.one_liner: Uses Muon's momentum orthogonalization to control spectral structure in reward-guided initial-noise optimization without enforcing Gaussianity
OIB8GJ5llR.problem: Reward-guided noise optimization approximates the feasible latent region by regularizing or projecting toward Gaussian properties, although pretrained generators tolerate substantial non-Gaussian deviations.
OIB8GJ5llR.method: Interventions on three generators show that generation quality depends on how noise is arranged rather than on entry-wise Gaussianity, motivating a weaker spectral description of the admissible source space. Reward-driven updates are then run with Muon, whose momentum orthogonalization flattens the update spectrum.
OIB8GJ5llR.key_idea: Flatten the spectrum of reward-driven noise updates with Muon's momentum orthogonalization, controlling spectral structure instead of enforcing Gaussian entry-wise statistics.
OIB8GJ5llR.evidence: Interventions on three recent generators (83 per generator according to a reviewer) and experiments on aesthetic and text-aligned generation comparing target and held-out rewards, plus an appendix optimizer study.
OIB8GJ5llR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the analysis of non-Gaussian noise tolerance and arrangement sensitivity interesting and well supported by interventions, with Muon a simple, well-motivated consequence.
OIB8GJ5llR.main_concern: The link from the arrangement analysis to Muon is indirect, and the method is an existing optimizer applied to a new variable, with an appendix operator (Fourier-block singular-value flattening) scoring slightly higher.

8QDrmv2Qn9.one_liner: Latent diffusion generates reasoning trajectories for RL, with hierarchical latent-text rollouts separating latent quality from decoding luck
8QDrmv2Qn9.problem: Token-level RL optimizes over discrete tokens, which mismatches semantic, trajectory-level reasoning decisions and collapses diversity, while latent-space RL faces a credit-assignment problem between the latent and its decoded text.
8QDrmv2Qn9.method: A diffusion model generates latent reasoning trajectories by iterative denoising, and hierarchical latent-text rollouts decode several answers per latent and score the latent by their mean reward. Reviewers also describe a repulsion-based diversity guidance that adjusts geometric distances between latent trajectories.
8QDrmv2Qn9.key_idea: Run RL on diffusion-generated latent reasoning trajectories, scoring each latent by the mean reward of several decoded answers to separate reasoning quality from decoding luck.
8QDrmv2Qn9.evidence: Code generation and math reasoning benchmarks compared with token-level RL and code-specific models, with pass@k and semantic-diversity analyses.
8QDrmv2Qn9.claimed_gains: Outperforms token-level RL by 10.5% on code generation and 6.5% on math reasoning in pass@1.
8QDrmv2Qn9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the diversity-collapse problem important and the latent-space solution with hierarchical rollouts sound, with comprehensive experiments including pass@k results.
8QDrmv2Qn9.main_concern: There is no direct validation that latent-space geometry (distances, diversity guidance) corresponds to semantic diversity, and averaging over decodes does not fully separate latent credit from decoder credit.

WDdONsxZOk.one_liner: Reduces dynamic regret to switching regret by constructing an unbiased low-switching random sequence for any comparator sequence
WDdONsxZOk.problem: Existing methods that attain optimal dynamic regret for strongly convex and exp-concave losses remain analytically intricate or computationally demanding.
WDdONsxZOk.method: For any comparator sequence, the paper builds an auxiliary random sequence that is unbiased at each round with controlled variance and few switches. With suitable surrogate losses, dynamic regret splits into expected switching regret against that sequence plus a variance-controlled approximation error, so any switching-regret algorithm can be plugged in.
WDdONsxZOk.key_idea: Replace the comparator sequence with an unbiased random sequence that rarely switches, so dynamic regret equals expected switching regret plus a variance-controlled error.
WDdONsxZOk.evidence: Regret-bound theory instantiated with existing switching-regret algorithms for strongly convex and exp-concave losses.
WDdONsxZOk.claimed_gains: Obtains an O~(T^(1/3) P_T^(2/3)) dynamic regret bound for strongly convex losses and O~(d^(2/3) T^(1/3) P_T^(2/3)) for exp-concave losses.
WDdONsxZOk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the reduction simple, elegant and well written, showing that controlling switching regret suffices to control dynamic regret.
WDdONsxZOk.main_concern: The significance and efficiency gains over prior work are not well argued: the computational comparison is informal, and the only clear improvement over prior bounds is the dependence on dimension d.

CSvwscsOjR.one_liner: Single unified model for face, hair, and head transfer using a mixture-of-experts (BioMoE) and swapping-based data construction.
CSvwscsOjR.problem: Deepface generation is task-specific, and unifying tasks is hard because of data scarcity and cross-task conflicts from heterogeneous attribute transformations.
CSvwscsOjR.method: Builds a unified data construction strategy (swapping-based corruption of real images, supervised against the original image) and BioMoE, a mixture-of-experts model with a two-stage training strategy that disentangles task-specific knowledge.
CSvwscsOjR.key_idea: Route tasks through a mixture-of-experts (BioMoE) with two-stage training to separate task-specific knowledge, while swapping-based corruption supplies training data across tasks.
CSvwscsOjR.evidence: Experiments compare against multi-task and task-specific methods on face transfer, reenactment, hair transfer and head transfer, with generalization to unseen tasks (lip, eye, glasses) via minimal fine-tuning, and ablations on data corruption and BioMoE versus naive sharing.
CSvwscsOjR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that handling several tasks in one model is practically useful, results are competitive with unified and task-specific methods, and the swapping-based data construction is well motivated and supported by ablations.
CSvwscsOjR.main_concern: The claim that the unified model beats task-specific models is weakly supported (small differences, no variance), and the contribution and cost of individual BioMoE components are not isolated.

68GxE5Vrso.one_liner: Agent builds executable multiphysics worlds from video and probes them with simulation to answer physical-reasoning questions.
68GxE5Vrso.problem: Direct VLM inference is unreliable on complex physical reasoning, while predefined tool pipelines depend on task-specific priors that limit generalization.
68GxE5Vrso.method: ATW has two adaptive stages: World Modeling calibrates a world from video (CEM-based system identification) and World Probing queries, simulates and intervenes on it for question-relevant evidence, using the Warp-based PolyWorld Engine for rigid bodies, soft bodies, cloth, ropes and fluids.
68GxE5Vrso.key_idea: Calibrate an executable simulated world from video, then run question-directed simulations and interventions on it, letting the agent choose how to model and probe.
68GxE5Vrso.evidence: Evaluated on CLEVRER, ContPhy and three real-world scenarios with Gemini-3-Flash as base VLM, with ablations on world modeling and a cross-backbone experiment with two VLM backbones.
68GxE5Vrso.claimed_gains: With Gemini-3-Flash as base VLM, ATW achieves 80.82% overall per-question accuracy (the abstract is truncated after this figure).
68GxE5Vrso.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the formulation separating world building from world probing is clear and well motivated, results on physical-reasoning benchmarks are strong, and the ablations are useful.
68GxE5Vrso.main_concern: Gains are not cleanly attributed (extra perception tools, simulation rounds and unequal inputs versus baselines such as PhysMind), and the real-world evaluation is small at about 60 examples.

lDfs80UfAL.one_liner: WorldRoPE integrates rotary embeddings in closed form over Gaussian world-frame token supports so multi-view attention handles uncertain depth.
lDfs80UfAL.problem: In multi-view attention, patch coordinates are defined per image, so the same 3D point has different coordinates across views and cannot establish cross-view correspondence.
lDfs80UfAL.method: At each layer, back-projects each patch token into volumetric Gaussian primitives in a shared world frame, projects them into the query view to get a distribution of key locations, and integrates the rotary operator over it in closed form with covariance-dependent attenuation; it reduces to deterministic RoPE when the support collapses to a point.
lDfs80UfAL.key_idea: Take the expectation of the rotary operator over a mixture of Gaussian 3D hypotheses for each token, so attention is attenuated by positional uncertainty.
lDfs80UfAL.evidence: Plug-and-play evaluation on novel-view synthesis, depth estimation and feed-forward 3D reconstruction (including VGGT and Objaverse per reviews), with unseen-set generalization.
lDfs80UfAL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the closed-form expected rotary operator is a principled, elegant formulation that reduces to RoPE and gives consistent plug-and-play gains across three tasks.
lDfs80UfAL.main_concern: Some improvements are marginal with no variance across runs reported, and the contribution relative to RayRoPE and the added computational cost need clearer treatment.

96sojUA2ug.one_liner: Web2LongTraj mines web corpora for audited agent trajectories and expands them into long-horizon mid-training data with two operators.
96sojUA2ug.problem: Long-horizon agent trajectories are expensive to obtain because existing pipelines synthesize them in manually engineered executable environments.
96sojUA2ug.method: Screens 317 million web records for multi-step problem-solving records and compiles 1.15 million source-grounded, audited trajectories, then expands them with AnchorStretch (inserting similar episodes between a premise and a dependent step) and ArtifactStitch (composing multi-task sessions through a graph of shared artifacts).
96sojUA2ug.key_idea: Two operators lengthen short trajectories: AnchorStretch inserts topically similar episodes between a premise and its dependent step, and ArtifactStitch joins trajectories sharing artifacts and working contexts.
96sojUA2ug.evidence: Mid-training of Olmo-3-7B and Olmo-3-32B against equal-budget baselines on tool calling, multi-step interaction, long-horizon memory and general benchmarks, with ablations over model size and training settings.
96sojUA2ug.claimed_gains: A 1.90B-token audited pool is expanded to 10.6B long-horizon trajectory tokens and gives consistent gains over equal-budget baselines, with reviews citing mean gains of 4.7 and 9.9 points at 7B under a 60B-token budget.
96sojUA2ug.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the corpus-first pipeline is a practical, scalable alternative to environment-first synthesis, with matched-budget experiments and broad ablations supporting its value.
96sojUA2ug.main_concern: Auditing checks only that observations look like machine output, so source fidelity, execution validity and state consistency of stitched sessions are unverified, and the control mixture contains no agentic data.

QZLw9EZ9KA.one_liner: Dion3 speeds Muon with Gram Newton-Schulz, symmetric GPU kernels, megabatching, and orthogonalizing only a fraction of momentum rows.
QZLw9EZ9KA.problem: Muon's cubic-time Newton-Schulz orthogonalization and the communication needed when weights are sharded add overhead that erodes its benefits.
QZLw9EZ9KA.method: Revises Muon at several levels: Gram Newton-Schulz reduces orthogonalization FLOPs, CuteDSL kernels exploit symmetry, megabatching reduces communication, and an update rule orthogonalizes only a selected fraction of momentum-matrix rows per step. It ships in the dion package as a drop-in Muon replacement.
QZLw9EZ9KA.key_idea: Newton-Schulz iterations are run in Gram form with symmetry-exploiting kernels, and each step orthogonalizes only a selected fraction of momentum-matrix rows.
QZLw9EZ9KA.evidence: Training comparisons with Muon (including a 418M model and large runs with a 1B model on 100B tokens), Gram-Newton-Schulz-only experiments across four architectures and two coefficient families, and optimizer step-time measurements.
QZLw9EZ9KA.claimed_gains: Dion3 matches or improves on Muon's loss while reducing optimizer step time by up to 6x, and its update rule improves on Dion in both speed and performance.
QZLw9EZ9KA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the speedups are practical, the pip-installable packages make it a drop-in Muon replacement, and the Gram Newton-Schulz and kernel work is well supported by experiments and appendices.
QZLw9EZ9KA.main_concern: No matched comparison against Dion, TRION or block-orthogonalization methods supports the claimed advantage, the 418M run takes 20% longer to reach loss 3.2, and large runs are limited to 1B parameters and 100B tokens.

QQ74GYa5tD.one_liner: CLAG-SNN preserves nonlinear dependencies at the local scale and suppresses them at the global scale in spiking point-cloud networks.
QQ74GYa5tD.problem: Discrete spiking representations and irregular point clouds make it hard for SNNs to preserve local geometry while forming high-level semantic abstractions.
QQ74GYa5tD.method: Hierarchical Structure-aware Token Compaction (HSTC) preserves local geometric dependencies through structure-aware token aggregation and compaction, and Nonlinearity-Aware Abstraction Bottleneck (NAAB) suppresses redundant input-feature nonlinear coupling to abstract compact tokens into global semantics.
QQ74GYa5tD.key_idea: Regulate nonlinear dependency in opposite directions by scale, preserving it before and after compression locally and suppressing it between inputs and spiking features globally.
QQ74GYa5tD.evidence: Experiments on multiple 3D point-cloud benchmarks (reviews cite ModelNet40 classification, SemanticKITTI segmentation and KITTI detection), with ablations, robustness analysis and a generalization theorem.
QQ74GYa5tD.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract claims consistent improvements over the baseline and higher inference speed, but the speed figure is cut off.
QQ74GYa5tD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the idea of regulating dependencies differently at local and global scales well motivated, with evaluations across classification, segmentation and detection showing accuracy and efficiency gains.
QQ74GYa5tD.main_concern: The generalization theorem is not valid because Assumption 3 directly assumes the HSIC-to-distortion relationships that need to be justified.

8OuDiCC4lw.one_liner: MOST-OPSD distills transcript-generated speech priors into a neural speech decoder via multi-teacher representation alignment and privileged self-distillation.
8OuDiCC4lw.problem: Discrete phoneme labels give limited guidance on continuous speech dynamics and graded phoneme similarity, which limits decoding accuracy and generalization from limited neural recordings.
8OuDiCC4lw.method: MOST aligns neural representations at multiple stages with structured speech representations through independent projections and a length-aware Soft-DTW loss. OPSD distills speech-conditioned phoneme distributions, queried with current neural states, through a shared phoneme head.
8OuDiCC4lw.key_idea: Align neural stages with several speech-teacher representations via Soft-DTW and distill a speech-conditioned phoneme posterior into a neural-only decoder through a shared phoneme head.
8OuDiCC4lw.evidence: Brain-to-Text Benchmark '24 hidden test set, supplementary results on Brain-to-Text '25, and ablations of components, teacher views, shuffling and data fraction reported in reviews.
8OuDiCC4lw.claimed_gains: Word error rate of 3.63% on the Brain-to-Text '24 hidden test set for the complete system with the language model.
8OuDiCC4lw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the speech-informed supervision effective, with strong WER on a public benchmark, ablations of both transfer paths, and no extra modality needed at inference.
8OuDiCC4lw.main_concern: The ablations do not isolate which part of the distillation design helps (no matched ordinary-KD or reverse-KL baseline), and novelty against earlier neural-audio alignment work such as MONA-LISA is questioned.

pIJ0FMoWhq.one_liner: Agent-Reflex mines reflection meta-skills from noisy tool environments and trains agents with reflective SFT and on-policy RL.
pIJ0FMoWhq.problem: MCP tool services return noisy feedback and users intervene to correct agents, yet existing methods give limited supervision for reflection learning and failure recovery.
pIJ0FMoWhq.method: Reflection Skill Discovery injects tool-feedback perturbations into environment scaling, samples a diverse LLM pool, mines matched success-failure pairs and summarizes reusable reflection meta-skills. ReSFT turns skills into supervision for self-reflection, skill recovery and user-centric correction, and ORPO combines agentic RL under noise with reflection-guided on-policy distillation.
pIJ0FMoWhq.key_idea: Mine matched success-failure pairs in perturbed environments into reusable reflection skills, then internalize them via skill-based SFT and RL with reflection-guided on-policy distillation.
pIJ0FMoWhq.evidence: Six agent benchmark suites, with reviews citing comparisons against GRPO, REINFORCE++, DAPO and two noisy-feedback methods, and ablations on AgentNoiseBench.
pIJ0FMoWhq.claimed_gains: not stated in the abstract; a review cites an overall Table 1 score of 57.6 versus 53.6 for Agent-World and 50.9 for EnvScaler.
pIJ0FMoWhq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that noisy tool feedback and user corrections are a realistic, well-motivated problem and that the proposed solution is sensible.
pIJ0FMoWhq.main_concern: Baselines are not matched to the many added components (large model pool, stronger analyzers), so the benefit of the mined reflection skills is not isolated.

ptNmbmCdj3.one_liner: Attributes loss spikes to LM-head quantization error and mitigates them by using SGD with momentum on the LM head.
ptNmbmCdj3.problem: Loss spikes in LM pretraining waste compute, and delayed terminal divergences ('time-bomb spikes') linked to output-logit growth emerge only after prolonged training.
ptNmbmCdj3.method: Replaces AdamW on the LM head with SGD with momentum to suppress logit growth and improve stability over long training horizons. It also shows that existing mitigations from the literature all reduce quantization error.
ptNmbmCdj3.key_idea: Time-bomb spikes are driven by finite-precision error from growing LM-head logits, so suppressing logit growth with SGD-momentum on the LM head reduces that error.
ptNmbmCdj3.evidence: Analysis showing LM-head quantization error rises before spikes, and that lower precision accelerates spikes while higher precision improves stability; reviews note the experiments use setups built to trigger spikes (high learning rates, small batch size).
ptNmbmCdj3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the analysis systematic and insightful, with a simple LM-head SGD-M fix that is easy to implement and that ties existing mitigations to a shared numerical mechanism.
ptNmbmCdj3.main_concern: Evidence is mostly correlational and drawn from setups designed to trigger spikes, so the causal role of finite-precision error and generalization to normal pretraining are not established.

Z61ILDDhQ1.one_liner: Tokenizer training that enforces Semantic Affine Consistency between direct noisy-latent semantic predictions and semantics of posterior-mean clean latents.
Z61ILDDhQ1.problem: Existing tokenizers train a projector to predict semantics directly from noisy latents, which predicts the average of clean-image semantics rather than the semantic of the averaged clean latents.
Z61ILDDhQ1.method: The semantic recovery error is decomposed orthogonally into the optimal direct-prediction error and the gap between the two semantic predictions, and that gap defines Semantic Affine Consistency (SAC). Msac is a tokenizer-side proxy for SAC, and per the reviews training uses GSCT and Posterior Mean Semantic Alignment (PMSA).
Z61ILDDhQ1.key_idea: Require consistency between the semantics predicted directly from the noisy latent and the semantics decoded from the posterior-mean clean latent.
Z61ILDDhQ1.evidence: Msac is checked across several tokenizers and diffusion model scales against SiT-XL gFID; reviews note AffineTok is trained on top of RecTok for class-conditional ImageNet-256 generation.
Z61ILDDhQ1.claimed_gains: Msac reaches a Pearson correlation of 0.960 with SiT-XL gFID; the generation results are cut off in the abstract.
Z61ILDDhQ1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the theoretical decomposition gives a clear, well-motivated view of the mismatch in existing semantic supervision, with promising generation results and a method that is easy to use.
Z61ILDDhQ1.main_concern: Experiments are narrow, with AffineTok trained only on RecTok for class-conditional ImageNet-256, and the link between the squared-loss theory and the practical PMSA objective is not fully validated.

V0Bjj1EaVe.one_liner: Single-image relighting by fine-tuning a pixel-space flow model to output native HDR, with a light-transport linearity constraint.
V0Bjj1EaVe.problem: Prior relighting methods modify the pretrained model's conditioning pathways and mostly produce LDR outputs through LDR-trained VAEs, which lose pretrained knowledge, fine source detail, and the physical nature of light transport.
V0Bjj1EaVe.method: Conditions are expressed in a form the pretrained model already accepts, the model predicts HDR directly in pixel space, and a linearity constraint based on the additivity of light transport is imposed. It is fine-tuned only on paired synthetic single-object images.
V0Bjj1EaVe.key_idea: Conform relighting conditions to the pretrained model, predict HDR in pixel space, and constrain outputs to be additive under summed lights (light-transport linearity).
V0Bjj1EaVe.evidence: Fine-tuned on paired synthetic single-object images and evaluated on complex real-world scenes; reviews mention 192 real-photo comparisons and OLATverse results.
V0Bjj1EaVe.claimed_gains: Claims to outperform previous methods even on complex real-world scenes; no numbers are stated.
V0Bjj1EaVe.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the light-transport linearity constraint is the clearest contribution, with a clean derivation, and that the results and preservation of source detail are strong.
V0Bjj1EaVe.main_concern: Gains are hard to attribute to the stated design choices, since baselines differ in backbone, data, and evaluation protocol and the ablations do not test the alternative designs.

HNZY0zgzZX.one_liner: Replaces the steering-layer MLP with a supervised transcoder, then fits steering directions on the frozen replacement.
HNZY0zgzZX.problem: Steering a model toward a target behavior can degrade other useful behaviors, including safety behavior.
HNZY0zgzZX.method: STR learns a replacement for the MLP computation at the steering layer through supervision for target control, non-target preservation, and fidelity without steering. Selected steering methods then fit their directions on the frozen replacement while keeping their own fitting objectives.
HNZY0zgzZX.key_idea: Train the layer's MLP replacement with preservation supervision so that any steering direction fitted afterward inherits protection against side effects.
HNZY0zgzZX.evidence: Three steering methods on Gemma and Llama models, with Corrigibility preferences, SALAD-Bench for training and in-distribution evaluation, and HarmBench, AdvBench, and StrongREJECT for out-of-distribution tests.
HNZY0zgzZX.claimed_gains: For target-only supervised steering vectors, pooled out-of-distribution attack success rate falls from 42.46% to 14.42% on Gemma-3-4B and from 34.97% to 12.91% on Gemma-3-12B.
HNZY0zgzZX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the idea of making the representation suitable for steering, rather than only optimizing the steering direction, interesting, with experiments across several steering methods, model families, and safety datasets.
HNZY0zgzZX.main_concern: Evaluation scope is limited: one fixed steering strength, a single Corrigibility-to-safety pairing that may not transfer to other behaviors, and unclear effects of the MLP replacement on general capabilities.

Ycx6kBNzAy.one_liner: Learns when and how to compress billion-edge graphs into answer-preserving certificate graphs before LLM tool execution.
Ycx6kBNzAy.problem: On large graphs, tool execution for LLM graph reasoning includes much computation unrelated to the answer, and compressing the graph can cost more than the execution it saves.
Ycx6kBNzAy.method: CAGR learns compression strategies through Certificate Compression Optimization, which combines toolchain search with LLM policy improvement, and a lightweight Compression Gate weighs further compression cost against execution savings to decide when to execute.
Ycx6kBNzAy.key_idea: Compress to an instance-dependent Certificate graph that preserves the answer, and gate further compression by comparing its cost with predicted execution savings.
Ycx6kBNzAy.evidence: GraphLarge, a new benchmark extending LLM graph reasoning benchmarks to billion-edge scale across 28 domain-task settings (abstract truncated).
Ycx6kBNzAy.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the compression-cost trade-off is a significant overlooked bottleneck and that GraphLarge, covering 28 domain-task settings up to billion-edge scale, is a useful testbed with substantial evaluation.
Ycx6kBNzAy.main_concern: Reviewers question the LLM's role, since the graph problems have established solvers and a simple cost-prediction gate, and cite heavy tool-library specialization, synthetic edge weights, and unquantified benchmark and training cost.

AWj9yXEzcr.one_liner: Compensation-aware rounding and improved error compensation for GPTQ-style LLM quantization, built on a shared compensation representation.
AWj9yXEzcr.problem: GPTQ-style methods choose each column's rounding with RTN independently of later compensation, treating error formation and error compensation as separate stages.
AWj9yXEzcr.method: CARE-Q derives a shared compensation representation and uses it in DiCR for compensation-aware rounding and in ODPP for enhanced error compensation.
AWj9yXEzcr.key_idea: Choose each column's rounding using diagonal and off-diagonal signals from the compensation that later columns will apply, instead of plain round-to-nearest.
AWj9yXEzcr.evidence: Experiments across diverse LLMs and quantization settings, with reviews citing Llama and Qwen models at multiple scales including aggressive 2-bit settings.
AWj9yXEzcr.claimed_gains: Consistently outperforms leading compensation-based quantization methods and complements representative transformation-based methods (no numbers stated in the abstract).
AWj9yXEzcr.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the problem formulation clear and the experiments broad, with consistent gains across Llama and Qwen models, including 2-bit settings.
AWj9yXEzcr.main_concern: Reviewers question whether the theory supports the method, since GPTQ already rounds after compensating earlier errors and the derivation assumes continuous adjustment of unprocessed weights that are later quantized.

0IJBxo578w.one_liner: Shows blind-replacement process scores for visual agents mostly reflect crop-turn structure, not pixels, and separates belief target from credit placement.
0IJBxo578w.problem: A common process score contrasts a judge's belief under a real image and a blind reference and reads it as visual credit, but it mixes answer parameterization with crop-turn structure.
0IJBxo578w.method: The authors decompose the score across serialization, path, and judge settings, and separate the belief target from the credited part of the turn. Under a shared GRPO setup they compare option-posterior turn credit with mass-matched, uniform, shuffled, and pixel-level credit.
0IJBxo578w.key_idea: Decompose blind-replacement contrasts into structural and pixel increments, and use an option-posterior belief target with credit placed on the right part of the turn.
0IJBxo578w.evidence: V*-Bench and HR-Bench-4K, 32 serialization, path, and judge settings, and a shared GRPO training setup.
0IJBxo578w.claimed_gains: Annotated crops improve answer accuracy over matched distractors by 8.9-10.5 points on V*-Bench, and option-posterior turn credit reaches 52.5% and 48.0% exact match on V*-Bench and HR-Bench-4K.
0IJBxo578w.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the controlled decomposition of action text, message structure, and pixels compelling and the measurement problem in process-reward design important.
0IJBxo578w.main_concern: Reviewers note that several conclusions rest on differences near one percentage point without seed variation or confidence intervals, and that the structural-dominance result partly reflects the tagged-sequence belief target.

75PPLZgaUM.one_liner: Regularizes agent-harness self-improvement by limiting edits per proposal, screening benchmark-specific changes, and pruning low-value edits.
75PPLZgaUM.problem: Recursive harness evolution can overfit the training tasks, showing large in-distribution gains that shrink or vanish on out-of-distribution benchmarks.
75PPLZgaUM.method: RRSI constrains both proposal and selection: the proposer uses a temporally annealed edit budget and favors unexplored trajectories based on evolution history, while the selector has a critic that screens benchmark-specific proposals and a pruner that removes changes that are too small, too expensive or no longer useful.
75PPLZgaUM.key_idea: Apply regularization-style constraints (annealed edit budget, history-based exploration, critic screening, pruning) to harness evolution to favor reusable mechanisms over benchmark-specific ones.
75PPLZgaUM.evidence: Eight benchmarks spanning coding, agentic workspace and engineering design tasks.
75PPLZgaUM.claimed_gains: Gains of up to 6.0 points, with the rest of the sentence truncated in the abstract.
75PPLZgaUM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper addresses an important problem, transferable gains versus overfitting to repeatedly reused evolution tasks, and that the transfer evaluation spans several domains.
75PPLZgaUM.main_concern: Ablations remove regularizers only in groups, so it is unclear which of the roughly nine mechanisms drives transfer, and simpler baselines such as a fixed single-edit budget or a compute-matched control are missing.

XOELT3GRtB.one_liner: Benchmark of 203 long-document instances for building relational databases, built by synthesizing documents from databases.
XOELT3GRtB.problem: Existing Document-to-Table benchmarks flatten evidence into single tables, which duplicates entities, hides many-to-many relationships and does not test whether extracted facts form a valid database instance.
XOELT3GRtB.method: Doc2DB-Bench contains 203 long-document instances across 42 schemas and seven domain groups (117 entity tables, 132 relationship tables, 7,341 rows, 41,935 cells), built by a controllable DB-to-Doc synthesis pipeline and organized by a taxonomy of intra-table extraction and inter-table reasoning. Generated documents undergo authenticity verification.
XOELT3GRtB.key_idea: Generate documents from real relational databases so ground-truth schemas and rows are known, then evaluate extraction by a taxonomy of intra-table and inter-table capabilities.
XOELT3GRtB.evidence: Model evaluation with taxonomy-level failure analysis (per reviews); the abstract is truncated before results.
XOELT3GRtB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree document-to-database construction is practically relevant and underexplored, and the synthesis pipeline and capability taxonomy enable scalable, fine-grained failure analysis.
XOELT3GRtB.main_concern: Benchmark validity and positioning are questioned: only 50 synthesized documents were manually checked, scoring uses a manual match threshold, and related entity-collection benchmarks are not distinguished.

M4S7kvmD9R.one_liner: Scores view reliability from joint Euclidean and hyperbolic Gramian geometry, trained on simulated view mismatches.
M4S7kvmD9R.problem: Test-time noisy correspondence, where views of a sample are mismatched, undermines multi-view fusion, and existing methods assess reliability from view-wise statistics while overlooking the geometric structure of multi-view features.
M4S7kvmD9R.method: HGR trains a view-reliability estimator with Noisy Correspondence Augmented Learning, which simulates diverse mismatch patterns, and Hybrid Geometric Learning, which builds Euclidean and Hyperbolic Gramian matrices to capture high-order joint geometry across views. A Gramian volume contrastive loss and a view consistency loss reinforce coherence of matched samples and amplify structural distortion of mismatched ones.
M4S7kvmD9R.key_idea: Judge view reliability from the Gramian volume of all views jointly in Euclidean and hyperbolic space, contrasting matched samples against mismatched ones.
M4S7kvmD9R.evidence: Extensive experiments on multiple multi-view benchmark datasets against existing methods such as BML; details are cut off in the available abstract.
M4S7kvmD9R.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the motivation is clear and that judging view reliability from the joint geometry of all views, rather than pairwise statistics, is an insightful design backed by extensive experiments.
M4S7kvmD9R.main_concern: Several design choices lack justification or analysis, including the apparent redundancy of the view consistency loss and of combining Euclidean and hyperbolic Gram geometry, and the effect of the fixed training perturbation ratio.

LZfkjrtKUq.one_liner: Applies one fixed-resolution generative mesh model across scene scales via an inference-time coarse-to-fine cascade of perturb-and-denoise levels.
LZfkjrtKUq.problem: Per-scene optimization lacks a learned 3D prior under sparse views or glossy and transparent surfaces, and existing generative methods work at fixed resolution over limited extent, so large scenes need independently processed regions that lose global consistency.
LZfkjrtKUq.method: T3lescope runs a single fixed-resolution generator in a coarse-to-fine cascade: a coarse level establishes scene layout and finer levels perturb and denoise inherited geometry within progressively finer spatial cells. The model is trained on individual cells at multiple scales with weights shared across levels, so the number of levels, cell scales, and cell locations are chosen at inference.
LZfkjrtKUq.key_idea: Train one generator on cells at multiple scales and apply it recursively at inference, with each finer level perturbing and denoising geometry inherited from the coarser level.
LZfkjrtKUq.evidence: Indoor, outdoor, and city-scale scenes (including ScanNet++ and city blocks per reviews) against feed-forward and generative methods and per-scene optimization, with component ablations such as parent initialization.
LZfkjrtKUq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that reusing one generator across scales through an inference-time cascade is a scalable design with strong, extensively evaluated reconstruction results across scene scales without per-scene optimization.
LZfkjrtKUq.main_concern: Cascade settings are hand-set per dataset without sensitivity analysis, coarse-level errors can propagate to finer levels, and city-scale baselines use downsampled images, which confounds the comparison.

NIDeTGy867.one_liner: SPBench is a multi-task benchmark for learning-based exploration seismic processing, adding SCoRE and RC_norm diagnostics for reconstruction and first-arrival picking.
NIDeTGy867.problem: Learning-based seismic processing results are hard to compare because studies rely on private datasets and few release code (only 25 of 368 surveyed papers).
NIDeTGy867.method: SPBench standardizes six tasks (random noise attenuation, trace interpolation, ground-roll suppression, multiple suppression, deblending, first-arrival picking) and releases datasets, implementations, configurations, and evaluation scripts. It adds signal-component-resolved evaluation (SCoRE) for reconstruction and a reference-free ridge-curvature score (RC_norm) for first-arrival picking.
NIDeTGy867.key_idea: Evaluate reconstruction by signal component (frequency and energy resolved) and first-arrival picks by reference-free ridge curvature, instead of global scores and per-trace pick errors.
NIDeTGy867.evidence: Evaluates 24 supervised methods and 10 traditional baselines on 12 datasets across 47 experimental settings, after a literature survey of 368 papers.
NIDeTGy867.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the benchmark is a substantial reproducibility effort with a clear multi-task structure and released resources, and that the two diagnostics are a useful core.
NIDeTGy867.main_concern: Hyperparameters follow the original papers rather than a common tuning budget, so it is unclear whether low ranks reflect weak methods or imperfect reproductions, and the findings are seen as largely descriptive.

t7fTGl4voo.one_liner: Training-free sampler that composes pretrained flows by adding a closed-form Gaussian endpoint-posterior correction to summed-score annealing.
t7fTGl4voo.problem: Composing pretrained flow-matching models by adding velocities or annealing summed scores does not target the composed distribution, for example overshooting the product mean of two unit-variance Gaussians.
t7fTGl4voo.method: From an exact identity for composed intermediate marginals, the gradient of the log-overlap of endpoint posteriors is the exact correction to summed-score annealing. Gaussian moment matching gives it a closed form computable from black-box flows using only velocities and velocity Jacobians, with a well-posedness certificate.
t7fTGl4voo.key_idea: Correct summed-score annealing with the gradient of the log endpoint-posterior overlap, approximated by Gaussian moment matching from velocities and Jacobians.
t7fTGl4voo.evidence: Theoretical derivation plus synthetic distribution and simple image experiments per the reviews; the abstract's results are cut off.
t7fTGl4voo.claimed_gains: Adding velocities overshoots the product mean of two unit-variance Gaussians by a factor of 1+pi/2; no performance numbers for CompFM are stated.
t7fTGl4voo.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper rigorously explains why direct velocity or score composition fails, derives a well-motivated correction, and offers a practical training-free closed-form approximation.
t7fTGl4voo.main_concern: Experiments are mostly synthetic or simple image settings with unclear practical need, the product target may not improve generation quality, and the correction adds a reported wall-clock overhead of about 4.7-4.8 over summed-score annealing.

3iP01ustNZ.one_liner: Tiny drafter predicts a diffusion LM's token commit order and proposes a tree verified losslessly via shared-Gumbel-noise coupling.
3iP01ustNZ.problem: Speculative decoding does not transfer directly to diffusion language models because they must choose both what to generate and where, while exact decoding fills only one position per pass.
3iP01ustNZ.method: A 0.62M-parameter model reads only the target's output distributions and proposes a tree of candidate continuations including predicted commit order, and the target verifies all of them in one pass using coupled-noise match verification that works at any temperature.
3iP01ustNZ.key_idea: Predict which position the diffusion LM commits next from its own output distributions, and verify tree proposals by matching under shared Gumbel noise.
3iP01ustNZ.evidence: Comprehensive experiments (details cut off in the abstract); reviews cite MBPP at T=1 against Spiffy, SSD-style, and BlockSpec-style baselines and cross-model transfer.
3iP01ustNZ.claimed_gains: Cuts target passes by up to 6.8x and reaches up to 3.2x (comparison cut off in the abstract); the TLDR states throughput up to 3.5x.
3iP01ustNZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the commit-order diagnosis is useful, the lightweight predictor reduces forward passes and raises throughput, and the verifier is principled and lossless across temperatures.
3iP01ustNZ.main_concern: Comparisons do not fully establish superiority because baselines are reimplemented in the authors' harness with fixed settings and MRP is compared only through published speedups under different hardware and settings.

RK969Wk0EU.one_liner: MoE prefill engine that starts expert FFN work before all replicas finish dispatch and lets fast replicas fetch expert weights.
RK969Wk0EU.problem: In data-and-expert-parallel MoE serving, synchronous expert parallelism delays expert FFN computation until all attention replicas dispatch, and scheduling for load balance and prefix KV reuse leaves residual attention imbalance.
RK969Wk0EU.method: ASYNCEP combines asynchronous expert parallelism, streamFFN that batches ready tokens to balance early execution and FFN efficiency, and opportunistic expert weight fetching (OEWF) that lets a faster replica fetch weights and run unstarted work from other GPUs.
RK969Wk0EU.key_idea: Let expert FFN computation begin on ready tokens from early replicas and reassign unstarted work by fetching expert weights, hiding attention-imbalance stalls.
RK969Wk0EU.evidence: Evaluated on DeepSeek-V4-Flash, DeepSeek-V4-Pro, and GLM-5.3, across scheduling policies and agentic workloads on an eight-GPU B200 node per the reviews.
RK969Wk0EU.claimed_gains: Up to 1.48x speedup in p95 time-to-first-token and up to 1.17x higher inference throughput.
RK969Wk0EU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it addresses a real MoE serving bottleneck with a coherent fine-grained systems design, evaluated on several recent models, workloads, and scheduling policies.
RK969Wk0EU.main_concern: Gains are modest and smallest under the cache-aware scheduling policies likely used in practice, MoE prefill may not be the key bottleneck given high KV reuse, and novelty over prior MoE overlap techniques is limited.

Xh36ESRChj.one_liner: HamiFormer mixes whole-window diffusion denoising with residual-corrected Hamiltonian propagation, accelerated by parallel affine symplectic scans.
Xh36ESRChj.problem: Predicting smooth dynamics and collisions requires continuous evolution and abrupt state changes, and autoregressive error accumulates over long horizons.
Xh36ESRChj.method: A diffusion expert denoises whole windows while a Hamiltonian expert propagates one step with a learned residual; mixed-state feedback, the Parallel Local Affine Scan (PLAS), and a Regime Model Tree route and correct errors.
Xh36ESRChj.key_idea: Feed back a mixed state from a whole-window diffusion expert and a symplectic Hamiltonian expert, computing derivatives in parallel via affine symplectic maps across physical time.
Xh36ESRChj.evidence: 192-step evaluations on HamiBalls-1 and HamiBalls-2 with ablations, solver-error checks for PLAS, and analysis giving finite-window error bounds.
Xh36ESRChj.claimed_gains: Reduces normalized phase-space MSE by 26.3% against PhysiFormer on HamiBalls-1 and 21.4% against DiT on HamiBalls-2 in 192-step evaluations.
Xh36ESRChj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that combining global diffusion refinement with structured local propagation is well motivated and that experiments and ablations show improved long-horizon accuracy.
Xh36ESRChj.main_concern: Ablations do not isolate key components (the Hamiltonian expert versus a standard local model, regime partitioning) and cover only the first 48 of 192 steps, on two related simulated systems.

SBqeVNGQV9.one_liner: Applying iterated line graph transformations lets 3-WL distinguish every pair of non-isomorphic finite simple graphs at some finite depth.
SBqeVNGQV9.problem: GNN expressivity is usually raised by increasing the WL dimension k, leaving open whether a fixed dimension can suffice when the input graph is transformed.
SBqeVNGQV9.method: The authors prove that 3-WL on the r-th iterated line graph separates any non-isomorphic pair for some finite r, while no fixed depth works for all graphs. They introduce a universal line graph adapter for 3-WL-equivalent models such as PPGN++ and G^2N^2 and extend the implicit line graph neural network (ILG-3-GNN) to arbitrary depth.
SBqeVNGQV9.key_idea: Apply an injective, isomorphism-invariant line graph transformation repeatedly before running 3-WL, trading transformation depth for WL dimension.
SBqeVNGQV9.evidence: Proofs plus BREC experiments on 3-WL-equivalent GNNs (untrained per reviews), and time and memory comparison against 4-WL on original graphs.
SBqeVNGQV9.claimed_gains: On BREC, the best results match 3-WL on L^r(G) for r<=3, which separates 399 of the 400 pairs.
SBqeVNGQV9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the universality theorem is elegant and non-trivial and opens a new expressivity axis beyond raising k in k-WL.
SBqeVNGQV9.main_concern: Required depth is impractical (no fixed depth suffices and iterated line graphs grow very large) and experiments use untrained models, so practical ML benefit and novelty over prior ILG preprints remain unclear.

rSiOpiyWXX.one_liner: Unifies token-level SFT objectives as gate x error gradients and proposes Cayley-transform and entropy-concentration (DEFT) gates.
rSiOpiyWXX.problem: Standard NLL applies uniform token weighting, which amplifies gradients on noisy low-probability targets and sharpens weakly when the model is already confident, leaving a plasticity-stability dilemma.
rSiOpiyWXX.method: Token-level SFT objectives are placed in a generalized deformed-log family that shares a gate x error gradient structure. A probability-level gate uses the Cayley transform to map model uncertainty to a focus trajectory, and DEFT gates on the concentration of the predictive distribution.
rSiOpiyWXX.key_idea: Scale each token's gradient by a gate reflecting how much the model trusts its prediction, using a Cayley-transformed probability gate or DEFT's predictive-distribution concentration gate.
rSiOpiyWXX.evidence: Per reviews, experiments across seven backbones, three model capability regimes and three task settings with five seeds in the main comparisons, plus ablations and diagnostics.
rSiOpiyWXX.claimed_gains: not stated (abstract text cuts off before the results).
rSiOpiyWXX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the gate x error framework gives a clear view of SFT objectives and that the methods are lightweight, adding no trainable parameters, with comprehensive experiments.
rSiOpiyWXX.main_concern: Experiments do not directly show the claimed balance between preserving priors and acquiring new knowledge, and DEFT's gate may attenuate corrections to confidently wrong predictions.

6KFATgx7MF.one_liner: Pure edge-differentially-private matching protocol where each vertex decodes a shortlist locally from a public coordination record plus its private neighbors.
6KFATgx7MF.problem: Participants who know their own relationships need to retain useful matching structure while those relationships stay private from outside observers.
6KFATgx7MF.method: Protocols publish a pure edge-differentially-private record of coordination messages, and each participant combines it with its private neighbor list to obtain a shortlist, with both endpoints agreeing on every selected relationship. The main protocol uses O(n) communication rounds and stores the public record in O(n log n) bits.
6KFATgx7MF.key_idea: Each vertex decodes a shortlist by intersecting the public record with its own neighbor list, so every omitted edge touches a vertex whose shortlist is nearly full.
6KFATgx7MF.evidence: Theory only: a capacity guarantee holding with probability at least 1-rho, lower bounds for local decoding and probabilistic capacity, and a characterization of consistent local decoders; reviews note there is no empirical evaluation.
6KFATgx7MF.claimed_gains: A per-vertex capacity of at least c_0 log(n/rho)/(eta eps) suffices, with probability at least 1-rho, for the selected graph to retain a 1/(2+eta) fraction of the best edge count and of the original maximum matching.
6KFATgx7MF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit the theory: parallel and streaming extensions, lower bounds on public sparse outputs and zero-failure degree guarantees, and a representation theorem for intersection decoding.
6KFATgx7MF.main_concern: There is no empirical evaluation, and reviewers also ask for a clearer concrete use of the shortlist and a fuller comparison with related work such as k-disjoint matchings.

aRCnhTjvwp.one_liner: Antibody and nanobody co-design with flow matching, post-trained by transporting terminal reward gradients along sampled trajectories.
aRCnhTjvwp.problem: Generative models trained to reconstruct observed antibody–antigen complexes do not necessarily optimize the quality of the interfaces they generate.
aRCnhTjvwp.method: RAFA jointly generates CDR sequences and the full antibody structure from an antigen structure, epitope, and framework sequence, using Cα coordinates plus per-residue latents (building on La-Proteina's partially latent autoencoder) with joint flow matching and geometry supervision. Reward-Gradient Transport (RGT) approximately transports terminal reward gradients on antibody Cα coordinates to recorded states along the same trajectory and updates the shared velocity field.
aRCnhTjvwp.key_idea: Reward-Gradient Transport carries terminal reward gradients on Cα coordinates back to recorded states of the same sampled trajectory to update the shared flow velocity field.
aRCnhTjvwp.evidence: A globally filtered, held-out benchmark for antibody and nanobody design with structure-prediction, refolding-confidence, and interface analyses; reviewers also mention Protenix-v2 refolding and comparisons with DRTune and full BPTT.
aRCnhTjvwp.claimed_gains: RAFA (RL) improves mean DockQ by 22.0% for antibody design and 28.9% for nanobody design relative to RAFA on a globally filtered, held-out benchmark.
aRCnhTjvwp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the post-training algorithm technically sound and computationally efficient, with experiments covering both antibody formats and multi-modal structural and biophysical rewards.
aRCnhTjvwp.main_concern: Reviewers say evidence for RGT's incremental benefit is thin: no direct comparison with Adjoint Matching, DRTune shown only graphically without paired-difference uncertainty, and gains may be expected because base RAFA already optimizes an auxiliary reward.

CC2q4aPPqF.one_liner: TD-Aug samples imagined goals from a geometric horizon model to augment goal-conditioned behavior cloning for stitching.
CC2q4aPPqF.problem: Offline-trained goal-conditioned policies generalize poorly to unseen goals that require composing existing knowledge, and world-model-generated experience degrades over long horizons.
CC2q4aPPqF.method: TD-Aug samples future outcomes from a geometric horizon model (GHM) and uses them as relabeled goals when training goal-conditioned BC policies. Per reviews, the GHM is trained with an objective (MCHC) that combines Monte Carlo supervision with TD bootstrapping, and no world model is needed at test time.
CC2q4aPPqF.key_idea: Relabel training trajectories with goals sampled from a geometric horizon model of the successor measure, so BC sees outcomes stitched across trajectories.
CC2q4aPPqF.evidence: Stitching-based OGBench tasks (state-based and visual navigation and manipulation per reviews), compared with GCFBC, GCIQL, CRL, HIQL and MC/TD2 augmentation controls, with 3 seeds.
CC2q4aPPqF.claimed_gains: No numbers in the abstract (it claims substantially improved generalization on stitching-based OGBench tasks); a reviewer cites 54 +/- 17 success on pointmaze-giant-stitch against 0 for most baselines.
CC2q4aPPqF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the problem well posed and relabeling imagined goals from a GHM neat, with consistent gains over BC and a control (MC-Aug) suggesting the gains come from the stitched futures.
CC2q4aPPqF.main_concern: MCHC is derived from TD-HC but never compared against it, and all experiments are in OGBench mazes with re-collected datasets that limit comparability with published baselines.

daA3rlGEni.one_liner: Live RL environment that stores prediction-time rollouts, backfills rewards after real-world outcomes, and replays trajectories for policy updates.
daA3rlGEni.problem: Standard RL training frameworks rely on immediate rewards, so agents cannot learn from real-world future events whose outcomes arrive later.
daA3rlGEni.method: The authors extend verl-tool into verl-tool-future, which stores prediction-time rollouts, backfills rewards once real-world outcomes become available, and replays completed trajectories for policy updates. This closes the loop between prediction, outcome realization and parameter updates.
daA3rlGEni.key_idea: Decouple rollout from reward: store prediction-time trajectories, attach rewards when outcomes resolve, then replay them for policy-gradient updates.
daA3rlGEni.evidence: Three open-source agents trained over successive FutureWorld rounds, measured by prediction accuracy, probabilistic scoring and calibration; reviews also cite a Qwen3-32B run.
daA3rlGEni.claimed_gains: not stated (qualitative only: consistent improvements in prediction accuracy, probabilistic scoring and calibration across three agents over successive training rounds).
daA3rlGEni.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it is a relevant, practical infrastructure contribution that closes the loop with delayed real-world outcome rewards and improves forecasting across several models.
daA3rlGEni.main_concern: Novelty is limited because outcome-based RL for forecasting already exists, and the benefit of live training is not tested against offline training at equal compute, with cost and discarded-question rates also under-reported.

QiagfbqgiD.one_liner: Trains a VLM to reason and move a camera in a rendered 3D scene via trajectory SFT then answer-correctness RL.
QiagfbqgiD.problem: Existing approaches hand VLMs multi-view images, videos or complete 3D representations instead of having the model decide what to observe in 3D space.
QiagfbqgiD.method: The VLM keeps its native single-image encoding and treats the 3D representation as an environment it acts in (for example moving left) and observes through rendered images. Each rollout starts from a fixed first-person view and a question; after trajectory-supervised fine-tuning, RL optimizes the interactive policy with rewards driven mainly by final-answer correctness.
QiagfbqgiD.key_idea: Learn exploration solely from final-answer-correctness RL, with no supervision over which viewpoints to visit, inside an interactive rendered 3D environment.
QiagfbqgiD.evidence: Six 3D benchmarks, compared with other active models and the base Qwen model (abstract truncated); reviews cite SFT versus RL comparisons and out-of-domain results.
QiagfbqgiD.claimed_gains: Highest average score among active models at 54.1% across six 3D benchmarks, improving on its base Qwen model by 22.9%.
QiagfbqgiD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it addresses a meaningful problem, acquiring missing evidence before answering spatial questions, and that RL improves over the SFT initialization on all six benchmarks.
QiagfbqgiD.main_concern: Methodological novelty over prior active-view methods such as CoV and Think3D-RL is unclear, and experiments do not separate better exploration from extra observations or better answering.

6EfLHHhUuD.one_liner: Streaming fraud detector using shallow multi-view hypergraph aggregation, RL-built adaptive hypergraphs, and LLM-assisted prompts to limit embedding drift.
6EfLHHhUuD.problem: Stacking aggregation layers to capture high-order fraud amplifies the embedding drift bound under continuous concept drift, causing unstable updates in streaming fraud detection.
6EfLHHhUuD.method: MC-SFD captures high-order fraud with shallow hypergraph aggregation, an RL-based Adaptive Hypergraph Constructor (RL-AHC) that evolves hypergraph structure, and a Multi-view Personalized Prompt Generator (MPPG) that adapts with minimal parameter updates. LLMs initialize the RL policy and enhance semantics.
6EfLHHhUuD.key_idea: Capture high-order fraud with shallow hypergraph aggregation instead of deep message passing to keep the embedding drift bound small, and adapt through prompts with few parameter updates.
6EfLHHhUuD.evidence: Theoretical analysis of the embedding drift bound, TGAT depth comparison, and experiments on four streaming fraud detection datasets against 23 baselines.
6EfLHHhUuD.claimed_gains: Outperforms 23 baselines by 1.63% to 3.71% in AUC across four streaming fraud detection datasets.
6EfLHHhUuD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the trade-off between high-order relationship modeling and representation stability is well identified, with theory supporting the design and ablations showing where gains come from.
6EfLHHhUuD.main_concern: The method resembles MH-LGC (multi-view hypergraph fraud detection with LLM components), whose differences and performance are neither clarified nor compared, and the drift theory covers conventional message passing rather than the full hypergraph architecture.

OMdE8nYcF6.one_liner: Assesses super-resolution hallucination with bidirectional VLM question answering between output and ground truth, plus a learned lightweight predictor.
OMdE8nYcF6.problem: Existing super-resolution metrics do not measure whether generated details stay grounded in the reference image, so hallucinated or altered content goes undetected.
OMdE8nYcF6.method: VHA builds question-answer pairs from each image, has a VLM answer them on both images, and uses discrepancies between the two directions to reveal missing or altered ground-truth information and unsupported additions; VHA+ is a learned lightweight model that predicts VHA scores directly from image pairs.
OMdE8nYcF6.key_idea: Compare VLM answers to questions built from each image on both images, so forward and reverse score gaps expose missing, altered, and unsupported content.
OMdE8nYcF6.evidence: A human-study benchmark, VHA-bench, on which VHA and VHA+ correlate highly with human judgments; per reviews, Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct is the VLM and VHA+ is also used as a loss to fine-tune a super-resolution model.
OMdE8nYcF6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the bidirectional VQA design addresses both missing and unsupported content and that VHA+ makes the assessment much cheaper.
OMdE8nYcF6.main_concern: Reduced hallucination after fine-tuning is shown with the same VHA and VHA+ scorers that supplied the training loss, with no independent human evaluation.

7VGMLbOJSr.one_liner: Chooses the surrogate Jacobian closest to a prior backward rule under a positive-definite metric, enforcing selected active constraints exactly.
7VGMLbOJSr.problem: Constrained or discrete optimisation layers have solution maps with zero or undefined derivatives, which blocks useful gradient propagation, and existing backward rules lack a unifying framework.
7VGMLbOJSr.method: VSJ picks the surrogate Jacobian nearest a prior backward rule under a positive-definite metric, with a unique closed form when selected active constraints are enforced exactly, adds adaptive weighting of inequality constraints from primal slacks and dual multipliers, and recovers established backward rules as particular configurations.
7VGMLbOJSr.key_idea: Frame a backward rule as the projection onto the nearest surrogate Jacobian that satisfies the active constraints, with constraint strength set adaptively by primal slacks and dual multipliers.
7VGMLbOJSr.evidence: Six established backward rules are reproduced numerically, and validation-selected VSJ configurations are tested across prior families on tasks including Knapsack, Portfolio, and TSP (per reviews).
7VGMLbOJSr.claimed_gains: VSJ closely reproduces six established rules, and composing VSJ with PEAR lowers mean Knapsack regret and raises mean Portfolio cumulative return; a reviewer cites a 13.8% reduction in mean binary knapsack regret (0.4358 to 0.3756).
7VGMLbOJSr.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the framework gives a rigorous geometric unification of existing backward rules, with reproduced baselines and a design space for new configurations that improve on the strong PEAR baseline.
7VGMLbOJSr.main_concern: Improvements are not clearly attributable to the VSJ correction, since several selected configurations use Omega = 0, and they rest on few seeds with overlapping error bars.

9BAPF6L77V.one_liner: Repurposes frozen tabular foundation models for anomaly detection via virtual supervised tasks scored by in-context predictive support.
9BAPF6L77V.problem: TFM-based anomaly detection either needs anomaly-specific pretraining from scratch, tying it to synthetic priors and costly updates, or repurposes general TFMs through expensive formulations with restrictive anomaly inductive biases.
9BAPF6L77V.method: TaskBridge constructs virtual supervised tasks that recast anomaly detection as supervised in-context inference with a pretrained general-purpose TFM; normal queries and their virtual target pairs receive high support while anomalies violate the induced structure and receive lower support, which serves as anomaly evidence.
9BAPF6L77V.key_idea: Recast anomaly detection as supervised in-context prediction on context-derived virtual tasks, and score each row by how well the induced predictive structure supports it.
9BAPF6L77V.evidence: 790 datasets and 30 baselines (31 methods with 5 seeds, per reviews), with ablations over five virtual task families and tests across TFM backbones (TabICLv2, TabPFN v2.6, v3).
9BAPF6L77V.claimed_gains: not stated in the visible abstract; a reviewer reports it beats DTE-NP on 460 datasets and loses on 303.
9BAPF6L77V.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that reusing general-purpose tabular foundation models without anomaly-specific pretraining is effective, with a large and checkable evaluation over 790 datasets and many baselines.
9BAPF6L77V.main_concern: Part of the anomaly evidence bypasses the TFM through rule-based out-of-range flags, coverage of real anomaly types by the virtual tasks is not justified, and top ranking does not persist across TFM backbones.

hlVfE7AHyu.one_liner: Selects anomaly detectors via meta-learning on dataset representations built from sample similarity graphs compared by graph-based distances.
hlVfE7AHyu.problem: Hyperparameter optimization for anomaly detection is expensive and relies on surrogate internal criteria, while existing meta-learning uses coarse statistical meta-features that miss structural and relational patterns.
hlVfE7AHyu.method: The method builds sample-wise similarity graphs that map heterogeneous datasets into a unified relational space, computes graph-based distances or similarities between datasets (multi-scale WL and MFD comparisons per reviews), and uses them as meta-features to predict detector performance for selection.
hlVfE7AHyu.key_idea: Represent each dataset by graph-based distances between its sample-similarity graph and those of other datasets, replacing statistical meta-features for detector-performance prediction.
hlVfE7AHyu.evidence: Comparisons with meta-learning selectors (MetaOD, ISAC, MetaOOD, ELECT) with paired tests, per reviews; the visible abstract is truncated.
hlVfE7AHyu.claimed_gains: not stated in the visible abstract; a reviewer reports AUPRC of 64.44% versus 57.79% for ISAC, 56.31% for MetaOOD, and 54.80% for ELECT.
hlVfE7AHyu.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that unsupervised anomaly-detection model selection is practically relevant and that graph-induced task representations are a concrete, well-validated improvement over statistical meta-features.
hlVfE7AHyu.main_concern: The closest prior selector (LOTUS) is not compared, the speed advantage over MetaOD vanishes near 1,400 samples, and the candidate pool omits foundation-model detectors.

dB5cPt86r3.one_liner: Estimates pretrained-model output sensitivity from generic unlabeled inputs and merges task vectors in sensitivity-transformed coordinates.
dB5cPt86r3.problem: Task vector values alone do not capture how the shared pretrained model's output responds to parameter updates, since identical perturbations can produce different responses at different parameter locations.
dB5cPt86r3.method: PAL estimates pretrained sensitivity from a small set of generic unlabeled inputs, builds an invertible parameter transform, applies the original merging rule in the transformed coordinates, and maps the merged update back to the original parameter space; the transform is computed once per checkpoint with no downstream data.
dB5cPt86r3.key_idea: Lift an existing merger into coordinates scaled by the pretrained model's output sensitivity, merge there, and map the result back with the inverse transform.
dB5cPt86r3.evidence: CLIP vision tasks, RoBERTa on GLUE, and Llama-3.2-3B capability merging with several base mergers (45 vision comparisons, six GLUE mergers, and four Llama mergers per reviews).
dB5cPt86r3.claimed_gains: PAL improves recent mergers across CLIP vision tasks, RoBERTa on GLUE, and Llama-3.2-3B capability merging, with higher aggregate scores for every evaluated base merger; no numeric gains are stated.
dB5cPt86r3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that using pretrained-model information to guide merging is well motivated and reusable without task data or inference overhead, with consistent aggregate gains across model families.
dB5cPt86r3.main_concern: Close precedents (AIM, CSP, GFWSVD) are not discussed or compared, and no controls isolate the sensitivity signal as the source of the gains.

DLnwLwg2e9.one_liner: Defines generation-aware layout analysis, recovering allocated text regions and alignment, and trains a parser with element-level advantage GRPO.
DLnwLwg2e9.problem: Bounding boxes that capture only a text element's visible extent do not specify the space available for replacement text or how it should be aligned when the element is edited.
DLnwLwg2e9.method: GLA recovers text, allocated regions, semantic categories, and alignment; the parser is trained with joint SFT, RL with layout-specific rewards, and accelerated decoding with a block-diffusion drafter, and EAA-GRPO augments GRPO with Element-level Advantage Assignment that compares predictions for the same element across rollouts.
DLnwLwg2e9.key_idea: Assign advantages per element by comparing predictions for the same element across GRPO rollouts, rather than using one image-level advantage.
DLnwLwg2e9.evidence: A 37K-image training set across nine domains and GLA-Bench (1,000 images, four tasks), with comparisons against zero-shot VLMs and against GRPO under the same reward on two backbones.
DLnwLwg2e9.claimed_gains: not stated in the visible abstract; a reviewer cites a headline of 46.59 vs. 6.26 against zero-shot VLMs.
DLnwLwg2e9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the distinction between visible bounds and allocated regions is useful, the benchmark and dataset are substantial, and EAA-GRPO is a simple, well-motivated way to assign local feedback.
DLnwLwg2e9.main_concern: Experiments measure parsing quality rather than editing outcomes, and no inter-annotator agreement has been reported for the ambiguous allocated-region labels.

ARjCWHgWyr.one_liner: Structures video reasoning as a chronological chain of entity primitives with timestamped boxes that prompt mask prediction.
ARjCWHgWyr.problem: Text-only chain-of-thought can explain a target choice without making visual references explicit, leaving a video reference gap between linguistic inference and the evidence spread across frames in video reasoning segmentation.
ARjCWHgWyr.method: TCoVP organizes query-relevant observations into a chain of primitives, each tying an entity reference to temporal support and timestamped spatial evidence and interleaved with language; the selected target primitives give box prompts and temporal support for video mask prediction, trained with TCoVP-SFT-15k and TCoVP-RL-13k through SFT and chain-aligned RL.
ARjCWHgWyr.key_idea: Make each reasoning step a primitive pairing an entity with its temporal support and timestamped boxes, so rewards apply to intermediate grounding and the final primitives prompt segmentation.
ARjCWHgWyr.evidence: Five video reasoning segmentation benchmarks and three model backbones, with reward ablations, intermediate grounding evaluations, SAM2/SAM3 comparisons, and an oracle experiment on GroundMoRe.
ARjCWHgWyr.claimed_gains: not stated numerically; the abstract claims strong performance across five VRS benchmarks and three model backbones.
ARjCWHgWyr.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the video reference gap is a clear, well-motivated problem and that the primitive chain gives verifiable intermediate steps, with competitive results and informative diagnostic experiments.
ARjCWHgWyr.main_concern: The roles of chronological ordering and entity identifiers are not ablated separately, and gains may reflect the extra TCoVP training data that baselines do not receive.

QJZXGaTyXT.one_liner: Training-free early token reduction for reference-based image generation, scoring reference token importance by probing the DiT on 2× downsampled references.
QJZXGaTyXT.problem: Concatenating multiple reference images into one DiT sequence causes token explosion with O(N^2) cost, and in-model acceleration cannot cut spatial redundancy or peak VRAM while pre-model alternatives need external models.
QJZXGaTyXT.method: A few denoising steps on spatially 2× downsampled references let the DiT itself estimate reference token importance; before the main denoising, low-importance tokens are discarded and mid-importance tokens are replaced by downsampled counterparts, with a third tier kept (three tiers per reviews, abstract truncated).
QJZXGaTyXT.key_idea: Use the generator itself as a cheap low-resolution probe to rank reference tokens, then keep, downsample, or discard them before the main denoising pass.
QJZXGaTyXT.evidence: Three base models and two benchmarks, with ablations of the reduction strategy and composability with in-model methods; quality scored by Qwen3-VL per reviews.
QJZXGaTyXT.claimed_gains: not stated in the visible abstract; a reviewer notes the fast setting moves average scores from 4.70 to 4.72 and from 6.18 to 6.20 (Table 1).
QJZXGaTyXT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is well motivated and the training-free design is clean, using the model itself as a probe, which enables peak-VRAM reduction and composability with in-model methods.
QJZXGaTyXT.main_concern: The quality gains are tiny and come from a single seed without confidence intervals, and the claim that early reduction beats in-model reduction is not tested against ToPi.

ah64v1jnvQ.one_liner: Evaluates AI-image forensic explanations by splitting them into atomic claims, grounding each, and judging forensic evidentiality with an SFT+GRPO-trained evaluator.
ah64v1jnvQ.problem: Explanations from MLLM-based AI-generated image detectors are often generic, hallucinated, or forensically insufficient, and existing metrics give only holistic scores that cannot check individual claims against the image.
ah64v1jnvQ.method: ClaimEval decomposes an explanation into atomic claims and evaluates each through language evaluation, claim grounding, evidence grouping, and forensic evidentiality assessment. A Qwen3-VL-8B evaluator is trained with supervised fine-tuning then Structure-Guided GRPO (SG-GRPO), and claim-level judgments are aggregated into an explanation score.
ah64v1jnvQ.key_idea: Splits explanations into atomic claims, checks visual grounding separately from forensic evidentiality, and trains a structured claim-level judge with SFT followed by structure-guided GRPO.
ah64v1jnvQ.evidence: Experiments on a newly built dataset with claim-level annotations and expert quality ratings; reviews mention zero-shot baselines (including Claude), agreement with independent expert ratings, and tests on unseen image and explanation sources.
ah64v1jnvQ.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract says only that ClaimEval achieves 'substantially better' results and the text is cut off before any numbers.
ah64v1jnvQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit the separation of visual grounding from forensic evidentiality, the claim-level design with a reward that resists hacking and an abstaining tool verifier, and a reasonably sized annotated dataset.
ah64v1jnvQ.main_concern: Missing module-level ablations (SFT-only, no-tool, per-module human alignment) and unclear tool-verification details, with one reviewer also noting overlap with XPlainVerse and DeepfakeJudge.

VJFxZoloNm.one_liner: Autoregressive video DMD distillation with ordered per-chunk noise levels for score queries and a role-conditioned shared fake-score backbone.
VJFxZoloNm.problem: In autoregressive video distillation, a single re-noising level in Distribution Matching Distillation couples preserving the context chunks with correcting the generated content.
VJFxZoloNm.method: ViDA assigns ordered noise levels across chunks in DMD score queries, so earlier chunks get lower, nonzero corruption and retain context while still being corrected. It also replaces the separate fake-score network with a role-conditioned shared backbone.
VJFxZoloNm.key_idea: Query DMD scores with chunk-ordered noise levels (lower for earlier chunks) instead of one scalar level, and replace the separate fake-score network with a role-conditioned shared backbone.
VJFxZoloNm.evidence: VBench ablations of ordered versus scalar, shuffled and reversed noise assignments with a 1.3B student distilled from a 14B teacher; reviews also cite Cosmos transfer, 60-second evaluations, and a human preference study.
VJFxZoloNm.claimed_gains: Ordered queries raise VBench Total by 0.75 over marginal-matched scalar queries and by 0.64 and 1.40 over shuffled and reversed assignments; the 1.3B generator reaches 85.62 VBench Total (1.12 above matched scalar querying, 1.38 above the locally evaluated official Self Forcing checkpoint), with half the student post-training GPU-hours and 13.6% lower peak allocated memory than the independent causal estimator at r=5.
VJFxZoloNm.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the ablations controlled and the VBench, memory-efficiency and human-preference results supportive, noting that the reversed-order result rules out heterogeneous noise alone as the explanation.
VJFxZoloNm.main_concern: Comparisons are thin or confounded: the sharing gain may come from extra fake-objective updates, the shared r=5 setting is untested, and several headline results rest on single runs.

zbJq1vy4sM.one_liner: Training-free sampler that adjusts class-conditioning injection per U-Net block using conditional pressure and SNR to diversify tail-class generations.
zbJq1vy4sM.problem: Class-conditional diffusion models trained on long-tailed data lose quality and intra-class diversity on tail classes, collapsing toward a few dominant modes.
zbJq1vy4sM.method: SABR keeps all weights frozen and modulates the strength of local class-conditioning injection according to the model's internal conditional response and the signal-to-noise ratio. It builds on analyses showing that lower training frequency gives stronger local conditional pressure and that modulating conditioning in the low-resolution encoding region improves tail coverage.
zbJq1vy4sM.key_idea: Gate class-conditioning injection block by block at sampling time, based on measured conditional pressure and SNR, to relax conditioning that concentrates tail-class samples on few modes.
zbJq1vy4sM.evidence: Experiments on multiple long-tailed datasets and baselines, plus mechanism analysis (Original/Reverse/Permuted frequency experiments, local interventions) mainly on CIFAR-100-LT; reviews mention a comparison with CADS.
zbJq1vy4sM.claimed_gains: not stated in the visible abstract (text cut off); a review cites CIFAR-100-LT DDPM Few-class FID dropping from 31.525 to 27.017.
zbJq1vy4sM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the frequency-dependent conditional-pressure analysis and the tail-class gains obtained without retraining across several datasets and baselines.
zbJq1vy4sM.main_concern: Limited novelty over existing training-free conditioning and guidance modulation (CADS, FreeU, interval guidance), with insufficient component ablations and narrow generalization evidence.

yqJ8FJBmDq.one_liner: Interactive benchmark of social engineering attacks on tool-using AI agents, plus MetaSEA co-evolution of attack tasks and defenders.
yqJ8FJBmDq.problem: The security of personal AI agents that act with real money and sensitive data has not been systematically evaluated under social engineering attacks.
yqJ8FJBmDq.method: SEA is an interactive environment of 320 tasks covering 8 daily-life domains, 30+ simulated applications, a 4-level difficulty gradient and a 5-dimensional evaluation framework, in Chinese and English. MetaSEA is a co-evolutionary framework for attack tasks and defenders used to train a defender model.
yqJ8FJBmDq.key_idea: Co-evolve attack tasks and defenders in an interactive environment of simulated apps, with executed tool calls and losses scored across five dimensions.
yqJ8FJBmDq.evidence: Evaluation of 11 frontier open-source and closed-source models (GPT-6 in Chinese only) on the 320 tasks, plus MetaSEA training of Qwen3-8B.
