yqJ8FJBmDq.claimed_gains: Chinese attack success rates range from 16.9% to 84.3% across models, maximum single-conversation losses exceed ¥40,000, proactive verification rates are below 32%, and MetaSEA-trained Qwen3-8B reaches defense performance comparable to closed-source models.
yqJ8FJBmDq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is timely and significant and that scoring executed tool calls and simulated losses makes the benchmark useful, with one noting MetaSEA substantially lowers Qwen3-8B's attack success rate.
yqJ8FJBmDq.main_concern: Benchmark realism and novelty are questioned: the threat model is idealized, the 8x5x4x2 combinatorial design makes tasks homogeneous, and overlap with prior work such as ConVerse is not resolved.

lLjcKCHNI3.one_liner: Interactive world model with an external camera-indexed geometry bank and a long-horizon sparse-attention teacher distilled into a bounded-context student.
lLjcKCHNI3.problem: Interactive world models must combine persistent memory, responsive interaction and long-horizon generation, but keeping history in the denoiser context or KV cache grows cost over time and few-step students are bounded by their teacher.
lLjcKCHNI3.method: Evoke stores scene geometry in an external camera-indexed world state bank and retrieves only view-relevant information, keeping the denoiser context bounded. Its teacher uses sparse attention combining chunk-wise grouping, retrieval of selected distant frames and a linear-attention global state, with per-chunk conditioning for prompt changes and event control.
lLjcKCHNI3.key_idea: Move persistent scene memory into an external camera-indexed state bank queried per view, and train the teacher with sparse plus linear attention so long-horizon supervision reaches the student.
lLjcKCHNI3.evidence: Matched-teacher comparisons, WBench results, a two-hour qualitative rollout, and a statistical analysis of eight 65.5-minute sequences, as described in the reviews.
lLjcKCHNI3.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract text is cut off before any numbers, and reviews mention strong WBench results and two-hour rollouts without figures.
lLjcKCHNI3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating persistent spatial memory from the denoiser with fixed storage and retrieval budgets is well motivated, and that matched teacher comparisons show long supervision improves photometric stability.
lLjcKCHNI3.main_concern: The benefit of long-horizon supervision is limited to photometric stability, with no significant gain in content descriptors or event realization, and teacher quality, training volume and window length are not disentangled.

Pul541M80q.one_liner: Pretrained LLM writes executable programs for articulated USD assets, grounded by textual source-mesh geometry analysis and iterative geometric rechecking.
Pul541M80q.problem: Mesh-based articulation methods struggle on real objects outside their training distribution or with incomplete or corrupted meshes, which limits real-to-sim robot manipulation.
Pul541M80q.method: USDCraft has a pretrained LLM write and revise programs without task-specific training. Source geometry analysis turns the mesh into a metric textual description separating observed surface from unknown space, iterative geometric rechecking re-encodes each candidate in the same representation so discrepancies point to edits, and visual feedback plus physical authoring guidance yield USD assets that load into Isaac Sim.
Pul541M80q.key_idea: Describe the source mesh to the LLM in a metric text representation that separates observed from unknown space, and re-encode each candidate program the same way to localize edits.
Pul541M80q.evidence: Articulation recovery experiments, ablations (Tables 6 and 7), a Mini Workflow comparison with the same backbone and inputs, and real-to-sim-to-real transfer experiments, as described in the abstract and reviews.
Pul541M80q.claimed_gains: not stated with numbers; the abstract claims best articulation recovery (text cut off), and a review cites part F1 improving from 74.48% with the Astra backbone (improved value cut off).
Pul541M80q.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the source geometry analysis well motivated for imperfect meshes and credit the thorough ablations and the sim-to-real transfer results.
Pul541M80q.main_concern: The method section lacks detail on the geometry analysis (feature detection, thresholds, noisy surfaces), limiting reproducibility, and comparisons with PartCrafter, OmniPart, SPARK and SINGAPO are requested.

873klOIcQn.one_liner: Source-anchored flow-matching video model for overlay removal, plus DVTE-Bench with 1,631 paired videos across eight text-overlay categories.
873klOIcQn.problem: Existing video overlay removal methods based on temporal propagation or source-conditioned generation can leave residual overlays and distort scene structure when useful source information is obscured.
873klOIcQn.method: DeOverlay reconstructs the clean video from the source latent with fixed source guidance, training a shared velocity network along paired source-to-clean paths with region-weighted flow matching. Visibility-normalized temporal aggregation selects local source cues, and global source context and edit-region embeddings are added through additive conditioning while keeping a single video-token sequence.
873klOIcQn.key_idea: Start the flow from the source latent and refine it in successive steps, using visibility-normalized temporal averaging of unmasked observations as fixed local guidance.
873klOIcQn.evidence: Experiments on DVTE-Bench (1,631 paired videos, eight text-overlay categories, OCR-screened clean targets, frame-aligned pixel masks) against four baselines on five reconstruction and perceptual metrics.
873klOIcQn.claimed_gains: DeOverlay outperforms four baselines on all five reconstruction and perceptual metrics, reducing Mask LPIPS by 58.3% and Mask VFID by 70.3% relative to a reference that the abstract cuts off before naming.
873klOIcQn.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree DVTE-Bench is valuable for evaluation and that the method performs strongly, with one also noting competitive inference speed and low GPU memory.
873klOIcQn.main_concern: Scope is narrow: evaluation centers on synthetic text overlays in eight similar categories, with no comparison to methods such as VACE and EffectErase and no general object-removal benchmark.

6uYPqLZOI4.one_liner: Benchmark and gray-box Reversal Gap method for membership inference on text-to-video diffusion transformers, with a non-member set complementing VideoUFO.
6uYPqLZOI4.problem: The only existing membership inference method for video generators targets old architectures and was calibrated and tested on members and non-members drawn from two fundamentally different distributions.
6uYPqLZOI4.method: The authors build and open-source a non-member dataset complementing VideoUFO, which trained a large text-to-video diffusion transformer, then adapt membership inference methods from image generation and classification across access levels. They add a gray-box method, The Reversal Gap (TRG), and find an ensemble of methods performs best.
6uYPqLZOI4.key_idea: TRG scores membership by the gap in model loss between a video's forward and time-reversed versions, giving an internal reference without training a reference model.
6uYPqLZOI4.evidence: Evaluation of adapted image and classification MI methods plus TRG on the new member/non-member split for a VideoUFO-trained T2V model; reviews cite blind baselines, cross-split transfer, and a disjoint-data reference model control.
6uYPqLZOI4.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract gives no numbers, and reviews cite TRG AUROC of 0.608 versus 0.514 for denoising loss in Table 1.
6uYPqLZOI4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit the careful evaluation methodology with matched non-members and the clear intuition of TRG, which needs no reference model.
6uYPqLZOI4.main_concern: Novelty over Vid-SME is unclear and TRG comparisons are confounded by unequal query budgets and averaging, with threat-model assumptions and inconsistent numbers across sections also raised.

6FCqTd8Fq7.one_liner: Vision-Transformer linear attention that subtracts a vanilla linear-attention redundancy branch from a group-weighted saliency branch, with dynamic kernel routing.
6FCqTd8Fq7.problem: Linear attention's smoothing lets redundant information obscure critical visual cues in the fused representation, degrading performance.
6FCqTd8Fq7.method: ADLA uses an asymmetric dual-branch design: a saliency branch with group-weighted key-value summarization and a redundancy branch with vanilla linear attention, combined differentially. A dynamic kernel routing mechanism further refines feature focusing.
6FCqTd8Fq7.key_idea: Treat linear attention's smooth weights as an explicit redundancy prior and subtract it from a group-weighted-summarization saliency branch to sharpen attention.
6FCqTd8Fq7.evidence: Experiments across diverse vision tasks and ablations; reviews cite controlled ablations (symmetric branches, non-differential baseline, static group weighting) and speedups on high-resolution PVT models.
6FCqTd8Fq7.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract says only that ADLA 'consistently achieves strong performance while preserving linear complexity', with no numbers.
6FCqTd8Fq7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the ablations give useful controlled evidence for the design and that the method works across several backbones and tasks.
6FCqTd8Fq7.main_concern: The redundancy-removal interpretation is not validated, the entropy diagnostic for differential weights that can be negative is undefined, and the contribution over MHLA and DyDiLA is called limited.

NT70RULWRV.one_liner: Recovers dense trajectories by rendering sparse points on maps and generating trajectory video with a one-step Drifting Model (DriftTraj).
NT70RULWRV.problem: Trajectory recovery methods that depend on city-specific road-segment vocabularies transfer poorly across cities.
NT70RULWRV.method: Sparse observed locations are rendered on a map and missing movement is recovered as video generation; DriftTraj adapts Drifting Models to produce each video block in one forward pass and chains blocks for longer trajectories. A differentiable red-marker extractor feeds spatial features into a geometric training objective that supervises marker location and structure.
NT70RULWRV.key_idea: Use rendered maps as a city-agnostic input, generate trajectory video blocks in one pass with a Drifting Model, and supervise marker positions through a differentiable marker extractor.
NT70RULWRV.evidence: Evaluated on Porto, Beijing, Xi'an and Chengdu, training only on Porto and transferring to the other three cities with zero-shot transfer and limited-data fine-tuning, using a newly built dataset pairing map-rendered sparse observations with dense-trajectory videos.
NT70RULWRV.claimed_gains: not stated in the abstract (text cut off); a review cites Beijing zero-shot MAE of 281.98 m versus 318.2 m for the best baseline.
NT70RULWRV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit reformulating trajectory recovery as map-based video generation, which gives a shared visual representation for cross-city transfer, and a reasonably comprehensive experimental comparison.
NT70RULWRV.main_concern: Reviewers question whether generating full video frames is necessary to recover 2D coordinates, citing missing comparisons with direct regression and classical route-inference baselines and mixed zero-shot results across cities.

6gwr7DedXj.one_liner: Training-free set-associative spatial memory retrofit for Point3R letting multiple states coexist at one 3D address, with bounded sparse readout.
6gwr7DedXj.problem: Point3R uses spatial proximity both to associate observations with memory entries and to decide whether to fuse them, so averaging nearby pointers can destroy complementary evidence from distinct surfaces or viewpoints.
6gwr7DedXj.method: Slot3R is a training-free retrofit that keeps the pretrained Point3R backbone frozen and lets multiple states coexist at a shared spatial address in a set-associative memory. A bounded sparse readout decouples persistent storage from per-frame decoder access.
6gwr7DedXj.key_idea: Let location determine the memory address but not force merging: store several states per address in a set-associative memory and read out a bounded sparse subset.
6gwr7DedXj.evidence: Evaluated at 300-500 and 600-1000 sampled frames on 7Scenes, NeuralRGBD, three pose benchmarks and video-depth estimation against Point3R and InfiniteVGGT; reviews cite K=1 to K=8 slot and component ablations.
6gwr7DedXj.claimed_gains: At 300–500 sampled frames Slot3R reduces Point3R's point-cloud accuracy error (Acc) by 57.1%–63.1% on 7Scenes and 64.0%–72.0% on NeuralRGBD, lowers Sim(3)-aligned ATE on all three pose benchmarks, and runs 600 to 1000 sampled frames at about 19 FPS where Point3R and InfiniteVGGT run out of memory.
6gwr7DedXj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the motivation (nearby observations should not be merged blindly) is clear and that the training-free retrofit gives large reconstruction and pose improvements.
6gwr7DedXj.main_concern: The motivation is not directly validated against Point3R's merging errors, and the merge threshold and sphere-hash design lack robustness analysis, including on larger scenes.

m9WXxBov4b.one_liner: Scaling study of egocentric-video world models separating agent from object fidelity, with an object-focused supervision scheme.
m9WXxBov4b.problem: It is unclear how far scaling egocentric human video takes world models, since opaque downstream metrics hide whether agents and object interactions are both modeled well.
m9WXxBov4b.method: The authors train world models on a 30,000-hour egocentric dataset (over 1,000 scene types, 14,000 contributors) and directly evaluate agent and object-interaction fidelity on an out-of-distribution benchmark. They test visual conditioning designs and introduce a supervision scheme that shifts capacity from scene appearance toward object dynamics.
m9WXxBov4b.key_idea: Measure agent and object fidelity separately under 100x data scaling and shift training supervision from scene appearance toward object dynamics.
m9WXxBov4b.evidence: Scaling experiments on 30,000 hours of egocentric video evaluated on an out-of-distribution benchmark, conditioning and supervision ablations, asymptote estimates from five checkpoints, and downstream humanoid modeling evaluations.
m9WXxBov4b.claimed_gains: Increasing training data by 100× improves agent and object fidelity unevenly (agent modeled well, object fidelity far lower and slower) and the proposed supervision improves object fidelity though a substantial gap remains; a review cites object SCS rising from 0.527 to 0.546 at 30K.
m9WXxBov4b.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it is a systematic, timely scaling study whose separation of agent and object fidelity exposes a gap that aggregate metrics hide, and that the object-focused supervision helps.
m9WXxBov4b.main_concern: Fidelity ceilings are extrapolated from a limited scaling range with data and compute varying together, and conclusions rest on one model family initialized from Cosmos weights.

Rtcp19g9wT.one_liner: Theory and experiments on active feature acquisition when training data has missing values, comparing aliasing, filtering and generative restoration.
Rtcp19g9wT.problem: Prior active feature acquisition work assumes complete training data, an assumption often violated in practice.
Rtcp19g9wT.method: The paper formalizes AFA with Incomplete Training Data and shows that under MCAR missingness one-step acquisition values are unchanged while multi-step values can decrease. It analyzes three ways to learn from incomplete data, aliasing, filtering and generative restoration, in terms of the training instances each requires.
Rtcp19g9wT.key_idea: Under MCAR missingness, one-step acquisition values are preserved but multi-step values degrade; filtering needs data exponential in dimension and generative restoration exponential in acquisition budget.
Rtcp19g9wT.evidence: Theoretical analysis, a controlled experiment, and common AFA datasets; reviews cite six methods, eight datasets, four missingness mechanisms, and released code.
Rtcp19g9wT.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract reports that missingness mainly damages methods using multi-step acquisitions and that generative restoration recovers lost performance in many experiments, without numbers.
Rtcp19g9wT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is practically relevant and clearly motivated, and that the theory is paired with a broad empirical study across methods, datasets and missingness mechanisms.
Rtcp19g9wT.main_concern: Real-world gains from generative restoration are mixed and the predictor is trained on complete data, while the MCAR-only theory is seen as close to classical missing-data results.

fOnqWNHZyk.one_liner: One-step OCT-to-OCTA synthesis that predicts a deterministic OCTA reference plus a generated residual using Pixel MeanFlow.
fOnqWNHZyk.problem: Deterministic OCT-to-OCTA translation underrepresents angiographic signals not specified by OCT, while full-target generation lets the whole volume vary, including structure that should stay tied to the input.
fOnqWNHZyk.method: Reference-centered generation decomposes each prediction into a subject-specific OCTA reference from translation and a generated residual, instantiated with Pixel MeanFlow for one-step synthesis. It requires neither vessel nor retinal-layer annotations.
fOnqWNHZyk.key_idea: Predict a deterministic subject-specific OCTA reference and use one-step Pixel MeanFlow generation only for the residual angiographic variation.
fOnqWNHZyk.evidence: Experiments on OCTA-3M and OCTA-6M plus mechanism analysis of the finite-interval transport; reviews cite volume and projection MAE tables and ablations with frozen and fine-tuned references.
fOnqWNHZyk.claimed_gains: The abstract claims top performance on OCTA-3M and OCTA-6M without numbers; a review cites OCTA-3M 3D MAE falling from 2.5674 to 2.4957 versus direct pMF in a single-seed comparison.
fOnqWNHZyk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers note the method needs no vessel or retinal-layer annotations, avoids iterative sampling, and reports the lowest volume and projection MAE among the compared methods.
fOnqWNHZyk.main_concern: The ablations do not show that the generative correction improves on the pretrained deterministic reference alone, and novelty over prior residual-plus-generation work such as ResDiff and PMRF is unclear.

dEvUqH7LoC.one_liner: Generative world model of 3D particle dynamics using an object-aware multi-resolution transformer with flow matching and diffusion forcing.
dEvUqH7LoC.problem: Learned particle-dynamics models are domain-specific and do not cover rigid, deformable, cloth and granular materials, in passive physics and robot interaction, under one architecture.
dEvUqH7LoC.method: GPWM is an object-aware multi-resolution transformer trained on ParticleWorlds, a 25.5-million-frame corpus, combining flow matching with diffusion forcing for streaming generation beyond the training horizon. For planning, an object-space goal reward is backpropagated through the learned interaction dynamics to the latent noise, steering actuator motion and contacts.
dEvUqH7LoC.key_idea: Pair flow matching with diffusion forcing in a multi-resolution particle transformer, and plan by backpropagating an object-space goal reward to the latent noise.
dEvUqH7LoC.evidence: Evaluation on ParticleWorlds across six physical domains with four retrained baselines, generalization tests to unseen geometries, properties, object counts and horizons, and open-loop simulation planning on pushing, picking and granular manipulation.
dEvUqH7LoC.claimed_gains: Within individual domains GPWM reduces prediction error by 29-53% relative to the strongest applicable prior learned-dynamics models, and its plans outperform unguided generation and planning with prior dynamics models in simulation.
dEvUqH7LoC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit the broad, carefully executed evidence across physical domains, the diverse dataset, and executing plans in the underlying simulator.
dEvUqH7LoC.main_concern: The contribution is seen as a combination of existing components, with few ablations of the multi-resolution design and limited planning experiments.

vfgEkycBBS.one_liner: VoxDirector generates multi-speaker speech and surrounding audio with voice design and cloning via reward-conditioned control and a Dual-Router MoE.
vfgEkycBBS.problem: Building audio scenes needs jointly generated multi-speaker speech, ambience, music and effects, but high-quality annotated data is scarce and supporting both voice design and cloning across several audio modalities is hard.
vfgEkycBBS.method: VoxCaps cleans media data, adds targeted synthetic data and uses a persona library to annotate multi-level scene descriptions; VoxVAE pairs a local anti-aliased encoder with a high-capacity decoder for a shared continuous representation; VoxDirector adds reward-conditioned quality control and a Dual-Router MoE for the two tasks and multiple audio modalities.
vfgEkycBBS.key_idea: Generate speech and non-speech audio in one shared continuous latent space, with reward-conditioned quality control and a Dual-Router MoE routing across the two tasks and audio modalities.
vfgEkycBBS.evidence: Experiments comparing VoxDirector with baselines on voice design and cloning metrics plus ablations; reviews cite an in-house benchmark scored by an LLM judge, InstructTTSEval and VoxBench-Instruct.
vfgEkycBBS.claimed_gains: not stated with numbers; the abstract says only that VoxDirector outperforms the baselines on key metrics for both voice design and cloning.
vfgEkycBBS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the unified voice design, cloning, dialogue and surrounding-audio framework is practically useful and a solid system-level effort with a large data pipeline.
vfgEkycBBS.main_concern: Novelty and component-level evidence are limited: the framework combines existing techniques, key ablations use one in-house benchmark with one LLM judge, and related work such as ScenA and UNISON is not compared.

l4qBHpMvXz.one_liner: Proves linear last-iterate convergence to Nash in sequence-form games with a proximal reference moving toward the iterate at constant speed.
l4qBHpMvXz.problem: Fixed-reference regularized solvers converge linearly but to a biased point, periodic-reset methods reach exact equilibria only at asymptotic or sublinear rates, and no finite-time rate was known for interior reference speeds.
l4qBHpMvXz.method: After every step the reference moves toward the iterate by a fraction beta_t in [0,1] (0 fixes the reference, 1 resets it). The paper proves rates for constant speed within an explicit window, characterizes summable speeds, and derives a closed-form asymptotic rate at interior equilibria.
l4qBHpMvXz.key_idea: Interpolate between fixed and reset proximal centers with a per-step speed beta_t, and identify which schedules give linear last-iterate convergence to the original game's Nash equilibrium.
l4qBHpMvXz.evidence: Theorems with a sharp window endpoint and closed-form asymptotic rates, plus experiments across four games using one parameter setting throughout (reviews mention a Leduc comparison with periodic reset).
l4qBHpMvXz.claimed_gains: A constant speed within an explicit window gives linear last-iterate convergence to an exact Nash equilibrium, and the moving reference lowers the saddle gap versus the fixed reference by 'more than three' (the unit is cut off in the abstract).
l4qBHpMvXz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers who gave strengths credit the analysis framework with an explicit convergence window and linear last-iterate convergence to Nash, which also generalizes several anchoring schemes.
l4qBHpMvXz.main_concern: One reviewer found the writing hard to parse (revised during rebuttal), and another notes the rate depends on a coefficient that can be arbitrarily small, as in earlier linear-convergence work.

JvCVetwXW7.one_liner: Shows full finetuning with the pretraining optimizer forgets less than other optimizers or LoRA, explained by optimizer-induced activation regularization.
JvCVetwXW7.problem: It is unclear how the optimizer used in supervised finetuning interacts with the pretraining optimizer to set the tradeoff between learning the new task and forgetting pretrained knowledge.
JvCVetwXW7.method: Controlled GPT-2 experiments pretrain with AdamW or Muon, then finetune each with AdamW, Muon and SGD on three task types and compare learning-forgetting frontiers, with theory on optimizer-induced activation regularization and weight-update structure. A synthetic language modeling experiment probes Muon's tendency toward rote memorization.
JvCVetwXW7.key_idea: Optimizers regularize activations and so shape the landscape around the pretrained checkpoint; SFT updates that match that structure, obtained by using the same optimizer, lower forgetting.
JvCVetwXW7.evidence: Controlled pretraining and SFT experiments on a small GPT-2 with AdamW, Muon and SGD, larger-model experiments (Llama and others per reviews), theoretical analysis, and a synthetic language modeling experiment on Muon memorization.
JvCVetwXW7.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract reports a better learning-forgetting tradeoff for the matched optimizer (less forgetting with the same or better new-task performance) and worse Muon results on reasoning finetuning, without numbers.
JvCVetwXW7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the clean controlled GPT-2 pretraining-to-SFT experiments and frontier analysis showing the matching optimizer has the best tradeoff, with larger-model experiments extending beyond small models.
JvCVetwXW7.main_concern: Large-model and mechanism evidence is weak: one reviewer says Figure 1 is likely mislabeled, and the memorization evidence is correlational and not tied to downstream reasoning performance.

NQE9LZLnXG.one_liner: Policy that builds constrained directed acyclic communication graphs per round for multi-round LLM agents, trained end-to-end on task reward.
NQE9LZLnXG.problem: Most multi-agent LLM methods fix the communication graph at inference or sample edges from behavior-independent distributions, so the topology cannot respond to evolving agent behavior.
NQE9LZLnXG.method: TodyComm is a task-oriented policy that constructs constrained, directed acyclic communication graphs conditioned on the unfolding interactions and is optimized end-to-end with the final task reward. It is evaluated where agents silently become unreliable at unknown rounds.
NQE9LZLnXG.key_idea: Learn a round-by-round graph policy over agent interactions, optimized with the final task reward, so the communication topology adapts as agent behavior shifts.
NQE9LZLnXG.evidence: Six benchmarks against fixed-graph and behavior-independent graph-learning baselines; reviews cite variations in attack rate, attack mechanism, agent count and backbone, a larger MMLU evaluation, transfer experiments, and a bounded-suboptimality theorem.
NQE9LZLnXG.claimed_gains: TodyComm outperforms fixed-graph and behavior-independent graph-learning baselines across six benchmarks while retaining generalizability; a review cites 67.32% on MMLU and 49.39% on MBPP at a 50% attack rate versus 44.44% and 31.71% for the strongest baselines.
NQE9LZLnXG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that adapting communication to observed behavior is sensible and that gains under changing agent reliability are substantial across attack settings, models and tasks.
NQE9LZLnXG.main_concern: The theoretical guarantee assumes accurate learned scores and leaves greedy graph construction uncontrolled, while the training procedure is underspecified and the adaptation ablation is limited.

aovKMgbn92.one_liner: Characterizes global minimizers of a parameter-sensitivity objective for algebraic completion, showing a complexity floor forces group structure.
aovKMgbn92.problem: It is unclear why continuous learning objectives favor functional compression (shared algebraic composition) and group operations over low-rank representations when learning finite binary operations.
aovKMgbn92.method: The paper analyzes global optimality of a canonical factorization model for algebraic completion and defines algebraic complexity as the infimum of its parameter-sensitivity objective under exact target reconstruction. It proves a universal complexity floor and characterizes minimizers at and above it; reviews note formal verification of foundational results in Lean 4.
aovKMgbn92.key_idea: Define algebraic complexity as the infimum of a sensitivity objective under exact reconstruction; attaining its universal floor forces unitary, homomorphic latent representations equivalent to a group's left-regular representation.
aovKMgbn92.evidence: Theorems (a lower bound with equality-case characterization via a matrix AM-GM lemma) and numerical sanity-check experiments on the HyperCube objective, as described in reviews.
aovKMgbn92.claimed_gains: not stated; the paper is theoretical and the visible abstract reports no numerical results.
aovKMgbn92.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the theory elegant and clearly developed, crediting the matrix AM-GM lemma, the characterization of global minimizers and the complexity lower bound.
aovKMgbn92.main_concern: The analysis covers exact reconstruction of fully observed tables under a specific regularizer, with no evidence it transfers to MLPs or transformers learning from partial observations, and the experiments are weak support.

PIsQv6iDXY.one_liner: Proves that zero-knowledge interactive arguments and debate for oracle-aided computation are impossible in the random oracle model.
PIsQv6iDXY.problem: Verifying AI outputs computed from confidential data without revealing the data is needed, but prior work on verifying oracle-aided computation focused on efficient verification rather than privacy.
PIsQv6iDXY.method: Allowing a verifier that runs in time polynomial in the computation, the paper proves a lower bound showing no zero-knowledge proofs for all oracle-aided computations in the random oracle model, extends it to debate, and gives a positive construction in a signed-oracle model.
PIsQv6iDXY.key_idea: A tradeoff bound shows completeness, soundness and hiding error cannot all be small in the random oracle model, so verifier leakage grows with reliability.
PIsQv6iDXY.evidence: Theoretical results: impossibility in the random oracle model even for witness hiding and with long-running prover and verifier, an extension to debate, and a positive signed-oracle construction.
PIsQv6iDXY.claimed_gains: not stated; the results are impossibility theorems, and a review cites the tradeoff bound that the sum of completeness, soundness and hiding errors is at least 1/e - o(1).
PIsQv6iDXY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that asking whether oversight verification can be private is a natural, useful question and that the lower bound, which holds even for witness hiding, and its debate extension are meaningful.
PIsQv6iDXY.main_concern: Reviewers question how much the proof goes beyond the existing lower bound for succinct arguments, and note the title overstates results limited to oracle-aided computation and debate.

js21L1V6ap.one_liner: Shows worst-query KV-cache quantization error equals, within a factor of two, the expected injective norm of a random sign tensor.
js21L1V6ap.problem: A quantized KV cache is written once and read by many future, possibly adaptive queries, so small error for a fixed query does not bound the worst-query read error.
js21L1V6ap.method: Convex-order, duality and symmetry reductions plus a structure theorem reduce the uniform read error to two scalar quantities, giving a Bernoulli counterpart of Chevet's inequality. Optimal precision allocation is then posed as a convex program.
js21L1V6ap.key_idea: Worst-query error reduces to an injective tensor norm; independent stochastic rounding is optimal among unbiased fixed-grid encoders, and value channels Gaussianize rounding noise.
js21L1V6ap.evidence: Theorems with numerical checks on synthetic Gaussian and Gaussian-mixture data, as described in reviews.
js21L1V6ap.claimed_gains: not stated as experimental numbers; the abstract claims a factor-of-two characterization of the read error and that Bernoulli and Gaussian noise models differ by a factor of order at most max{1, (log n/d)^(1/2)}.
js21L1V6ap.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit the worst-case quantization analysis as new for attention and coherent, with weak assumptions on queries and keys and a framework linking error characterization to precision allocation.
js21L1V6ap.main_concern: The results hold only for conditionally unbiased stochastic rounding with fixed grids and mainly value quantization, with validation limited to synthetic data and an extremely dense presentation.

4LEZouxTXe.one_liner: Tests whether local quadratic Taylor models at intermediate checkpoints predict LLM pretraining dynamics, then analyzes their Hessian spectrum and stability.
4LEZouxTXe.problem: Optimization theory relies on idealized loss-landscape models whose tractability trades off against accuracy, and it is unclear whether the simplest quadratic model describes real LLM training.
4LEZouxTXe.method: The authors Taylor expand the model and loss at intermediate checkpoints of a 150M-parameter LLM trained on 3B tokens and compare predicted and actual dynamics. They then estimate the Hessian spectrum with Lanczos quadrature using very deep probes and test local linear stability against theoretical predictions.
4LEZouxTXe.key_idea: Predict optimization with a quadratic Taylor expansion at intermediate checkpoints, and use deep Lanczos quadrature to characterize its Hessian spectrum and stochastic edge-of-stability behavior.
4LEZouxTXe.evidence: A single 150M-parameter LLM trained on 3B tokens, with Lanczos spectral estimates validated against ground truth and a 5x5 learning-rate by batch-size stability grid with 10 seeds per cell, per reviews.
4LEZouxTXe.claimed_gains: The quadratic expansions accurately predict optimization dynamics over windows lasting up to 10% of training; no other numbers are stated.
4LEZouxTXe.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the study is thorough and that local quadratic models predicting loss trajectories over a nontrivial fraction of training is a useful, unexpected finding that bridges theory and LLM practice.
4LEZouxTXe.main_concern: All experiments use a single 150M-parameter model, and the approximation is weak early in training and with constant learning rates, so transfer to larger LLMs and the premise of the 'defense' are unclear.

8YSUYtQHu7.one_liner: Learns domain-specific causal graphs by combining within-domain conditional independences with cross-domain invariances, via inv-Markov equivalence and Diverse-FCI.
8YSUYtQHu7.problem: Multi-domain causal discovery usually assumes domains arise from interventions on a common baseline graph, which fails when domain graphs differ structurally through edge additions, deletions or reversals.
8YSUYtQHu7.method: The paper shows that mechanisms stable across domains induce cross-domain distributional invariances, characterizes the constraints these impose on tuples of domain-specific causal graphs (the inv-Markov equivalence class), and develops the Diverse-FCI algorithm to learn them.
8YSUYtQHu7.key_idea: Treat mechanisms stable across domains as cross-domain distributional invariances and combine them with within-domain conditional independences to orient edges unidentifiable in any single domain.
8YSUYtQHu7.evidence: Theoretical characterization of inv-Markov equivalence plus experiments on runtime scaling with the number of domains and real-world datasets (SEER and MIMIC-IV), as described in reviews.
8YSUYtQHu7.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract claims the algorithm learns cause-effect relations beyond what each domain alone identifies, even when graphs differ, without numbers.
8YSUYtQHu7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the setting (domains with structurally different graphs and no shared baseline) is well motivated and the theory is fairly complete and clearly distinguished from prior work.
8YSUYtQHu7.main_concern: Reviewers cite an incremental contribution, a counterexample to Lemma B.5 on which the central characterization relies, and runtime that grows quickly with the number of domains.

1QjSmJ1dVO.one_liner: Feed-forward generative 3D scene reconstruction distilling video-diffusion and 2D foundation models into 3D Gaussians carrying semantics and instances.
1QjSmJ1dVO.problem: Generative 3D reconstruction from a single image lacks the scene semantics and object identities needed in robotics, while existing 3D understanding methods need captured multi-view scenes, generalize poorly, or rely on per-scene optimization.
1QjSmJ1dVO.method: LucidLyra distills knowledge from a camera-controlled video diffusion model and frozen 2D vision foundation models into 3D Gaussians that jointly encode geometry, appearance, open-vocabulary semantics and class-agnostic instance cues, predicted feed-forward from video latents. Training needs neither manual 3D annotations nor captured multi-view data.
1QjSmJ1dVO.key_idea: Predict open-vocabulary semantic and instance features per Gaussian from video latents inside the generative reconstruction decoder, supervised by distilled 2D foundation-model features.
1QjSmJ1dVO.evidence: Comparison against baselines combining 3DGS segmentation approaches with generative 3D reconstruction on curated synthetic and real-image-conditioned benchmarks, plus component ablations and a monocular-video extension.
1QjSmJ1dVO.claimed_gains: not stated with numbers; the abstract says only that it outperforms baselines combining 3DGS segmentation with generative reconstruction while preserving reconstruction quality.
1QjSmJ1dVO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that jointly predicting geometry, appearance, semantics and instances in a feed-forward 3DGS representation is practical and gives competitive segmentation with preserved reconstruction quality.
1QjSmJ1dVO.main_concern: The contribution is seen as an incremental extension of Lyra with standard 2D-to-3D distillation, and newly revealed regions and the benefit of joint learning are not separately evaluated.

zZu1tOtGDW.one_liner: Latent-space world-model RL for driving using shortcut forcing, an autoregressive dense reward model, and Gaussian vocabulary sampling for GRPO.
zZu1tOtGDW.problem: Video-generation world models can replace real interaction for RL, but multi-step denoising and RGB decoding make imagined rollouts computationally expensive.
zZu1tOtGDW.method: DreamerAD uses denoised latent features from video generation models with three mechanisms: shortcut forcing that distills multi-step flow updates into low-step latent rollouts, an autoregressive dense reward model predicting step-wise rewards from latents, and Gaussian vocabulary sampling for GRPO that constrains exploration to physically plausible trajectories.
zZu1tOtGDW.key_idea: Distill multi-step flow denoising into few-step latent rollouts and score them with a latent dense reward model, avoiding RGB decoding during RL policy optimization.
zZu1tOtGDW.evidence: NAVSIM v2 and zero-shot closed-loop HUGSIM, on both the driving-specific Epona world model and the Wan2.2 video backbone, with ablations (Table 4) described in reviews.
zZu1tOtGDW.claimed_gains: Shortcut forcing accelerates world model inference by up to 80×, and DreamerAD reaches 91.4 EPDMS on NAVSIM v2 and 55.0 HD-Score on zero-shot HUGSIM.
zZu1tOtGDW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree DreamerAD improves over its backbones on NAVSIM and zero-shot closed-loop HUGSIM, with one-step latent rollouts that cut world-model latency on two different backbones.
zZu1tOtGDW.main_concern: The experiments do not isolate latent imagination from additional trajectory supervision, expert-anchored candidate filtering and reward approximation, and the novelty is mainly a combination of existing components.

83K2OoCrcv.one_liner: ViT backbone that recursively groups patch embeddings into part-whole hierarchies through graph reasoning and hierarchical pooling with readable assignments.
83K2OoCrcv.problem: Hierarchy-aware visual backbones give limited quantitative access to the part-whole relations they induce.
83K2OoCrcv.method: HIVE maps image patches to fine-level embeddings, recursively organizes them into higher-level structures through graph-based reasoning and hierarchical pooling, and reintegrates multi-level representations into the token space. Cross-level assignments are directly readable as a part-whole composition graph, and part-whole contribution analysis quantifies fine-to-mid and mid-to-coarse composition.
83K2OoCrcv.key_idea: Keep the cross-level assignment matrices used for pooling as an explicit part-whole composition graph, reused for feature aggregation and patch-level projection.
83K2OoCrcv.evidence: Experiments as a general-purpose ViT backbone; reviews cite PartImageNet NMI and ARI comparisons under the same MPAE pipeline and a controlled ADE20K comparison.
83K2OoCrcv.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract says only that HIVE is a competitive general-purpose ViT backbone with class-relevant, structurally coherent multilevel embeddings.
83K2OoCrcv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the motivation is clear and that the assignment-preserving, graph-based design makes the structure natively explainable, with supporting empirical gains.
83K2OoCrcv.main_concern: The evidence does not show that learned parent-child assignments are semantically correct part-whole relations, and the architecture is seen as an evolution of established grouping and pooling ideas.

ssa0Epyz3L.one_liner: Certifies BPE's gap to optimal token count via dual decomposition over integer linear programs, scaling to 113 GB of ClimbMix.
ssa0Epyz3L.problem: BPE searches the tokenizer space greedily, and it is unknown how close its token alphabet is to the optimal token count on realistic-size corpora.
ssa0Epyz3L.method: The authors cast four declaratively specified tokenization objectives (DVS, OPE, OMS, LVS) as integer linear programs and apply dual decomposition, so subproblems for DVS, OPE and LVS are solved by specialized data-parallel algorithms over strings, to bound the gap between standard tokenizers and the optimal alphabet.
ssa0Epyz3L.key_idea: Decompose tokenization ILPs into per-string subproblems solved by specialized data-parallel algorithms, yielding certified bounds on the optimal token count.
ssa0Epyz3L.evidence: Certification experiments on corpora up to 113 GB of ClimbMix on one GPU, with candidate tokens restricted to observed substrings of two to five bytes occurring at least twice, as described in reviews.
ssa0Epyz3L.claimed_gains: The bounds certify that BPE is close to the DVS and OPE optima under the evaluated tokenization constraints and becomes closer as the token alphabet grows; the solver scales to 113 GB of ClimbMix on one GPU.
ssa0Epyz3L.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the question of how close BPE is to optimal tokenization is important and well motivated, and that the unified ILP framework and scalable solver make certificates practical.
ssa0Epyz3L.main_concern: The near-optimality conclusion holds only under restricted candidate tokens and Viterbi segmentation rather than BPE's merge-order encoding, and the text is very dense.

4oYHhkEtbA.one_liner: Proves matching O(ε^-6) upper and Ω(ε^-6) lower communication bounds for FedAvg(LoRA) and proposes FedStabLoRA with persistent client corrections.
4oYHhkEtbA.problem: Existing FedAvg(LoRA) convergence analyses assume bounded LoRA factors, and multiple local steps introduce client drift that grows with the factor norms.
4oYHhkEtbA.method: The paper proves an O(ε^-6) communication upper bound for FedAvg(LoRA) under full client participation without the bounded-factor assumption, and an Ω(ε^-6) lower bound for multiple local steps even with adaptive stepsizes. FedStabLoRA adds persistent client corrections to reduce client drift; reviews describe it as a SCAFFOLD-style correction with a FedProx-style penalty.
4oYHhkEtbA.key_idea: Control factor-amplified client drift in federated LoRA with persistent client corrections combined with a proximal penalty, using a correction scale tailored to the penalized local updates.
4oYHhkEtbA.evidence: Theorems (upper and lower bounds and FedStabLoRA convergence rates) plus experiments on language and vision tasks under heterogeneous data and partial participation, as described in reviews.
4oYHhkEtbA.claimed_gains: FedAvg(LoRA) attains an O(ε^-6) communication upper bound (centralized LoRA gradient descent achieves O(ε^-4)) with an Ω(ε^-6) lower bound for multiple local steps, and FedStabLoRA is introduced to accelerate this rate (abstract cut off).
4oYHhkEtbA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that removing the bounded-factor assumption and proving matching upper and lower bounds is a meaningful theoretical contribution, with experiments on both language and vision tasks.
4oYHhkEtbA.main_concern: The theory covers exact local gradients and specific step sizes while experiments use stochastic gradients and larger learning rates, and algorithmic novelty and direct evidence for factor-amplified drift are limited.

uIgzy7Ua48.one_liner: Trains mobile-manipulation VLAs only on simulation data (SimAction, SimVQA, SimDeploy) for zero-shot transfer to real homes.
uIgzy7Ua48.problem: VLAs for robotics are limited by the cost of real-world data collection, and zero-shot sim-to-real VLA learning for mobile manipulation is underexplored.
uIgzy7Ua48.method: SimVLA is pre-trained on SimAction (large-scale action data over 30 mobile manipulation tasks composed from atomic skills) and SimVQA (spatial, geometric and subtask-level visual-language supervision from privileged simulator state), then post-trained on SimAction plus SimDeploy, a dataset collected from policy rollouts across simulated environments.
uIgzy7Ua48.key_idea: Combine action data from composed atomic skills, privileged-state VQA supervision, and policy-rollout data from simulation to train a VLA without teleoperation.
uIgzy7Ua48.evidence: Tasks including restocking, pouring and cleaning, with zero-shot real-world transfer including real home environments; reviews cite component ablations and binary success counts.
uIgzy7Ua48.claimed_gains: SimVLA outperforms policies trained on 50 in-domain real-world demonstrations; a review cites 26/60 pantry trials versus 3/60 for π0.5 fine-tuned on 200 demonstrations per task.
uIgzy7Ua48.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that real-world transfer with coordinated base-arm control, the comprehensive synthesis pipeline, and component ablations with binary success counts give convincing evidence.
uIgzy7Ua48.main_concern: The mechanism enabling sim-to-real transfer is not isolated: ablations do not separate visual representations, domain randomization and spatial supervision, and the SimDeploy gain is confounded with scene coverage and success filtering.

1MI7X0ZL2J.one_liner: On-policy self-distillation for safety alignment that bounds rollout length by Teacher Rescue Rate and distills only safety-critical tokens.
1MI7X0ZL2J.problem: On-Policy Self-Distillation for safety alignment suffers supervisory collapse over long rollouts, where the teacher's corrective efficacy falls as the student's prefix lengthens, and gradient dilution from stylistic shifts induced by privileged prompting.
1MI7X0ZL2J.method: EOPSA adds Adaptive Rollout Scheduling, which bounds the generation horizon using a Teacher Rescue Rate (TRR) metric, and Selective Distillation, which filters out safety-neutral tokens so gradients focus on safety-critical tokens.
1MI7X0ZL2J.key_idea: Cap the on-policy rollout horizon where the teacher still reliably corrects (measured by Teacher Rescue Rate) and restrict the distillation loss to safety-critical tokens.
1MI7X0ZL2J.evidence: Experiments across multiple model scales with ablations and efficiency evaluation on safety and reasoning benchmarks, as described in the TL;DR and reviews.
1MI7X0ZL2J.claimed_gains: Reduces rollout compute by ~50% while improving safety compliance and reasoning retention (TL;DR); no other numbers are stated.
1MI7X0ZL2J.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is important and the motivation clear, and that TRR scheduling and token filtering are simple and effective, with comprehensive experiments across model scales, ablations and efficiency.
1MI7X0ZL2J.main_concern: The definition and validation of safety-critical tokens and of the TRR metric are weak, and the 1k rollout cap versus the baseline's 4k may confound scheduling with simple truncation.

l0IpwY3UFn.one_liner: Persistent 3D object memory from egocentric video that clusters observations by resting location and records moves after repeated evidence.
l0IpwY3UFn.problem: Embodied assistants must recall where objects were left and what containers held, including objects the person never touched, without re-accessing the original video.
l0IpwY3UFn.method: LEDGER associates observations across the recording, retains objects after they leave the view, clusters each object's observations by resting locations, and records a move only after repeated evidence to reduce localization noise. Short descriptions preserve details such as contents or supporting surface, and the records answer spatial questions without the original images or video.
l0IpwY3UFn.key_idea: Store per-object records of resting locations, repeated-evidence move histories and short descriptions, then answer spatial questions from these records without re-reading the video.
l0IpwY3UFn.evidence: HD-EPIC, UCS-Bench and Ego4D evaluations, component analyses of temporal persistence, descriptions and retrieval, and a study on 100 stitched multi-scene streams.
l0IpwY3UFn.claimed_gains: Raises HD-EPIC accuracy from 29.7% to 42.6% and UCS-Bench accuracy from 33.8% to 38.5%, and localizes Ego4D objects with a 0.99 m median error on returned predictions.
l0IpwY3UFn.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is well motivated, that separating memory construction from query-time reasoning removes a look-back shortcut, and that the evaluation and diagnostic analysis are thorough.
l0IpwY3UFn.main_concern: Conceptual novelty is incremental and the method is a complex pipeline of existing components, with weak object identity association and no mechanism to bound storage on long videos.

enNFbX4WOc.one_liner: Neural operator for fiber orientation distribution super-resolution that preserves antipodal symmetry on the sphere, with patch-based NFONet.
enNFbX4WOc.problem: Learning-based FOD angular super resolution methods ignore the spherical-native geometry of FOD and treat the task as conventional regression.
enNFbX4WOc.method: The task is reformulated as spherical operator learning: the Neural Fiber Operator (NFO) learns the solution operator while preserving the antipodal symmetry of FOD, and NFONet applies it patch-wise for whole- or partial-brain FOD modeling. Reviews describe the operator as a per-degree scalar multiplication of even-order spherical harmonic coefficients.
enNFbX4WOc.key_idea: Learn a spherical operator over even-degree spherical-harmonic FOD coefficients, which builds antipodal symmetry into the model, instead of regressing FOD voxels as 3D images.
enNFbX4WOc.evidence: Three diffusion MRI datasets covering in-domain reconstruction, zero-shot generalization to independent cohorts and acquisition protocols, and ex-vivo validation; reviews cite HCP-YA, MGH and corpus callosum data and tractography.
enNFbX4WOc.claimed_gains: The abstract reports consistent top performance and a favorable accuracy-efficiency trade-off without numbers; a review cites 2.74M trainable parameters, fewer than FOD-Net and FOD-Swin-Net.
enNFbX4WOc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is practically motivated and that evaluation across protocols, cohorts and in vivo to ex vivo transfer gives useful evidence under distribution shift.
enNFbX4WOc.main_concern: Novelty over existing spherical operators such as GSNO is not established, since the operator reduces to a simple per-degree spectral scaling, and ablations do not isolate its contribution.

FkyrrVjfMT.one_liner: Shows that adding descent after each move erases most of learned local-search policies' advantage over random move selection.
FkyrrVjfMT.problem: Learned local-search policies are evaluated without the descent step used by iterated local search, so their advantage over random move selection may be overstated.
FkyrrVjfMT.method: The authors define commit depth (cd), the number of descent steps run after each applied move, and compare learned and random move selection at their best commit depths in a controlled job-shop study and six published methods. They then fine-tune policies with descent in the training loop.
FkyrrVjfMT.key_idea: Vary commit depth (descent steps per move) for learned and random selectors; scorers trained on one-step outcomes prefer moves that change the solution least, which loses under descent.
FkyrrVjfMT.evidence: A controlled job-shop study with a random-forest move scorer and six published methods (including ECO-DQN, NeuOpt, DACT, L2S and a learned SAT heuristic the authors trained), plus fine-tuning with descent in the loop.
FkyrrVjfMT.claimed_gains: A random-forest scorer beats random selection by 220 makespan units at cd=1 but trails it by 126 with descent to a local optimum, and the learned advantage shrinks by a factor of 34 to 69 in ECO-DQN and 42 in NeuOpt and disappears or reverses in DACT, L2S and the SAT heuristic.
FkyrrVjfMT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper raises a relevant, self-critical evaluation question and that the controlled job-shop experiment, which varies only commit depth, is convincing.
FkyrrVjfMT.main_concern: Reviewers call the finding unsurprising given classical iterated local search, find the terminology and presentation unclear, and note thin causal and fine-tuning evidence beyond job-shop scheduling.

xuuGeDYUIb.one_liner: Benchmark of 172 instruction-conditioned EEG analysis tasks across 17 datasets for evaluating LLMs and EEG agents with executable references.
xuuGeDYUIb.problem: Existing EEG evaluations focus on isolated decoding tasks or system-specific demonstrations and capture only limited aspects of the competence needed to interpret instructions, process signals, derive evidence and draw grounded conclusions.
xuuGeDYUIb.method: BrainBench has four subsets (Foundational Analysis, Sleep Assessment, Neurocognitive Assessment, Physiological Integration) covering 17 datasets, 172 tasks and over 4K real-data instances. Systems perform the requested analysis and produce verifiable outputs, evaluated for 13 LLMs under autonomous code execution and structured agentic analysis.
xuuGeDYUIb.key_idea: Score LLMs on executable, instruction-conditioned EEG analyses against reference outputs under two paradigms, code generation and structured agentic tools, rather than on fixed-label decoding.
xuuGeDYUIb.evidence: 13 representative LLMs across more than 100K executions under autonomous code execution and structured agentic analysis, with reasoning and failure analyses and expert cross-review mentioned in reviews.
xuuGeDYUIb.claimed_gains: not stated as accuracy numbers; the abstract reports that results vary substantially across models, subsets, difficulty levels and execution paradigms.
xuuGeDYUIb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the benchmark is broad and useful, covering preprocessing, quantitative analysis, multimodal integration and artifact generation, with comprehensive model and paradigm comparisons.
xuuGeDYUIb.main_concern: What the benchmark measures is not disentangled: scoring may reward agreement with hidden implementation choices or supplied tools, and the four overlapping subsets are not well justified.

P2Orv13zzw.one_liner: Router learns when a small draft model should call a large teacher by comparing the future outcomes of their actions.
P2Orv13zzw.problem: Existing routers based on draft confidence or process scores judge the draft's proposed action but do not estimate how replacing it with a teacher action would affect later task completion.
P2Orv13zzw.method: During training, draft and teacher propose actions from the same state and an offline evaluator compares the two successors under the same remaining step budget; the outcome difference supervises the router. At inference, the router estimates replacement benefit from information available before the teacher call, weighs it against teacher cost, and the teacher provides one action before the draft resumes.
P2Orv13zzw.key_idea: Train the router on the difference in task outcomes between draft and teacher successor states under equal step budgets, so it estimates replacement benefit rather than draft uncertainty.
P2Orv13zzw.evidence: Five benchmarks spanning symbolic reasoning and interactive tasks; reviews cite baselines, ablations, transfer experiments, an independent RuleTaker evaluation and ALFWorld token-cost comparisons.
P2Orv13zzw.claimed_gains: not stated with numbers in the visible abstract (text cut off); a review cites RuleTaker pAUC gains of 1.18 on Qwen and 1.59 on Phi over draft-safety.
P2Orv13zzw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that comparing successors from the same state gives the router a concrete supervision target, with substantial accuracy gains and lower teacher cost on symbolic reasoning tasks.
P2Orv13zzw.main_concern: Training labels depend on privileged offline outcome evaluation that is costly for general tasks, gains are weaker on interactive tasks, and novelty over value-based routing is limited.

LR03iLS9xG.one_liner: MLLM agent learns an executable Colored-Petri-Net forensic skill graph for image forgery detection while keeping the MLLM and tools frozen.
LR03iLS9xG.problem: Existing MLLM-plus-tool forensic methods encode tool-use experience in model parameters or predefined workflows, so it cannot be directly updated when new attacks and tools emerge.
LR03iLS9xG.method: ForensicCPN represents forensic experience as an executable skill graph inspired by Colored Petri Nets, where the agent proposes a manipulation hypothesis and gathers evidence until it is confirmed, revised or resolved into a verdict. A forensic harness executes the skill, which evolves through skill learning (agents distill labeled trajectories into validated revisions) and test-time evolving (label-free exploration consolidated back into the skill).
LR03iLS9xG.key_idea: Make the forensic skill, an executable Colored-Petri-Net graph of hypothesis, evidence and verdict states, the learning target, revised from trajectories while the MLLM and expert tools stay frozen.
LR03iLS9xG.evidence: Seven conventional manipulation benchmarks and two generative-manipulation benchmarks, with comparisons of skill representations, majority-voting and learned-fusion baselines, and analyses of skill evolution.
LR03iLS9xG.claimed_gains: not stated in the visible abstract (text cut off); a review cites the evolved skill beating majority voting and a dataset-level oracle by +7.1 and +4.4 weighted accuracy.
LR03iLS9xG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that representing forensic experience as an executable, revisable, evidence-conditioned skill graph is a meaningful alternative to parameter updates, evaluated across many benchmarks.
LR03iLS9xG.main_concern: Controls are insufficient: the test-time protocol evolves the skill on target benchmark data, and comparisons neither separate CPN benefits from execution control nor measure the learning procedure against competing agentic or skill-learning methods.

zSqvpMEG2m.one_liner: Pre-backbone sparse token selection under spatio-temporal coverage constraints plus recovery adapters for lightweight video temporal grounding.
zSqvpMEG2m.problem: MLLM-based video temporal grounding is expensive for long videos because of large parameter counts and dense visual encoding cost.
zSqvpMEG2m.method: CoverVTG selects a sparse set of tokens within each local spatio-temporal tube under explicit spatial and temporal coverage constraints before the backbone, so discarded observations stay locally observable from retained tokens. Lightweight tube-local recovery adapters inserted in a frozen visual backbone progressively exploit these complementary observations.
zSqvpMEG2m.key_idea: Treat pre-backbone token pruning as structured sparse observation: select tokens under spatial and temporal coverage constraints so dropped content stays recoverable from retained neighbors.
zSqvpMEG2m.evidence: Four datasets under zero-shot and fine-tuned settings, a stated bound on local recovery error under spatio-temporal smoothness, and latency and ablation tables described in reviews.
zSqvpMEG2m.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract text is cut off before results, and reviews describe a promising accuracy-efficiency trade-off and reduced latency without figures.
zSqvpMEG2m.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that pruning tokens before the backbone targets a real bottleneck for long videos and that results across four datasets show a promising accuracy-efficiency trade-off.
zSqvpMEG2m.main_concern: The benefit of coverage-constrained selection is not isolated (no equal-budget resizing baseline), its distinction from prior pre-encoding token reduction and UniversalVTG is unclear, and dynamic-scene behavior is untested.

QOPnL3LVFC.one_liner: Post-processes Fourier neural operator Jacobians via purification into preconditioners for GMRES, without retraining.
QOPnL3LVFC.problem: Solution supervision alone does not ensure that neural operators yield effective preconditioners, so existing approaches modify training objectives or impose additional constraints.
QOPnL3LVFC.method: The paper shows theoretically that FNOs trained for solution prediction contain recoverable preconditioning structure, and introduces purification, a post-processing step that extracts it from FNO Jacobians without retraining. The resulting preconditioner (NOP) is used with flexible GMRES and Newton-GMRES.
QOPnL3LVFC.key_idea: Treat the FNO as an approximate inverse PDE operator and clean its Jacobian by removing off-diagonal components (purification) to obtain a usable preconditioner.
QOPnL3LVFC.evidence: Poisson experiments supporting the theory, Helmholtz problems with FGMRES, and nonlinear convection-diffusion with Newton-GMRES; reviews note 2D experiments on 64x64 grids and theory covering only a simplified linear FNO.
QOPnL3LVFC.claimed_gains: For Helmholtz problems NOP reduces mean FGMRES iterations by up to 12.4× versus unpreconditioned FGMRES, and for nonlinear convection-diffusion it reduces mean cumulative GMRES iterations by up to 9.6× versus unpreconditioned Newton-GMRES.
QOPnL3LVFC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that extracting preconditioning structure from an already trained FNO without retraining is an interesting, practical idea backed by clear theory in the simplified linear case.
QOPnL3LVFC.main_concern: The theory covers only linear, Fourier-diagonal FNOs while the experiments use nonlinear 2D models on small grids, and the benefit over classical preconditioners such as the Fast Poisson Solver is unclear.

r7kVoq2Sz5.one_liner: Bayesian bound-guided test-time adaptation that rectifies the class prior, restricts updates to a low-displacement subspace, and weights samples by reliability.
r7kVoq2Sz5.problem: Test-time adaptation methods often degrade below the frozen source model on non-stationary medical streams because plasticity for tracking the target and stability for preserving generic knowledge compete for the same parameters.
r7kVoq2Sz5.method: The paper decomposes the predictive posterior into a class prior and a class-conditional likelihood, giving a Bayesian Generalization Error Bound (BGEB) that factorizes target risk into finite-batch uncertainty, prior mismatch, conditional shift and parameter drift. SynerTTA rectifies the online prior, restricts updates to a low-displacement subspace, and weights adaptation by instance reliability.
r7kVoq2Sz5.key_idea: Use a Bayesian decomposition of target risk to turn the stability-plasticity dilemma into a trade-off, addressed by prior rectification, low-displacement parameter updates and reliability weighting.
r7kVoq2Sz5.evidence: Eight medical benchmarks across three modalities against thirteen baselines, with ablations and robustness evaluations described in reviews.
r7kVoq2Sz5.claimed_gains: SynerTTA outperforms thirteen baselines, surpassing the second-best method by 8.51% in accuracy and 5.71% in macro-F1 (abstract cut off after that).
r7kVoq2Sz5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the stability-plasticity problem in non-stationary medical test-time adaptation is important and that a bound-motivated algorithm with multi-modality experiments is a reasonable, promising approach.
r7kVoq2Sz5.main_concern: The link between the bound and the algorithm is weak (conditional shift ignored, bound terms unobservable, displacement argument assumes plain gradient descent), with limited theoretical novelty and inconsistent reported numbers noted.

Nl50dd67jb.one_liner: Confidence-gated exploration algorithm CGT-UCB for strategyproof linear contextual bandits with private contexts, plus a minimax regret lower bound.
Nl50dd67jb.problem: In contextual bandits with private contexts, agents may misreport to avoid exploration, yet classical strategyproof algorithms lack polylogarithmic problem-dependent regret or incur linear regret, and LinUCB suffers linear regret in strategic settings.
Nl50dd67jb.method: The paper shows gaps in Explore-then-Commit, truthful Thompson sampling and LinUCB, proves an Ω(T^(2/3)) minimax regret lower bound for strategyproof algorithms, and proposes CGT-UCB, which combines confidence-gated exploration with an LP-based mechanism.
Nl50dd67jb.key_idea: Gate exploration by confidence and combine it with a linear-program mechanism so misreporting contexts does not help, giving sublinear worst-case and instance-dependent regret.
Nl50dd67jb.evidence: Regret upper and lower bounds with synthetic and real-world dataset experiments, as described in reviews (short horizon, few synthetic configurations).
Nl50dd67jb.claimed_gains: Establishes an Ω(T^(2/3)) minimax regret lower bound for strategyproof algorithms and instance-dependent regret guarantees with worst-case scaling matching up to logarithmic factors; no empirical numbers are stated.
Nl50dd67jb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is well motivated and the theory is solid, with upper and lower bounds matching in T and the lower bound clarifying the cost of strategyproofness.
Nl50dd67jb.main_concern: The lower bound needs clarification (choice of K and the dimension in the proof), the bounds have gaps in M and d, and experiments are limited to short horizons and few synthetic configurations.

xmpyzuagpu.one_liner: Automated curriculum for agent harness optimization: failure-pattern bandit arms adaptively choose which training scenarios drive harness updates.
xmpyzuagpu.problem: Harness optimization methods improve how the harness is updated but fix which training scenarios generate feedback, even though the most useful scenarios change as the harness evolves.
xmpyzuagpu.method: ActiveSaddler models the curriculum as a non-stationary bandit whose arms are reusable failure patterns abstracted from recurring failures, estimates the learning progress from targeting each pattern, and balances revisiting known weaknesses with exploring unseen scenarios. Optimization outcomes update the discovered patterns and their priorities.
xmpyzuagpu.key_idea: Treat scenario selection as a non-stationary bandit over dynamically discovered failure-pattern arms prioritized by estimated learning progress, so the curriculum co-evolves with the harness.
xmpyzuagpu.evidence: Experiments on GAIA2 and Terminal-Bench 2.0, with ablations, cost analysis and an added experiment applying the curriculum to GEPA, as described in reviews.
xmpyzuagpu.claimed_gains: Improves test Pass@1 by 4.4 and 7.5 percentage points over the same harness optimizer with a fixed scenario order (comparison text cut off in the abstract).
xmpyzuagpu.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that adaptive scenario selection is a timely, well-motivated direction and that results show consistent improvements over fixed-order baselines on two benchmarks.
xmpyzuagpu.main_concern: The contribution is seen as combining existing ideas, with limited robustness evidence (few independent optimization runs), missing overhead and LLM-cost analysis, and baselines lacking adaptive failure-based replay.

BXHawAvJsy.one_liner: Unified (ε,δ)-certified continual learning-unlearning framework for regularization-based CL, with first-order and second-order unlearning mechanisms.
BXHawAvJsy.problem: Integrating certified unlearning into continual learning is largely unexplored, though models must learn sequentially, retain past knowledge, and reliably remove requested information.
BXHawAvJsy.method: The paper derives an algorithm-dependent CL excess-risk bound for nonconvex losses and develops two certified-unlearning mechanisms: a first-order one exploiting natural forgetting from CL updates, and a second-order one for request-specific unlearning of arbitrary requests whose loss depends on request order.
BXHawAvJsy.key_idea: Certify unlearning in regularization-based CL via natural forgetting from later updates or second-order correction, showing the regularizer trades retained knowledge against removal of deleted-task influence.
BXHawAvJsy.evidence: Theoretical bounds for nonconvex losses with instantiations for EWC, MAS and task-additive regularizers, plus empirical Pareto frontiers; reviews note experiments on CIFAR-100 with one ResNet-18 architecture and a fixed pretrained backbone.
BXHawAvJsy.claimed_gains: not stated as numbers; the abstract reports that stronger regularization such as MAS gives lower unlearning loss and that the two methods show distinct Pareto frontiers (text cut off).
BXHawAvJsy.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree continual learning-unlearning is a genuine gap and that the unified framework, risk decomposition and two complementary algorithms with Pareto analysis give a useful conceptual account.
BXHawAvJsy.main_concern: Assumptions such as strong convexity and Lipschitz Hessian do not hold for deep networks, and experiments are thin (one dataset, one architecture, no unlearning baselines) with presentation issues.

vSSGBObQIY.one_liner: Decoder-only view synthesis model sharing weights between scene reconstruction and rendering, using a per-layer KV cache as the scene representation.
vSSGBObQIY.problem: It is unclear which composition of encoder-decoder, decoder-only or latent scene representation is most effective for regression-based view synthesis.
vSSGBObQIY.method: DVSM builds a KV cache from context views with a decoder and renders each target through unidirectional cross-attention using the same decoder weights. Foundation features can be injected during context prefill as an orthogonal enhancement.
vSSGBObQIY.key_idea: Share one decoder's weights across context prefill and target rendering, with its KV cache as the scene representation, so features from the two stages align.
vSSGBObQIY.evidence: Benchmarks on DL3DV and zero-shot out-of-distribution datasets, ablations of weight decoupling under matched data and schedules, and feature analyses; reviews mention sparse and dense inputs and higher resolutions.
vSSGBObQIY.claimed_gains: DVSM improves PSNR over the strongest baseline in each setting by 1.1-3.3dB on DL3DV and 0.6-1.8dB on zero-shot out-of-distribution benchmarks, without an explicit 3D scene representation.
vSSGBObQIY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the architecture is simple and clear, with weight sharing supported by controlled ablations and evaluation across sparse and dense inputs and multiple zero-shot datasets.
vSSGBObQIY.main_concern: Generality and novelty are limited: the gain may stem from the per-layer KV cache rather than weight sharing, and conclusions may not hold under other data scales, few-view inputs or architectures.

6WXGN1g1Fr.one_liner: Routes likely long-tail prompts, identified from partial-rollout completion status, to isolated low-concurrency replica groups in synchronous LLM rollouts.
6WXGN1g1Fr.problem: In synchronous LLM rollouts a few long-tail generations dominate a rollout step, and uniform routing slows them further by placing them in high-concurrency decoding batches.
6WXGN1g1Fr.method: TailSieve uses partial-rollout completion status as a training-free signal to identify candidate tail groups, combines them with newly sampled prompts, and generates all responses from scratch under the current policy. A hierarchical controller adjusts the number of isolated groups in a fast inner loop and the number of serving replicas in a slower outer loop, and the low-concurrency execution enables route-specialized speculative decoding with MTP or DFlash.
6WXGN1g1Fr.key_idea: Exploit the persistence of prompt-level tail tendencies across policy updates to isolate predicted tail prompts onto separate low-concurrency replicas, sized by a two-timescale controller.
6WXGN1g1Fr.evidence: Evaluated across several configurations on a single node with eight H100 GPUs using a customized vLLM build, plus an offline routing analysis in which top-k isolation is within 4% of the oracle across 100 sampled instances, as described in reviews.
6WXGN1g1Fr.claimed_gains: Achieves up to 1.67× speedup (the abstract is cut off after this).
6WXGN1g1Fr.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it is a simple, practical fix for a real rollout bottleneck that keeps training on-policy without an extra length predictor, with a principled offline analysis and a broad systems evaluation.
6WXGN1g1Fr.main_concern: The evaluation is limited to one 8-GPU node with re-implemented routing-only baselines, and it does not disentangle tail-aware routing from partial-rollout selection or measure end-to-end RL training time.

qhfSTsw4FV.one_liner: Benchmark of 1,500 real visual metaphors with multiple-choice and dimension-based MLLM-judge evaluation for text-to-image models.
qhfSTsw4FV.problem: The ability of text-to-image models to produce visual metaphors, images that convey abstract ideas by combining elements from two domains, remains largely unexamined.
qhfSTsw4FV.method: VMetaphor-Bench has 1,500 visual metaphors curated from real-world creative imagery, organized into three levels and ten categories, each paired with two prompts of differing specificity. Evaluation combines an MLLM-as-judge multiple-choice protocol of 9,594 questions across four levels of metaphorical fidelity with a dimension-based score along three perceptual dimensions.
qhfSTsw4FV.key_idea: Decompose metaphor fidelity into four levels of MLLM-judged multiple-choice questions, separating object recognition from relationship and mapping errors, with prompts at two specificity levels.
qhfSTsw4FV.evidence: Evaluation of 12 representative text-to-image models, with human validation and a second-judge reliability check described in reviews.
qhfSTsw4FV.claimed_gains: not stated as scores; the abstract reports that even the strongest proprietary models among 12 evaluated struggle with compositional structuring and cross-domain mapping.
qhfSTsw4FV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the benchmark is built from real metaphors with verified annotations, and that its multi-level protocol, human-agreement checks and 12-model coverage give fine-grained diagnostic insight.
qhfSTsw4FV.main_concern: The validity of the evaluation is questioned: conceptual prompts are not truly abstract, mapping-level questions may penalize alternative realizations, and MLLM judges may share biases with limited human validation.

D2AfBRZ01K.one_liner: Training-free LLM provenance fingerprint comparing top-k vocabulary projections of late hidden states on 250 fixed probes via Jaccard overlap.
D2AfBRZ01K.problem: Establishing a language model's provenance, meaning its base checkpoint and possible training-data overlap, is a governance challenge that metadata alone cannot resolve.
D2AfBRZ01K.method: TokenPrint compares the top-k vocabulary projections of late hidden states on 250 fixed probes using Jaccard overlap of decoded token strings, calibrated on 32 open-weight models (0.6B-32B) with documented relationships.
D2AfBRZ01K.key_idea: Fingerprint a model by the set of tokens its late hidden states project to on fixed probes, so Jaccard overlap tracks shared base weights or training data without generating text.
D2AfBRZ01K.evidence: Calibration on 32 open-weight models with documented relationships, lineage retrieval on five DeepSeek-R1 distillations and 16 parent-child pairs, comparison with PhyloLM and LLM DNA, and replication on three independent probe suites.
D2AfBRZ01K.claimed_gains: Similarity is 0.67 for instruction-tuned models against their base, 0.48 for identical-data models without shared weights, 0.39 for reasoning distillations against their documented base and 0.22 for unrelated models; the documented base ranks in the top two for all five DeepSeek-R1 distillations and for 88% of 16 parent-child pairs, and on identical models TokenPrint scores 5/5 in the top two versus 2/5 for PhyloLM and 0/5 for LLM DNA.
D2AfBRZ01K.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the training-free fingerprint addresses an increasingly important provenance question, and that the shared-data experiments, where similarity appears before task competence, are a main contribution.
D2AfBRZ01K.main_concern: Comparison with prior fingerprinting methods such as PhyloLM and LLM DNA is judged thin, evidence for stability under quantization is limited, and the method section is unclear.

TQsYTmdtjC.one_liner: Two-stage RL: a Priming policy inserts bridging triples as verifiable evidence, then a Reasoning stage answers from the original input.
TQsYTmdtjC.problem: End-to-end methods entangle knowledge elicitation with reasoning, so it is hard to tell whether correct factual answers come from parametric knowledge or from the input context.
TQsYTmdtjC.method: Given a query and an insufficient retrieved subgraph, the Priming policy inserts bridging triples, rewarded by answers that a separate frozen model generates over the augmented subgraph. The Reasoning stage then trains the model to answer from the original input to test whether the elicitation capability transfers to implicit reasoning.
TQsYTmdtjC.key_idea: Externalize latent knowledge as inserted bridging triples rewarded through a frozen answerer, then train the model to answer from the original input so elicitation transfers to implicit reasoning.
TQsYTmdtjC.evidence: Seven benchmarks and two backbone families (Qwen2.5-7B and Qwen3-8B per reviews), compared with inference-time methods (Self-Ask, RECITE, Unlock) and GRPO, plus analysis of how many inserted triples are attributed to model parameters.
TQsYTmdtjC.claimed_gains: VAKE achieves the best average performance on both the in-distribution multi-hop and OOD benchmark groups, outperforming inference-time methods and GRPO; no numbers are stated in the visible abstract.
TQsYTmdtjC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that helping LLMs access knowledge they already hold is a meaningful question and that separating elicitation from reasoning with a frozen answerer makes the contribution inspectable.
