TQsYTmdtjC.main_concern: The evidence is confounded: stage 2 is extra GRPO training that may explain the gains, inserted triples need not reflect true parametric knowledge, and the setup still depends on retrieved subgraphs and Qwen backbones.

inoCYu42TC.one_liner: Latent-attention PDE surrogate whose routing queries are synthesized from the input by FLARE's encoder, keeping linear O(NM) cost.
inoCYu42TC.problem: Latent-space attention methods such as PerceiverIO, Transolver and FLARE compress tokens with learned templates that are the same for every input.
inoCYu42TC.method: FLARE++ uses FLARE's own encoder to map the N input tokens to M query tokens that correct the learned queries, and the adapted queries determine how the same input is compressed and redistributed. It preserves the explicit low-rank factorization and linear O(NM) complexity, uses only standard SDPA calls, and adds a multi-GPU context-parallel implementation.
inoCYu42TC.key_idea: Correct FLARE's learned latent queries with input-synthesized queries produced by its own encoder, so the compression template adapts to each input.
inoCYu42TC.evidence: Five standard PDE benchmarks, industrial-scale DrivAerML and Long Range Arena, with depth and latent-budget sweeps and ten-seed runs on Elasticity, as described in the abstract and reviews.
inoCYu42TC.claimed_gains: FLARE++ reduces FLARE's error by 25% on average across five standard PDE benchmarks, achieving the lowest errors among the efficient models compared.
inoCYu42TC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree FLARE++ gives consistent, well-controlled improvements over FLARE across PDE benchmarks and DrivAerML, is simple to implement, and has a practical multi-GPU implementation.
inoCYu42TC.main_concern: Comparisons are not controlled for the 14-23% extra parameters and added compute, ablations do not isolate components such as the gate and normalization, and novelty over latent query refinement is limited.

ryqdH3sHmj.one_liner: Robust Ensemble Guidance weights ensemble corrections by predictive spread and clips standardized residuals for diffusion-based scientific inverse problems.
ryqdH3sHmj.problem: In ensemble guidance with black-box forward models, observation coordinates with large predictive spread or extreme residuals can dominate the ensemble correction and degrade reconstruction accuracy.
ryqdH3sHmj.method: REG uses ensemble predictive spread to balance observation scales and adaptively clips standardized residuals to limit extreme discrepancies, reusing existing particles and forward predictions with no extra denoiser or forward-model evaluations. Under a local linear Gaussian model, the paper derives conditions for reduced one-step estimation risk and bounds the influence of individual observation coordinates.
ryqdH3sHmj.key_idea: Rescale each observation coordinate by ensemble predictive spread and clip its standardized residual, so no single coordinate dominates the ensemble guidance step.
ryqdH3sHmj.evidence: Navier–Stokes inversion, black-hole imaging and acoustic full-waveform inversion, plus a local linear Gaussian analysis; one review notes the Navier–Stokes gain varies with ensemble size.
ryqdH3sHmj.claimed_gains: REG increases black-hole reconstruction PSNR by 6.2–8.2 dB across three observation regimes and reduces Navier–Stokes reconstruction error by 26.4% in a matched-budget comparison.
ryqdH3sHmj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is simple, adds no extra evaluations, is easy to add to existing ensemble guidance, and is effective across several scientific inverse problems.
ryqdH3sHmj.main_concern: Novelty is seen as incremental, since the weighting and clipping resemble standard robust-statistics and normalization techniques, and the local linear theory is only loosely tied to the nonlinear iterative algorithm.

sDtxHvhGWe.one_liner: Calibrates a frozen neural PDE surrogate with sparse measurements via a recursive block residual update, without backpropagation.
sDtxHvhGWe.problem: Simulation-trained neural PDE surrogates degrade when deployed on measured physical streams or shifted target dynamics.
sDtxHvhGWe.method: BROC maintains a spatially shared residual map, updated recursively per forecast block from matured sparse measurements, coupling prediction steps and physical components without gradient steps or parameter updates. The authors prove exact optimality of the recursive update, strict temporal non-anticipation, and a finite-sample certificate for full-field improvement.
sDtxHvhGWe.key_idea: A spatially shared residual map is updated by a recursive block (ridge-style) solve from matured sparse measurements, replacing gradient-based test-time adaptation of surrogate weights.
sDtxHvhGWe.evidence: 20 system-surrogate-checkpoint cells in RealPDEBench and 12 PDEBench cells under controlled physical-parameter shifts, against a frozen surrogate and recent adaptation baselines, plus the stated theorems.
sDtxHvhGWe.claimed_gains: Best accuracy in all 20 RealPDEBench cells with MSE reduced by 32.56% versus Frozen and 23.84%-29.84% over adaptation baselines; on 12 PDEBench cells it removes 38.31%-80.47% of Frozen error; the calibration core runs in 5.317 ms on RealPDEBench and 4.458 ms on PDEBench.
sDtxHvhGWe.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit the clean evaluation protocol (separate development and evaluation trajectories, predict before update), the broad baselines and measured-system results, and the simple, fast corrector.
sDtxHvhGWe.main_concern: BROC is not clearly distinguished from classical exponentially weighted ridge regression / RLS, and the RLS comparison lacks matched features, regularization and observation sequence.

EL8KM5aBIc.one_liner: Speeds up one-step video super-resolution with local-plus-sparse-global attention and reward-weighted teacher rollouts for distribution matching distillation.
EL8KM5aBIc.problem: Distilled one-step VSR models remain costly at high resolution and are hard to align with human preferences.
EL8KM5aBIc.method: Hybrid attention exploits locality observed in pretrained VSR models while keeping sparse global interaction for long-range consistency. Ry-DMD adds black-box rewards to distribution matching distillation through reward-weighted teacher rollouts, without backpropagating through the reward model.
EL8KM5aBIc.key_idea: Reward-weighted teacher rollouts shift the DMD teacher term toward high-reward outputs, so non-differentiable rewards enter distillation without reward-model gradients.
EL8KM5aBIc.evidence: Latency and memory measurements at 2K/4K on an RTX 4090 and a second hardware platform, restoration metrics including DOVER, OCR-reward training on synthetic text VSR, a 20-videos-per-pair preference comparison, and a T2I extension on SDXL and SD3.5-M.
EL8KM5aBIc.claimed_gains: Up to 2x DiT speedup and 45% lower peak memory, enabling spatially untiled 4K VSR on a single 24GB RTX 4090.
EL8KM5aBIc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree hybrid attention gives large latency and memory savings with small quality loss, and that Ry-DMD is a simple route to non-differentiable rewards, backed by OCR and T2I results.
EL8KM5aBIc.main_concern: Preference and reward gains are weakly isolated: only 20 videos per pair with unclear rater counts, and Ry-DMD is tested mainly with a synthetic-text OCR reward.

nnVUaabR27.one_liner: Distills a compact vision encoder to directly predict spatio-temporally compressed teacher tokens, cutting Video LLM encoding latency.
nnVUaabR27.problem: After post-hoc token reduction, per-frame vision-encoder processing becomes the latency bottleneck for long-form Video LLMs.
nnVUaabR27.method: LiteFrame is a lightweight video encoder trained with Compressed Token Distillation (CTD), in which a compact student predicts the information-dense compressed representations of a large teacher vision model, followed by Language Model Adaptation (LMA).
nnVUaabR27.key_idea: A small student encoder is trained to output the teacher's already spatio-temporally compressed tokens directly, skipping redundant per-frame full-resolution encoding.
nnVUaabR27.evidence: Video benchmarks with ablations, compared against post-hoc token compression methods (ToMe, PruMerge, FastVID) and efficient encoders, with InternVL3-8B as the reference model.
nnVUaabR27.claimed_gains: 35% lower end-to-end latency than InternVL3-8B while processing 8x more frames and improving average video understanding accuracy across multiple benchmarks.
nnVUaabR27.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the vision-encoder bottleneck is well motivated, the framework is simple and effective, and experiments show efficiency gains with supporting ablations.
nnVUaabR27.main_concern: Recent in-encoder token compression methods are missing from the comparison, novelty is limited (compressed feature distillation), and evaluation is confined to video benchmarks and the InternVL family.

utXuOW0dBw.one_liner: Fine-tuning-free low-rank PTQ that permutes columns by importance and applies block-wise Walsh-Hadamard rotation to the residual.
utXuOW0dBw.problem: Weight-only PTQ at 2-3 bits often needs fine-tuning, and applying a full Hadamard rotation after low-rank decomposition degrades residual quantization.
utXuOW0dBw.method: LoPRo ranks and permutes residual columns by importance, protects key columns, and rotates the remaining ones block-wise with Walsh-Hadamard transforms. It also uses R1SVD, a mixed-precision fast low-rank decomposition based on rank-1 sketching, to cut quantization cost.
utXuOW0dBw.key_idea: Importance-based column permutation lets blocks of similar-importance columns share a partial Walsh-Hadamard rotation, instead of rotating the whole low-rank residual globally.
utXuOW0dBw.evidence: Dense and MoE LLMs with scalar and vector quantization at 2 and 3 bits, compared with fine-tuning-free PTQ, GPTVQ, MoEQuant++ and other low-rank methods, plus a proxy-loss analysis.
utXuOW0dBw.claimed_gains: Up to 5x quantization speedup over GPTVQ; on Mixtral-8x7B quantization finishes in under 2.5 hours, reducing perplexity by 0.75 over MoEQuant++ (3.17 vs. 3.00 avg. bits) and boosting BoolQ accuracy by 5.4 points, with latency overhead of at most 10.3% at batch 1.
utXuOW0dBw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the conflict between low-rank residuals and global rotation is a useful finding, the permutation plus partial rotation design works for scalar and vector quantization, and R1SVD gives practical speed gains.
utXuOW0dBw.main_concern: The theory relies on a diagonal Hessian proxy and an incoherence assumption (A3) not verified on real LLM residuals, and ablations do not separate column ordering from partial rotation.

vuh798aNjV.one_liner: Reranks RAG documents by Shapley-style contributions to evidence-set utility, with an amortized single-pass estimator for speed.
vuh798aNjV.problem: Point-wise relevance misses a document's complementary or redundant role within the set that jointly supports an answer.
vuh798aNjV.method: A valuer is trained with a set-contrastive objective on local set-utility comparisons; at inference, regression over small coalitions sampled from a truncated KernelSHAP-inspired distribution gives document contributions, and coalition utilities supervise an amortized single-pass estimator (SHAPRank-A).
vuh798aNjV.key_idea: Document scores are regression-based Shapley-style attributions over small sampled coalitions of a learned set-utility model, and coalition utilities then supervise a single-pass scorer.
vuh798aNjV.evidence: Five multi-hop QA benchmarks with controlled ablations (set-wise training, attribution, coalition supervision) against point-wise, list-wise and set-wise rerankers, using Qwen3-Reranker-0.6B as the backbone.
vuh798aNjV.claimed_gains: Improves average reranking recall and downstream answer quality over strong baselines (no numbers given), and the amortized variant keeps latency comparable to standard neural rerankers with a 7.2x speedup over sampling-based attribution.
vuh798aNjV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the cooperative-game framing principled and the matched controls and amortized estimator convincing, with cross-dataset gains and much lower latency than sampling-based attribution.
vuh798aNjV.main_concern: It is unclear whether gains come from modeling complementarity and redundancy or from the Shapley-inspired weighting, and scalability evidence is limited (about 30 candidates, coalitions of at most four, one reranker backbone).

1cYh01go7K.one_liner: Trains AI-generated image detectors by regressing real-fake mixing ratios, then selects a compact source-response subspace for the classifier.
1cYh01go7K.problem: Binary-classification training of AI-generated image detectors overfits to shortcut cues and generalizes poorly across generators.
1cYh01go7K.method: CuRe adapts the backbone by regressing the mixing ratio of real and generated images (pixel-space interpolation), then selects a compact subspace of the learned source responses so the final classifier has limited access to shortcut cues.
1cYh01go7K.key_idea: Replace binary endpoint labels with continuous real-generated mixing-ratio regression during backbone adaptation, then restrict the classifier to a selected source-response subspace.
1cYh01go7K.evidence: Ten public benchmarks, experiments across visual backbones and under common image degradations; reviewers cite a matched LoRA protocol with repeated seeds across four backbones.
1cYh01go7K.claimed_gains: Average balanced accuracy of 89.7% across ten public benchmarks, exceeding the second-best method by 5.2%.
1cYh01go7K.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the ratio-regression reformulation is a sensible alternative to binary supervision and that evaluation across ten benchmarks, backbones and degradations shows consistent generalization.
1cYh01go7K.main_concern: Comparisons are confounded by backbone (CuRe uses PE Core L/14, which alone performs much better), and it is unclear that mixing-ratio supervision rather than simpler shortcut mitigation or blend detection drives the gain.

seDgcBTV76.one_liner: Two-stage one-step generator: fixed-noise reconstruction pretraining, then feature-space distributional post-training.
seDgcBTV76.problem: Training one-step generators with distributional objectives from scratch is difficult, and existing approaches rely on complex training machinery.
seDgcBTV76.method: Priming Models are first trained on a reconstruction objective such as pixel-space denoising at a fixed noise level, then post-trained with feature-space distributional losses. The paper reports that the reconstruction stage alone removes the difficulty of distributional training.
seDgcBTV76.key_idea: A single fixed-noise denoising stage gives a one-step generator an initialization from which feature-space distribution matching trains efficiently.
seDgcBTV76.evidence: Class-conditional image generation, text-to-image generation and world modeling, with ablations over corruption levels, reconstruction tasks and distributional objectives, plus ImageNet 256x256 evaluation.
seDgcBTV76.claimed_gains: FID of 1.25 among one-step generators on ImageNet at 256x256 resolution, using approximately one-tenth the training compute of prior methods with comparable FID.
seDgcBTV76.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the single-noise reconstruction initialization is a simple, well-supported principle, backed by ablations across tasks and losses and strong compute-efficiency results.
seDgcBTV76.main_concern: Stage 2 overlaps substantially with W-Flow's Sinkhorn-based distributional training, and the framing overclaims novelty for a combination of existing pretraining, OT and perceptual-loss components.

FEqJ91D8ql.one_liner: Repurposes an LLM to predict 4D human motion, activity and interacted objects from a few wearable IMUs.
FEqJ91D8ql.problem: Human-object activity understanding relies on cameras, which pose privacy, safety, energy and scalability challenges.
FEqJ91D8ql.method: IMU4D repurposes a large language model for non-visual spatiotemporal understanding: from a few inertial sensors in earbuds, watches or smartphones it predicts detailed 4D human motion together with the objects the person interacts with, sharing representations across tasks.
FEqJ91D8ql.key_idea: An LLM maps sparse IMU signals into shared representations that jointly decode full-body motion, activity descriptions and interacted objects.
FEqJ91D8ql.evidence: Diverse human motion and human-object datasets compared with cascaded pipelines, real-IMU evaluation (DIP-IMU and a small IMU4D-Real set with 2 participants), and joint-training ablations.
FEqJ91D8ql.claimed_gains: More coherent and temporally stable results than cascaded pipelines; no quantitative numbers in the abstract.
FEqJ91D8ql.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the camera-free, privacy-friendly setting interesting and the IMU-to-motion results on real IMU data convincing.
FEqJ91D8ql.main_concern: Object recovery is weakly supported (a fixed set of known objects per dataset, fine-tuned per dataset) and real-world evaluation is thin: two participants, pseudo ground truth, unclear sensor calibration, and possible HumanML3D train-test overlap.

ejuhxQdPTJ.one_liner: Derives closed-form guided flows for classifier-free guidance on a Gaussian-mixture conditional with a single-Gaussian unconditional.
ejuhxQdPTJ.problem: Classifier-free guidance is empirically and theoretically poorly understood because transport equations for arbitrary flows are hard to solve.
ejuhxQdPTJ.method: The conditional distribution is modeled as a Gaussian mixture with means on an ellipsoid and the unconditional as one Gaussian; the resulting flows are closed under scaling, giving analytic solutions for the guided distribution at all noise scales and guidance levels.
ejuhxQdPTJ.key_idea: A capacity mismatch between conditional (mixture) and unconditional (single Gaussian) distributions yields a mean-axis shift and a persistent skew toward a singular point of the conditional sample.
ejuhxQdPTJ.evidence: Analytic derivations (e.g., Theorems 3.4 and 3.7) checked against empirical predictions; the abstract is cut off before the validation details.
ejuhxQdPTJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the analytic model clean and fresh, with closed-form results (notably Theorem 3.4) that match empirical evidence.
ejuhxQdPTJ.main_concern: The setting is restrictive (shared covariance, closed form only in limited cases such as 1-D), so it is unclear that it explains mode collapse in practice.

QvbJZhSLIi.one_liner: Benchmark of 590 biological cases testing how LLM perturbation predictions depend on the cross-scale evidence provided.
QvbJZhSLIi.problem: Evaluating foundation models for cellular perturbation reasoning requires knowing how predictions depend on the biological evidence provided, not only whether they are correct.
QvbJZhSLIi.method: CellChain links perturbation experiments and external resources through a provenance-aware evidence graph spanning molecular, pathway, transcriptional and phenotypic information, and varies evidence coverage, composition or assignment while fixing questions, candidates and scoring.
QvbJZhSLIi.key_idea: Matched evidence-condition instances hold the question, candidate answers and scoring fixed while varying only the evidence, isolating evidence dependence.
QvbJZhSLIi.evidence: 590 cases and 2,360 matched evidence-condition instances over gene-dependency prediction, cytokine-axis identification and drug-sensitivity ranking, evaluated on 18 foundation models.
QvbJZhSLIi.claimed_gains: Highest accuracies under prespecified target-evidence conditions are 57.5%, 75.5% and 70.8% across the three tasks, and broader evidence coverage does not consistently improve accuracy.
QvbJZhSLIi.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit the paired, controlled design that holds tasks fixed while varying evidence, with provenance preserved and behavior changes hidden by accuracy exposed.
QvbJZhSLIi.main_concern: The diagnostic value is unclear: no model beats a simple mean-history baseline on Drug, and controls are missing to show how much predictions depend on measured cellular responses versus annotations.

xqKOk0O2Ra.one_liner: Benchmark of 132 business-logic vulnerabilities, anonymized and oracle-instrumented, testing whether agents discover or memorize.
xqKOk0O2Ra.problem: Synthetic vulnerability benchmarks lack realism, real-life ones are prone to contamination, and many existing ones are already saturated.
xqKOk0O2Ra.method: A semi-automated pipeline anonymizes each real application task, injects oracles from expert-written specifications, and differentially verifies proof-of-concept exploits, with black-box and grey-box tracks across nine languages.
xqKOk0O2Ra.key_idea: Semantics-preserving anonymization plus embedded semantic oracles at key exploitation steps separate genuine discovery from reliance on historical vulnerability identity.
xqKOk0O2Ra.evidence: Six vulnerability-discovery agents evaluated on 132 tasks in nine languages, measuring discovery success, cost-effectiveness and anonymization sensitivity.
xqKOk0O2Ra.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the benchmark targets an important evaluation gap, with careful construction, executable tasks and matched black-box and grey-box access.
xqKOk0O2Ra.main_concern: The anonymization experiment does not cleanly separate discovery from memorization, since anonymization also changes routes, names and runtime information that affect search difficulty.

3Ilori3mo8.one_liner: GPU-parallel Isaac Lab benchmark for 40 manipulation tasks plus demonstration-guided PPO with progress-adaptive behavior cloning and task weighting.
3Ilori3mo8.problem: Existing GPU-parallel benchmarks rarely combine large-scale simulation with heterogeneous manipulation tasks and standardized multi-task RL evaluation.
3Ilori3mo8.method: Hebero trains and evaluates a single policy on 40 heterogeneous tasks. DGPO reuses demonstrations for dense tracking rewards and asymmetric value learning, and IW-ABC uses a per-task learning-progress signal to relax adaptive behavior cloning and upweight lagging tasks in PPO.
3Ilori3mo8.key_idea: A lightweight per-task learning-progress signal anneals behavior-cloning guidance (ABC) and importance-weights lagging tasks (IW) in PPO updates.
3Ilori3mo8.evidence: 40 tasks (LIBERO suites ported to Isaac Lab) with 50 demonstrations per task, comparison against baselines including FAMO-ABC, scaling over parallel replicas, and sim-to-real transfer to four physical robot tasks.
3Ilori3mo8.claimed_gains: With 50 demonstrations per task, IW-ABC achieves 90.1% state-input mean success, outperforming the strongest baseline FAMO-ABC by 7.8 percentage points, and its visual counterpart reaches 93.5% mean success.
3Ilori3mo8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree Hebero is useful, standardized infrastructure and that IW-ABC improves on the evaluated baselines, with a real-robot deployment.
3Ilori3mo8.main_concern: IW-ABC looks like an incremental combination of task weighting and adaptive imitation, and its margin over FAMO-ABC is hard to attribute because FAMO-ABC weights only the critic and few seeds are used.

KtoceE7tyD.one_liner: Benchmark adding an 'ask' action to streaming video understanding, testing when and what models should ask under uncertainty.
KtoceE7tyD.problem: Proactive streaming-video paradigms only wait or answer, so incomplete video or user information makes models wait forever or hallucinate.
KtoceE7tyD.method: AskStream is a multi-turn benchmark of 438 videos with 2,714 manually annotated frame-level time windows labeled wait, ask or answer, across four task categories and eight subtasks, scored with an Ask-F1 metric.
KtoceE7tyD.key_idea: Frame-level wait/ask/answer time windows covering video and user uncertainty let the benchmark score both when to ask and what to ask.
KtoceE7tyD.evidence: Multiple-choice and open-ended evaluations of closed-source, open-source and streaming proactive models, with an oracle ablation.
KtoceE7tyD.claimed_gains: Even the strongest model attains only 52.18% on the proposed Ask-F1 metric.
KtoceE7tyD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the ask-before-answer formulation is meaningful and underexplored, and that the benchmark is carefully built with manual time-window annotation and broad model evaluation.
KtoceE7tyD.main_concern: The conclusion that asking is the bottleneck may reflect the strict timing constraint in the ask score rather than model ability, and the benchmark lacks no-ask cases and text-only baselines.

PXBOsYM7YY.one_liner: Benchmark of 85 repository-grounded tasks testing whether LLMs can engineer and optimize LLM training and inference infrastructure.
PXBOsYM7YY.problem: Existing benchmarks cover isolated kernels, predefined operators or pre-specified targets, and cannot evaluate open-ended, long-horizon infrastructure engineering.
PXBOsYM7YY.method: Builds 85 executable tasks in nine infrastructure categories and three formats, from kernel completion to repository-wide optimization, from real pull requests, issues and code, with rewards gated by correctness and anti-hacking checks.
PXBOsYM7YY.key_idea: Tasks derived from real PRs and repositories are validated bidirectionally and rewarded by gated correctness plus performance, leaving bottleneck identification to the agent.
PXBOsYM7YY.evidence: Eight frontier models evaluated on the 85 tasks, with trajectory analysis of how stronger models run controlled experiments.
PXBOsYM7YY.claimed_gains: The strongest model, Claude Opus 5, scores only 36.53%.
PXBOsYM7YY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the target is well chosen and goes beyond kernel-level benchmarks, with tasks from real repositories and validated tests.
PXBOsYM7YY.main_concern: The score mixes task completion with reference-beating speedups (reward is zero at parity with the reference), so 36.53% is not a success rate and format-level comparisons are hard to interpret.

CaY2m86vEL.one_liner: CLIP visual reprogramming with one visual prompt and residual inter-class correction that folds into a linear classifier.
CaY2m86vEL.problem: Existing visual reprogramming aggregates prompts within each class independently and ignores correlated, overlapping class descriptions that leave cross-class ambiguity.
CaY2m86vEL.method: RVP aggregates multiple text prompts per class and applies residual correction across classes, built on a view of CLIP reprogramming with linear output aggregation as a linear map from frozen image embeddings to logits; it reparameterizes into a frozen backbone plus a linear classifier at inference.
CaY2m86vEL.key_idea: A learned inter-class residual matrix over text-derived class responses corrects cross-class ambiguity and folds exactly into a linear head at inference.
CaY2m86vEL.evidence: 11 few-shot classification benchmarks and four CLIP backbones, with ablations of the inter-class module and a supporting theoretical analysis.
CaY2m86vEL.claimed_gains: Consistently improves over prior visual reprogramming methods across 11 few-shot benchmarks and four CLIP backbones with comparable or better inference efficiency and nearly zero computational overhead.
CaY2m86vEL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the cross-class ambiguity problem is meaningful, results are extensive across datasets and backbones, and the exact inference folding gives a credible efficiency advantage.
CaY2m86vEL.main_concern: Novelty is limited relative to residual-classifier and logit-correction ideas, and evidence that the inter-class matrix works by suppressing shared semantics is weaker than claimed.

xyIDJGaPB5.one_liner: Learns a task-aligned scaffolding encoder for latent visual targets and a variance-learning RL sampler for multimodal latent reasoning.
xyIDJGaPB5.problem: In latent visual reasoning, the SFT stage encodes helper images with an off-the-shelf encoder that may not suit the task, and the RL stage regularizes deterministically without exploring alternative latent trajectories.
xyIDJGaPB5.method: A dedicated scaffolding encoder, trained with the task loss, provides optimized targets for the latent tokens in SFT, and the RL stage learns both the mean and variance of the latent sampler to enable stochastic exploration.
xyIDJGaPB5.key_idea: Train the helper-image encoder with the answer loss to get task-aligned latent targets, and learn the sampler's mean and variance so RL can explore latent trajectories.
xyIDJGaPB5.evidence: FrozenLake spatial planning (including 32x32 grids) and nine visual-centric benchmarks, with target-representation ablations on a single model and a controlled Zebra-CoT comparison.
xyIDJGaPB5.claimed_gains: Improves over the strongest latent-reasoning baseline by +9.5 points on FrozenLake spatial planning, widening to +19 points on 32x32 grids, and by +5.6 points on average on the visual benchmarks.
xyIDJGaPB5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that learning a reasoning-oriented target encoder is sensible, and that controlled FrozenLake ablations show the gains do not come from the RL stage alone.
xyIDJGaPB5.main_concern: Experiments cover a single model and rely on helper images, and gains on real visual benchmarks are less controlled (mixed baseline sources, no multi-seed error bars) with Monet already learning helper-conditioned targets.

Zr8MSV01KG.one_liner: On-policy dual-teacher distillation: a video teacher and a multi-view teacher jointly supervise a few-step multi-view video generator.
Zr8MSV01KG.problem: Synchronized multi-view video training data is scarce, and separate monocular-video and static multi-view supervision, or depth-based geometry guidance, compromises cross-view consistency.
Zr8MSV01KG.method: MultiLive distills a student generator from a video teacher (motion within each view) and a multi-view teacher (geometry and appearance across views), applying both distribution-matching objectives to the same student-generated sample, with 4 denoising steps at inference and no explicit 3D reconstruction.
Zr8MSV01KG.key_idea: Both teachers' distribution-matching losses update the student on the same on-policy generated sample, keeping temporal and multi-view capabilities compatible.
Zr8MSV01KG.evidence: Comparisons with mixed-data SFT, single-teacher distillation and sequential distillation, plus ablations of the main design choices.
Zr8MSV01KG.claimed_gains: High visual quality, strong cross-view consistency and coherent temporal dynamics without multi-view video training data, using only 4 denoising steps at inference; no other numbers stated.
Zr8MSV01KG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the dual-teacher on-policy design is simple and well motivated, makes use of separately available supervision, and is supported by comparisons and ablations.
Zr8MSV01KG.main_concern: The multi-view teacher may be out of distribution for moving content and the evaluation omits a direct motion metric (e.g., VBench dynamic degree), so consistency gains could reflect reduced motion.

MWwGSaKNXE.one_liner: Encodes reasoning steps from text, image, 3D and robot-state modalities into shared latent thoughts generated by a diffusion reasoner.
MWwGSaKNXE.problem: Each modality is encoded in its own space, so every modality switch in multimodal reasoning pays a modality-switching gap of translating between formats.
MWwGSaKNXE.method: A unified encoder maps teacher reasoning steps from different modalities into latent thought tokens in a shared space, trained to preserve the information needed for later steps and the final output; a jointly trained diffusion reasoner generates these tokens at inference without teacher observations.
MWwGSaKNXE.key_idea: A shared latent space trained by continuation prediction holds reasoning steps of any modality, and a jointly trained diffusion model generates them.
MWwGSaKNXE.evidence: Eleven VLM benchmarks and two VLA suites across four backbones, with ablations (unified vs separate encoding, reconstruction vs continuation objectives) and a latent-intervention study.
MWwGSaKNXE.claimed_gains: Relative gains over the strongest baselines of 7.3% on four mathematical and logical VLM benchmarks and 6.1% on RLBench manipulation tasks.
MWwGSaKNXE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the unified latent formulation is well motivated and general across VLM and VLA settings, with extensive experiments and ablations.
MWwGSaKNXE.main_concern: Gains from unification vary by dataset (no gain on MathVista and EMMA) and baselines use different data and recipes, with no matched same-data fine-tuning control.

awUpfbYXXb.one_liner: Shows sigmoid contrastive (SigLIP) logits estimate pointwise mutual information, and uses this for synthetic-trained multimodal medical image registration.
awUpfbYXXb.problem: Histogram-based MI similarity measures and learned representations for multimodal registration are not connected, so the link between representation learning and mutual information is lost in registration.
awUpfbYXXb.method: Shows that the optimal logits of a sigmoid contrastive model recover pointwise mutual information up to a class-prior correction, then trains fully convolutional SigMI models on domain-randomized synthetic images from five brain segmentation maps, whose dense feature dot products estimate local PMI.
awUpfbYXXb.key_idea: Optimal logits of a classifier separating joint pairs from deranged pairs equal PMI minus a log class-prior term, so correcting for the prior gives calibrated PMI.
awUpfbYXXb.evidence: Registration across three algorithms and four datasets, plus calibration against ground-truth PMI and an excess-classification-risk analysis of estimation error.
awUpfbYXXb.claimed_gains: Two SigMI variants each win in 6 of 12 settings, together in 8.
awUpfbYXXb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the PMI reinterpretation of SigLIP is clear and correct, with practical implications and transfer from synthetic training to other anatomies, modalities and solvers.
awUpfbYXXb.main_concern: The theoretical contribution is a special case of DEMI and other prior logit-equals-PMI results, and registration evidence is weak (small test sets, no significance tests, wins combined across two variants).

Bk9w4hEw98.one_liner: Point-prompted 3D part decomposition that jointly assigns every shape position to exactly one part via a coarse-to-fine part decoder.
Bk9w4hEw98.problem: Existing 3D part decomposition methods produce overlapping or gappy parts instead of a non-overlapping, exhaustive partition of the whole shape.
Bk9w4hEw98.method: Built on a pretrained 3D generation model, a prompt encoder maps each 3D point prompt to a part token that attends to the shape latent, and a part decoder scores the whole shape against all part tokens coarse-to-fine, assigning each volume position to one part. One model covers image-to-part, mesh-to-part and part segmentation.
Bk9w4hEw98.key_idea: Score all part tokens jointly against the shape volume and assign each position by argmax, so parts are non-overlapping and exhaustive by construction.
Bk9w4hEw98.evidence: Part generation and segmentation evaluations with ablations and cross-dataset tests, including PartNeXt segmentation.
Bk9w4hEw98.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree joint partitioning is a well-motivated way to avoid inter-part overlap, with strong segmentation results, much lower penetration, and supporting ablations.
Bk9w4hEw98.main_concern: Methodological novelty is limited: the joint prompt segmentation resembles the uncited Instruct-Particulate and exhaustiveness follows from argmax, while whole-shape geometry quality and part interfaces are weaker.

eQPQhpHuhk.one_liner: Proves matching upper and lower bounds on feedback rounds for recovering an MDP transition kernel from singleton-avoidance critic libraries.
eQPQhpHuhk.problem: Any n-1 critics identify the transition kernel exactly, but under noise it is unclear how many adaptive feedback rounds are needed to match the full critic library's recovery and execution rates.
eQPQhpHuhk.method: A blockwise residual rule for arbitrary finite action sets uses n-1 queries in at most ceil((n-2)/(b-1)) rounds, and a hidden-core lower bound shows at least ceil((n-1)/b) rounds are necessary, where b = ceil(1/kappa) for a row-diameter bound kappa.
eQPQhpHuhk.key_idea: Batching critic queries in blocks acquires the n-1 critics in fewer rounds, and the final redundant critic removes the adaptive bottleneck, buying parallelism rather than identifiability.
eQPQhpHuhk.evidence: Theorems with matching upper and lower bounds for the stated query model; reviewers note the absence of experiments on larger or benchmark RL environments.
eQPQhpHuhk.claimed_gains: Without a per-round cap, depth is Theta(1 + n*kappa) for n-1 critics and one round for all n; with at most W critics per round, the minimum identifying depth is Theta(1 + n*max{kappa, 1/W}).
eQPQhpHuhk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the matched upper and lower bounds and the distinction between exact and noise-robust identifiability, which go beyond showing the kernel is recoverable.
eQPQhpHuhk.main_concern: Presentation lacks motivation and context, and the setup (full singleton-avoidance critic columns, query budget capped at n-1, global overlap assumption) may be too specific to bear on real RL.

bcgS8yBMmD.one_liner: Test-time cooperative self-play co-evolves code solutions and self-generated unit tests, using Code-UT pass counts to weigh each side.
bcgS8yBMmD.problem: Ground-truth unit tests are expensive, and self-generated tests and codes are both noisy, so treating either as ground truth propagates errors.
bcgS8yBMmD.method: CoSPlay derives discriminative unit-test ideas from failure modes of diverse solution ideas, then alternately updates the code and test pools, keeping items with higher support counts on the Code-UT execution matrix and using them to fix or regenerate the rest, followed by a final selection stage.
bcgS8yBMmD.key_idea: Pass counts on the code-by-unit-test execution matrix correlate with correctness, so each pool filters and repairs the other without any ground-truth reference.
bcgS8yBMmD.evidence: A theoretical argument and empirical check that pass counts correlate positively with correctness, plus experiments on four code benchmarks with Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and CURE-7B.
bcgS8yBMmD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that improving test quality jointly with code at inference time, without ground-truth tests, is a well-motivated problem and that the empirical study is thorough.
bcgS8yBMmD.main_concern: The theory assumes independent sampling while the procedure couples codes and tests, cost is high (about 682K generated tokens and 776 model calls per problem), and the approach resembles UTGen.

pvCdVEkCYL.one_liner: Accelerates 3D Gaussian Splatting with frequency-aware importance masks, localized densification and pruning, and learnable per-Gaussian scale modulation.
pvCdVEkCYL.problem: General-purpose 3DGS acceleration methods lose rendering quality on complex, large-scale scenes.
pvCdVEkCYL.method: Importance is scored by combining pixel-wise reconstruction error with a scheduled difference-of-Gaussians mask; densification and pruning are restricted to Gaussians with valid projected footprints in sampled views; and learnable per-Gaussian scale modulation adjusts primitive extent while keeping the Compact Box rasterization rule.
pvCdVEkCYL.key_idea: Stage-dependent frequency-aware importance scoring guides active-set-restricted densification and pruning, with a learnable per-Gaussian scale factor adjusting effective primitive extent.
pvCdVEkCYL.evidence: Bounded and large-scale scene datasets (including Mill-19), component ablations and matched-primitive-budget comparisons against FastGS and other methods.
pvCdVEkCYL.claimed_gains: Reconstruction quality comparable to or better than vanilla 3DGS with a favorable balance of quality, training time and primitive count; no numbers in the abstract.
pvCdVEkCYL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree EffGS addresses a practical limitation and improves reconstruction quality over FastGS, especially on large-scale scenes, with evaluation across multiple datasets and ablations.
pvCdVEkCYL.main_concern: The distinction from FreGS, FDS-GS and other frequency or scale-based 3DGS work is insufficiently established, and coupled components mean ablations do not isolate each contribution.

ecmL77OzWO.one_liner: Benchmark of 101 text-to-Simulink tasks scored by native simulation and a hierarchical engineering-qualification evaluator.
ecmL77OzWO.problem: Existing Simulink benchmarks check only whether generated models compile, run or resemble a reference, not whether they meet engineering requirements.
ecmL77OzWO.method: SimuVerity provides 101 tasks across ten engineering domains with executable-system profiles and four families of native simulation scenarios. A hierarchical evaluator checks artifact delivery, native executability and engineering qualification, then scores six dimensions.
ecmL77OzWO.key_idea: Native simulation scenarios plus a qualification gate and six-dimension scoring measure engineering requirements directly instead of structural similarity to a reference model.
ecmL77OzWO.evidence: Six agent systems evaluated on the 101 tasks, with root-cause failure analysis, expert validation of the evaluator, and a comparison with graduate students on hard tasks.
ecmL77OzWO.claimed_gains: The best of six evaluated agent systems achieves an overall score of only 42.86.
ecmL77OzWO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the benchmark fills a clear gap, with an evaluator and scenario design that separate engineering quality from structural similarity, supported by expert validation.
ecmL77OzWO.main_concern: Analysis of why models fail is shallow for an ML venue, and evaluator validity is lightly tested (expert validation covers only 30 candidates from one run of one agent).

gYkRVCORE6.one_liner: Frequency-guided Gaussian adaptation for large-scale 3DGS: couples high-frequency evidence to spatial support and densification, with adaptive staged optimization.
gYkRVCORE6.problem: Gaussian primitives are low-pass, so capturing high-frequency detail in large urban scenes needs excessive densification, pushing methods toward multi-GPU training or scene partitioning.
gYkRVCORE6.method: SpecGS estimates Gaussian-level high-frequency evidence from image-space frequency responses and uses it for spatial-support regulation and densification prioritization, with a three-stage coarse-to-fine schedule driven by an Adaptive Convergence Trigger (ACT) and final Difference-of-Gaussian supervision.
gYkRVCORE6.key_idea: Image-space frequency responses give per-Gaussian high-frequency evidence that allocates support and densification capacity to detailed regions, while ACT schedules resolution on optimization saturation.
gYkRVCORE6.evidence: Multiple urban datasets, with supplementary GauU-Scene and Mip-Splatting results, compared against 3DGS, CityGaussian and CityGS-X.
gYkRVCORE6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree SpecGS gives a practical memory-quality trade-off, using substantially fewer Gaussians and less memory than baselines, with broader supplementary evaluation.
gYkRVCORE6.main_concern: Novelty and baseline coverage are incomplete (FreGS and FDS-GS already use frequency-guided densification), the frequency-dependent allocation is not directly validated, and many hyperparameters are hand-tuned.

PooGRGFcqo.one_liner: Predicts in-context transfer gains for graph foundation models from a single task-label agreement statistic using a Bayesian posterior-concentration law.
PooGRGFcqo.problem: Whether a graph foundation model will learn a new task in context cannot be predicted before training, and standard graph few-shot evaluations conflate in-context inference with structural shortcuts.
PooGRGFcqo.method: Builds a cross-graph rule-induction testbed with no demonstration-query edges and per-episode randomized label polarity, and shows in-context gain is governed by the polarity-symmetrized label agreement between training and test tasks, as predicted by a Bayesian posterior-concentration argument.
PooGRGFcqo.key_idea: In-context gain follows the polarity-symmetrized label agreement between training and test tasks, derived from Bayesian posterior concentration with no free parameters for a reference learner.
PooGRGFcqo.evidence: Synthetic node, multi-class and link-level rules, five real graph datasets, and a frozen externally pretrained graph foundation model (GraphPFN).
PooGRGFcqo.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the testbed controls (no support-query edges, polarity randomization, label permutation and wrong-rule contexts) convincingly show gains depend on support labels, and that the law is backed by broad evidence.
PooGRGFcqo.main_concern: The law rests on a restrictive binary-classification Bayesian task model and requires labeled samples to compute similarity, so the claim of a general parameter-free law exceeds the evidence.

UAUwDIekdq.one_liner: Spiking point-cloud network that takes the neighborhood max on continuous features before spike generation, plus pseudo-temporal expansion-compression.
UAUwDIekdq.problem: Naively replacing LeakyReLU with spiking neurons in EdgeConv quantizes features before max aggregation, weakening credit assignment and causing severe accuracy loss.
UAUwDIekdq.method: Spiking DGCNN applies a Max-First Spiking Rule that selects the neighborhood max on continuous values before spiking, plus an Adaptive Pseudo-Temporal Expansion-Compression (APTEC) module using leaky spiking integration, adaptive thresholding and binary spike compression.
UAUwDIekdq.key_idea: Reordering neighborhood max aggregation before spike generation keeps discriminative continuous responses intact, so gradients flow to the selected features.
UAUwDIekdq.evidence: Ablations on ModelNet40 and ScanObjectNN, S3DIS segmentation in the appendix, comparison against DGCNN and SPMamba, and an operation-level energy estimate.
UAUwDIekdq.claimed_gains: Max-First lifts ModelNet40 accuracy from 79.09% to 91.77% at T=1 and from 84.11% to 92.18% at T=4; the complete model reaches 92.38% versus 92.9% for DGCNN while the energy estimate falls from 11.23 mJ to 0.22 mJ.
UAUwDIekdq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the Max-First ordering ablation shows a large, consistent gain on classification and segmentation, and the compact model nearly matches DGCNN accuracy.
UAUwDIekdq.main_concern: APTEC's benefit is dataset-dependent and its pseudo-time evidence accumulation is weakly justified (identical inputs, constant threshold), while Max-First is not clearly distinguished from existing pooling-order designs.

ZJJ1RPC4de.one_liner: Long-term conversational memory that keeps context inside facts and links them across sessions via source-grounded entity representations.
ZJJ1RPC4de.problem: In long-term conversations, facts are scattered across turns and sessions, so retrieval misses evidence that comes with enough context.
ZJJ1RPC4de.method: ContextFact builds context-preserving fact memories and, across sessions, aligns recurring referents and revisits the source dialogue to reconstruct entity representations linked to supporting facts; at query time it retrieves fact and entity views, reranks them independently, and expands through entity links.
ZJJ1RPC4de.key_idea: Keep fact-specific context local in each fact memory while organizing cross-session evidence in separate entity representations reconstructed from the source dialogue.
ZJJ1RPC4de.evidence: LoCoMo and LongMemEval-S against many baselines with different LLM backbones and component ablations, plus a study of retrieval-unit boundaries.
ZJJ1RPC4de.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the design is well motivated, with source-grounded entity reconstruction and entity-based memory giving clear gains on multi-hop questions across a comprehensive evaluation.
ZJJ1RPC4de.main_concern: The contribution looks incremental, combining known memory-extraction, entity-linking and reranking techniques, with small gains over the strongest baseline and limited analysis of reconstruction errors and construction cost.

KjsCl9HgWS.one_liner: Training-free clarification policy that asks or acts by reasoning about the value of information of candidate questions.
KjsCl9HgWS.problem: Assistants facing ambiguous requests must choose between acting and asking, and uncertainty-minimizing question selection ignores downstream reward, asking cost and unprompted user corrections.
KjsCl9HgWS.method: REVOIR reasons at inference time about the expected improvement in task reward from a question's answer, comparing asking against acting immediately and allowing for the user correcting the assistant without being asked.
KjsCl9HgWS.key_idea: Estimate a question's value of information as the expected task-reward gain from its answer, looking ahead through a simulated correction on the act branch.
KjsCl9HgWS.evidence: Two assistive tasks, ambiguous question answering (CondAmbigQA) and preference-aligned household planning (ADAPT), against prompting, chain-of-thought, fine-tuning and information-gain baselines across several LLMs.
KjsCl9HgWS.claimed_gains: Improves preference satisfaction on ADAPT by 13-15% over a fine-tuned clarification policy while requiring no training and asking five times fewer questions.
KjsCl9HgWS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is practical and under-studied, the value-of-information framing is clear, the method is training-free, and evaluation spans several LLMs.
KjsCl9HgWS.main_concern: Novelty relative to prior value-of-information and EVPI clarification work is unclear, and reliance on LLM-simulated users (internal and external) is not validated against humans.

8jkqWXsJ0n.one_liner: Shows in parallel PPO that conditioning the critic on a logged environment index fixes value mismatch across environments.
8jkqWXsJ0n.problem: A critic without environment information must fit different value targets for the same state across environments, shifting sampled advantages and reinforcing unhelpful actions.
8jkqWXsJ0n.method: Analyzes illustrative multi-environment bandits to characterize how value mismatch redistributes policy updates, then gives the critic only a logged environment index so it can separate value targets, tested on CartPole, MuJoCo, BipedalWalker and Procgen.
8jkqWXsJ0n.key_idea: Keep the actor shared but condition the critic on the environment index, so value targets separate per environment and advantages are no longer shifted.
8jkqWXsJ0n.evidence: Bandit analysis (Propositions 1-3 per reviewers), controlled CartPole and MuJoCo experiments, and BipedalWalker and Procgen settings.
8jkqWXsJ0n.claimed_gains: More stable learning and higher returns in BipedalWalker and Procgen; the abstract's final summary over all 16 settings is cut off.
8jkqWXsJ0n.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the bandit theory gives a sound, useful explanation of value mismatch and the controlled experiments make the practical result persuasive.
8jkqWXsJ0n.main_concern: Theory is on simple bandit models and the intervention depends on stable environment identifiers, with limited increment over multitask PopArt and limited experimental breadth.

fSHuzhX6Gn.one_liner: Builds raw, global-principal and local-structural representations per view, then aligns granularities across views with gating and low-rank bilinear fusion.
fSHuzhX6Gn.problem: Multi-view clustering mostly exploits cross-view complementarity and overlooks structural diversity inside each high-dimensional view, which a single representation may not capture.
fSHuzhX6Gn.method: LIVC constructs three representations per view, performs granularity-aligned cross-view interaction with learnable gating for selective information transfer, and applies residual low-rank bilinear fusion to capture second-order dependencies. A joint self-supervised objective preserves view-specific information while coordinating representations across granularities and views.
fSHuzhX6Gn.key_idea: Expose within-view structure through raw, PCA-based global and KNN-based local branches, then exchange information only between matching granularities across views via learnable gates.
fSHuzhX6Gn.evidence: Multiple high-dimensional multi-view datasets (multi-omics per reviewers) over five seeds with ablation and parameter studies; reviewers report best mean results on 14 of 15 dataset-metric combinations.
fSHuzhX6Gn.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that building three complementary per-view representations is a thoughtful design and that extensive experiments show effectiveness on high-dimensional, small-sample data.
fSHuzhX6Gn.main_concern: The motivation for intra-view complementarity is not established: it is unclear which structures a single representation loses, gains may come from denoising or smoothing, and the PCA and KNN branch contributions are not analyzed separately.

UR4LGuL05t.one_liner: Three-stage alignment that attributes refusals to tokens, adds contrastive benign samples, and regularizes consistency under template-ablated attention.
UR4LGuL05t.problem: Safety alignment of large reasoning models via SFT and RL yields near-perfect safety scores but severe over-refusal and degraded general capabilities, tied to spurious formatting and lexical shortcuts.
UR4LGuL05t.method: Refusal Sensitivity Attribution masks input tokens to measure their effect on the refusal distribution; Attribution-Guided Contrastive Augmentation builds benign contrastive samples from high-sensitivity tokens; Counterfactual Consistency Regularization uses attention blinding to create template-ablated states and enforce decision consistency across SFT and RL.
UR4LGuL05t.key_idea: Mask tokens to find those driving refusals, contrast them in benign samples, and blind attention to the chat template to force format-invariant safety decisions.
UR4LGuL05t.evidence: Template-stripping and RL training-dynamics analyses, then comparisons against standard SFT and GRPO with 1000 SFT and 340-400 RL training prompts and GPT-4o as judge according to reviewers.
UR4LGuL05t.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the shortcut diagnosis (formatting and lexical) compelling and the attention-blinding consistency term a pluggable, differentiable addition to SFT, PPO, and GRPO pipelines.
UR4LGuL05t.main_concern: Baseline coverage is thin (SafeChain, SafeKey, and STAIR are missing from the main comparisons) and training relies on GPT-4o as judge with small training sets, while one reviewer questions whether the formatting-shortcut threat model is practical.

YwbaJYv7HU.one_liner: Four-task scientific benchmark varies agent configuration (information, reasoning, verification, time budget, model) to measure effects on performance and consistency.
YwbaJYv7HU.problem: Agent evaluations report cost, consistency, and robustness but treat the agent as fixed, although users choose what to tell it, how long it runs, and which model it uses.
YwbaJYv7HU.method: The authors build a benchmark of four scientific tasks where a coding agent must find and correctly operate a published specialist model, and vary five configuration parts: task information, reasoning, self-verification, time budget, and backbone model. A trajectory-based taxonomy of agent behavior is also built.
YwbaJYv7HU.key_idea: Treat the agent as a configurable system and measure each configuration axis and its interactions, including run-to-run variance from repeating one configuration.
YwbaJYv7HU.evidence: 432 configurations repeated 5 times each per task on four tasks in two scientific domains, with ablations across model families and a trajectory taxonomy, according to reviews.
YwbaJYv7HU.claimed_gains: About 54% of outcome variance comes from repeating the same configuration rather than changing it.
YwbaJYv7HU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the study is large, holistic, and robust, decomposes the agent into useful configuration axes, and addresses a pertinent but often neglected evaluation problem.
YwbaJYv7HU.main_concern: Scope is narrow (four tasks in two domains) so claims about each knob may not generalize, unfinished runs are excluded non-randomly, and the headline that information beats time budget does not hold for every model.

hi2kjQQnyN.one_liner: Alternately trains an LLM policy and a harness editor as approximate best responses in a common-payoff game.
hi2kjQQnyN.problem: LLM agent capability depends jointly on the policy and the harness, but existing work optimizes one side or updates both in an essentially one-sided way.
hi2kjQQnyN.method: DuetHarness casts policy and harness as a common-payoff game and alternates learned updates: with the policy frozen, an editor learns to revise the harness from rollout feedback, and with the harness fixed, the policy trains against current and historical harnesses.
hi2kjQQnyN.key_idea: Alternate approximate best-response updates, a learned harness editor against a frozen policy and a policy trained on current and historical harnesses, toward a mutual best response.
hi2kjQQnyN.evidence: Three agent benchmarks with Qwen3.5-9B, including WebShop and ALFWorld, with ablations on alternation (policy-only, editor-only, sequential, frozen editor).
hi2kjQQnyN.claimed_gains: Lifts WebShop success by 23.6% and ALFWorld unseen/seen by 53.0%/42.8% (from the TL;DR).
hi2kjQQnyN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the policy-harness split is clear, training the editor rather than using a frozen proposer is meaningful, and the WebShop ablations isolate the effect of alternation.
hi2kjQQnyN.main_concern: The alternation ablation exists only for WebShop (ALFWorld gains lack policy-only or sequential controls), the Nash-equilibrium claim is stronger than the evidence, and the closest co-evolution baselines are not evaluated.

9Qpnzx8pbZ.one_liner: MemAff-Bench tests retrieving a past frame and pixel-localizing an affordance from visual memory; MemAff does retrieve, rerank, then ground.
9Qpnzx8pbZ.problem: Affordance prediction methods assume the target object is visible in the current image, which fails when an instruction refers to an object seen much earlier in an agent's visual memory.
9Qpnzx8pbZ.method: The paper formulates memory-grounded affordance prediction and builds MemAff-Bench with 3,628 tasks from egocentric videos and indoor panoramas, with memories of 120-960 frames. MemAff is a training-free framework that retrieves promising observations, visually reranks them and grounds the target object.
9Qpnzx8pbZ.key_idea: Retrieve candidate frames from long visual memory, visually rerank them, and ground the target only in the selected frame, instead of passing the full memory to a VLM.
9Qpnzx8pbZ.evidence: MemAff-Bench with increasing memory size, comparing single-pass long-context VLMs against the retrieve-then-rerank pipeline, with frame accuracy and mask IoU decomposition and retrieval ablations.
9Qpnzx8pbZ.claimed_gains: MemAff matches or exceeds the frame accuracy of a 4x larger Qwen3-VL-32B single-pass model while using one to two orders of magnitude fewer (quantity cut off in the source abstract).
9Qpnzx8pbZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the benchmark fills a meaningful gap by jointly evaluating long-term memory retrieval and pixel-level grounding, with memory-size scaling and error decomposition giving diagnostic value.
9Qpnzx8pbZ.main_concern: The strict exact-frame metric gives zero credit when the same object appears in other frames, so performance drops with memory size may partly reflect annotation ambiguity rather than retrieval difficulty.

yO3aSuGr8P.one_liner: Proves a worst-case exponential-in-dimension lower bound for spline KANs; controlled experiments show their advantage depends on target structure.
yO3aSuGr8P.problem: KANs have a dimension-independent approximation exponent for targets with smooth univariate-edge representations, and it is unclear whether this favorable scaling belongs to the architecture or to the assumed target class.
yO3aSuGr8P.method: For arbitrary-depth standard spline-KANs on isotropic Sobolev balls, the paper proves that below a dimension-independent accuracy threshold the number of spline coefficients must grow at least exponentially with input dimension. It complements this with MLP comparisons: spline-KAN approximants transfer exactly to cubic-ReLU MLPs, and ridge-profile scans vary how many inputs each nonlinear component couples.
yO3aSuGr8P.key_idea: Exact spline-to-ReLU^k realization plus a parameter-count and shattering argument gives a lower bound; ridge-profile scans isolate the number of inputs each component couples.
yO3aSuGr8P.evidence: A theorem on Sobolev balls, four scaling-law targets, controlled ridge-profile scans and a random-label MNIST test comparing spline KANs, KANs with a SiLU branch and ReLU-MLPs.
yO3aSuGr8P.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers regard the formal lower bound, with a dimension-independent accuracy threshold, and the controlled ridge-profile experiments as useful and technically sound.
yO3aSuGr8P.main_concern: The theorem covers only spline-only KANs, excluding the SiLU branch and newer variants, and extends a bound the original KAN work already acknowledged, so its scope is narrow.

FWvTc7u9pz.one_liner: On-policy self-distillation where the teacher sees a short answer-or-refuse instruction instead of a reference response, improving VLM safety.
FWvTc7u9pz.problem: VLMs that refuse harmful text requests often comply when a benign-looking request is paired with an image that makes it harmful, and it is unclear what privileged context an OPSD teacher should see for safety.
FWvTc7u9pz.method: SA2-OPSD maps each pair's image, request, and pair safety labels to a short instruction stating whether to answer or refuse and where the risk lies; the student, seeing only image and request, learns from the teacher's next-token distributions on its own responses.
FWvTc7u9pz.key_idea: Give the self-distillation teacher the action (answer or refuse, and where the risk lies) as privileged context rather than a full reference answer.
FWvTc7u9pz.evidence: Comparison with six baselines across two model scales and three safety benchmarks, a response-level analysis of Qwen3-VL-4B baselines, and HoliSafe-Bench ASR averaged over three runs.
FWvTc7u9pz.claimed_gains: Lowest attack success rate in five of six settings; against OPSD, HoliSafe-Bench mean ASR drops from 37.7 to 25.8% at 4B and from 32.2 to 25.8% at 8B.
FWvTc7u9pz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is important and the idea of stating the action instead of an answer is simple and intuitive, with strong controlled results against OPSD and comprehensive robustness checks.
FWvTc7u9pz.main_concern: Simple baselines and safety-specific methods are missing (such as directly training to refuse unsafe inputs), novelty is a small change to OPSD, and the action-only variant nearly matches the full method.

l9QJO8BIoE.one_liner: Defines the signed decision value of escalating perception compute and introduces DEEP, scoring allocators against a budget-constrained decision oracle.
l9QJO8BIoE.problem: Adaptive perception spends extra compute where perception should improve, but a better perception output need not produce a better downstream decision.
l9QJO8BIoE.method: Decision value is the single-step reduction in downstream loss from escalating an input from a cheap to an expensive perception mode, and it can be negative. DEEP scores allocators that see only pre-escalation information against a budget-constrained decision oracle under selection, latency, and energy budgets, charging each allocator for its own computation.
l9QJO8BIoE.key_idea: Judge perception escalation by the signed change in downstream decision loss, and compare allocators with an oracle that escalates only where the decision improves under a budget.
l9QJO8BIoE.evidence: KITTI, nuScenes, nuPlan, and NAVSIM with braking and trajectory controllers and published planners, including all 850 nuScenes scenes.
l9QJO8BIoE.claimed_gains: 34-62% of escalations that change the downstream loss make it worse; on 850 nuScenes scenes the budgeted oracle removes 31% of braking loss while escalating at most one frame in five; perception gains disagree in sign with decision value on 25-51% of frames.
l9QJO8BIoE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that valuing perception compute by its downstream decision effect is an important, underexplored framing, with a clear benchmark, oracle definition, and metrics.
l9QJO8BIoE.main_concern: Conceptual novelty over value-of-information ideas is thin, conclusions depend on the chosen braking and planning losses, and the learned allocators are weak and regress per-frame value instead of optimizing the budgeted objective.

sfXaWdUHoI.one_liner: Divide-and-conquer causal discovery that groups variables by edge-related sets and derives group order, using quadratic-time decomposition and aggregation.
sfXaWdUHoI.problem: Causal discovery has exponential complexity in the number of variables, and prior divide-and-conquer methods incur heavy decomposition or aggregation overhead and lose local correctness and completeness.
sfXaWdUHoI.method: The framework partitions variables into groups defined by edge-related sets, exports the topological order between groups, and merges local solutions, with proofs of lossless decomposition and consistency with the global graph; it plugs into solvers such as PC, LiNGAM, GOLEM, and SCORE.
sfXaWdUHoI.key_idea: Define variable groups via edge-related sets and read off the topological order between groups, avoiding recursive cut-set search while using quadratically many conditional independence tests.
sfXaWdUHoI.evidence: Theorems on lossless decomposition and a consistent global graph, plus experiments on a wide range of benchmark datasets with multiple base causal discovery algorithms; main experiments use oracle conditional independence tests, with sample-based tests in the appendix.
sfXaWdUHoI.claimed_gains: Provably quadratic-time decomposition and aggregation, and consistent, significant improvements in scalability and performance of various causal discovery algorithms; no numbers stated.
sfXaWdUHoI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the grouping idea simple and different from prior cut-set approaches, solver-agnostic as a plugin, backed by theoretical guarantees, and broadly evaluated.
sfXaWdUHoI.main_concern: Main experiments rely on oracle conditional independence tests, so robustness under realistic finite-sample test errors is weakly established.

qF2gbvBQOf.one_liner: Automated pipeline synthesizes runnable GUI software environments, verified by GUI evaluation and iterative repair, to train computer-use agents.
qF2gbvBQOf.problem: Native application environments are costly to build and risk application-specific overfitting, while browser-hosted environments offer limited interaction depth and workflow complexity.
qF2gbvBQOf.method: SoftwareGym generates structurally diverse application designs, realizes them as runnable applications, and uses GUI evaluation with iterative repair to ensure functional reliability. Trajectories collected from the synthesized environments are used to train a computer-use agent.
qF2gbvBQOf.key_idea: Generate diverse application designs, implement them, then run GUI tests and repair the application from GUI feedback until behavior is runtime-verified.
qF2gbvBQOf.evidence: 182 synthesized applications in twelve categories, the 120-task SoftwareGym-Bench, and OSWorld evaluation; reviews cite a GUI-guided versus source-only repair ablation and data-source comparisons.
qF2gbvBQOf.claimed_gains: Synthesizes 182 applications across twelve categories with a mean GUI task pass rate of 91.5%, raises Pass@3 on OSWorld from 41.39% to 56.97%, and reaches 40.0% on the 120-task SoftwareGym-Bench.
qF2gbvBQOf.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the pipeline is well engineered, GUI-guided repair clearly beats source-only repair, and training on synthesized trajectories improves performance on real applications.
qF2gbvBQOf.main_concern: The source of the OSWorld gains is not isolated (category overlap with test domains, undisclosed teacher model, confounded data volume), and novelty over earlier environment-synthesis pipelines is unclear.

r1ikqi2kFf.one_liner: Benchmark where coding agents build end-to-end inference serving systems, verified by a token-level correctness check and scored by speedup.
r1ikqi2kFf.problem: Prior coding benchmarks cover localized code changes or tuning an existing engine, not building a full serving system across kernels, memory management, scheduling, and parallelism.
r1ikqi2kFf.method: MLServingBench gives an agent 12 to 36 hours in a sandbox with up to 8 H200 GPUs to build a correct, performant serving system for a model architecture, compute topology, and production workload. A token-level verifier compares outputs against a reference implementation, and correct submissions are scored by speedup over a production serving framework.
r1ikqi2kFf.key_idea: Score end-to-end agent-built serving systems by speedup over a production framework, gated by a token-level output verifier against a reference implementation.
r1ikqi2kFf.evidence: Frontier proprietary and open models evaluated across seven tasks spanning text generation, agentic workloads, and speech and multimodal models; reviews cite 126 main builds with three runs per model-task pair.
r1ikqi2kFf.claimed_gains: No agent outperforms the production baseline reliably on all seven tasks, and only 23.0% of runs produce a correct system faster than the baseline.
r1ikqi2kFf.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the benchmark tests challenging end-to-end system building beyond localized code changes or isolated kernel optimization.
r1ikqi2kFf.main_concern: The correctness verifier's false-rejection risk is not characterized well enough, and a rejected submission scores zero.

0qwgjSHZzV.one_liner: Releases a hedge-confidence dataset and mapper to measure, prompt, and fine-tune linguistic confidence in LLMs.
0qwgjSHZzV.problem: LLM confidence estimation is impractical because logits are often hidden, multi-sampling is expensive, and verbalized numeric scores deviate from natural communication.
0qwgjSHZzV.method: They release a large human-annotated dataset of hedging expressions with confidence scores and a lightweight mapper from hedges to confidence at near-zero cost. They then study linguistic confidence across LLMs and QA benchmarks with calibration and discriminability criteria and add a fine-tuning framework to improve it.
0qwgjSHZzV.key_idea: Convert hedging language into confidence scores with a small mapper trained on human annotations, then evaluate and fine-tune LLMs on the calibration and discriminability of those scores.
0qwgjSHZzV.evidence: A new human-annotated hedging dataset, a mapper compared with LLM judges, and calibration and discriminability evaluations across modern LLMs and QA benchmarks, plus fine-tuning.
0qwgjSHZzV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the human-annotated dataset and lightweight mapper are valuable, practical tools and that the cross-model evaluation of linguistic confidence is informative.
0qwgjSHZzV.main_concern: The competitiveness of explicit hedging prompts and fine-tuning is overstated, since results are mixed against numeric verbalized confidence and no error bars or confidence intervals are reported.

zL2kRfGRom.one_liner: RL trains an LLM to navigate textbooks through a BookNavigator interface, with exploration bonuses against tool collapse.
zL2kRfGRom.problem: Solving problems in unfamiliar domains needs tightly coupled knowledge acquisition and reasoning, beyond factual retrieval or learning from a preassembled context.
zL2kRfGRom.method: Formulates textbook-based mathematical proof solving with reference solutions withheld, and introduces a BookNavigator interface whose use is trained with RL. Tool collapse under correctness-only rewards is countered with correctness-gated exploration bonuses and centered round-level credit.
zL2kRfGRom.key_idea: Gate exploration bonuses on answer correctness and give centered round-level credit so RL keeps the agent using textbook-navigation tools.
zL2kRfGRom.evidence: An environment of 158 textbooks and 5,183 proof problems (per reviews), in-domain and out-of-domain textbooks and subjects, RL-trained textbook-free and fixed-retrieval baselines, and long-context benchmarks.
zL2kRfGRom.claimed_gains: Raises Intern-S2-Preview-35B's overall proof accuracy from 51.5% to 79.5%, outperforming RL-trained textbook-free and fixed-retrieval baselines, with improvements over the base model of 1.7 and 2.3 on long-context benchmarks (unit truncated in the abstract).
zL2kRfGRom.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the textbook-based self-learning task is useful and that controls such as textbook substitution and section removal support that the reference content drives the gains.
zL2kRfGRom.main_concern: Proof correctness is judged by one LLM (GLM-5.2) for both training rewards and evaluation, with no human or independent-judge validation.

Ag9G9NWnj4.one_liner: Policy learning from a real contact world and a simulated spatial world, completing each other's missing factors with world models.
Ag9G9NWnj4.problem: Learning robotic ultrasound policies needs costly complete real-world expert demonstrations, while simulation lacks the faithful contact-dependent dynamics that scanning requires.
Ag9G9NWnj4.method: CrossWorld learns from a real contact world and a simulated spatial world via cross-world factor completion: contact completion transfers appearance dynamics from local real interactions to simulated observations, and spatial completion transfers action-conditioned spatial dynamics from simulation to sparse real observations. The policy jointly perceives each observed ultrasound image and its cross-world completed view.
Ag9G9NWnj4.key_idea: Two world models complete missing factors in each domain, adding real contact appearance to simulated frames and simulated spatial dynamics to sparse real frames, and the policy sees both views.
Ag9G9NWnj4.evidence: Experiments with three policy backbones and a real-robot evaluation on one phantom with three human participants, judged by two blinded clinicians, per reviewers; the abstract is cut off before results.
Ag9G9NWnj4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is well motivated and that CrossWorld improves performance across three policy backbones, with large gains in real-robot evaluation.
Ag9G9NWnj4.main_concern: Related work on sim-real co-training is missing and the controls do not separate cross-world factor completion from extra temporal context, with real evaluation limited to one phantom and three participants.

DBDVNF3dMF.one_liner: Non-manifold surface reconstruction by learning pairwise point affinities to split clouds into manifold patches, then stitching patches along non-manifold curves.
DBDVNF3dMF.problem: Marching-cubes-style methods resolve non-manifold topology locally and tend to produce missing, broken, or fragmented non-manifold edges.
DBDVNF3dMF.method: A learned decomposition partitions the point cloud into overlapping blocks and predicts whether neighboring point pairs belong to the same manifold patch, then thresholding and union-find yield manifold patches and non-manifold curve points. Each patch is reconstructed with an off-the-shelf manifold reconstructor and the patches are stitched with explicitly non-manifold edges.
DBDVNF3dMF.key_idea: Predict same-patch affinities for neighboring point pairs, group them with union-find, and reconstruct each manifold patch separately before stitching along non-manifold curves.
DBDVNF3dMF.evidence: Three benchmarks including CAD models and point clouds sampled from neural implicit fields, with the network trained only on shapes made by intersecting manifold meshes and tested zero-shot.
DBDVNF3dMF.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract only says it matches strong baselines in Chamfer distance while achieving the lowest (text cut off).
DBDVNF3dMF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the decomposition-and-assembly formulation is clear and well motivated and gives large topological gains (non-manifold Chamfer distance, Betti numbers, Euler characteristic) from learning only local pairwise affinities.
DBDVNF3dMF.main_concern: Generalization evidence is narrow (author-built test sets, no raw scans) and the Chamfer distance is higher than some competitors, with a costly deterministic assembly step.

AfSPfRUopu.one_liner: Trains a streaming video policy with SFT then GRPO to sense evidence and decide when to respond.
AfSPfRUopu.problem: Streaming interaction models decide when to respond but handle evidence acquisition separately, so response timing is not tied to what evidence has actually been acquired.
AfSPfRUopu.method: Self-Focus builds its own working context through continuous active sensing, before and after a query arrives. The policy is initialized by SFT on streaming episodes, then optimized with GRPO over its self-generated context using a delayed sensing credit.
AfSPfRUopu.key_idea: Learns sensing actions and response timing in one policy, crediting each sensing action by its advantage in the subsequent interaction return (delayed sensing credit).
AfSPfRUopu.evidence: Evaluated on proactive and retrospective tasks across four benchmarks, plus offline long-video reasoning and iterative video agents; reviewers note ablations over sensing actions and SFT-only and trajectory-level GRPO variants.
AfSPfRUopu.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract reports best results on four benchmarks and better performance at fewer search iterations for video agents, without numbers.
AfSPfRUopu.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the problem well motivated, the evaluation extensive across streaming benchmarks, and the ablations of individual sensing actions informative.
AfSPfRUopu.main_concern: Limited novelty and weak differentiation from prior streaming and adaptive-selection work (e.g., QueryStream, Thinking-QwenVL), and a delayed sensing credit that resembles a standard return-to-go estimator with a leave-one-out baseline.

f2RqhnMBby.one_liner: Heterophilous-graph GNN using mixed-curvature embeddings, parallel transport of messages, and separate smooth and contrastive diffusion tracks.
f2RqhnMBby.problem: On heterophilous graphs, aggregation mixes semantically incompatible nodes and a single latent geometry cannot capture coexisting hierarchical, flat, and cyclic structure.
f2RqhnMBby.method: CTS-Net embeds nodes in a mixed-curvature product manifold, parallel-transports neighbor messages to the receiver tangent space, and routes them into smooth and contrastive tracks through a learned orthogonal operator. Track-specific polynomial diffusion then learns distinct spectral responses for the two signal types.
f2RqhnMBby.key_idea: Aligns neighbor messages by parallel transport into the receiver's tangent space before an orthogonal operator routes them into smooth and contrastive spectral tracks.
f2RqhnMBby.evidence: 14 datasets with different homophily levels and scales (highest mean Macro-F1 on 11 of 14 per reviews), with theory on orthogonal routing and transport.
f2RqhnMBby.claimed_gains: not stated in the visible abstract (reviewers report the highest mean Macro-F1 on 11 of the 14 datasets in Table 1).
f2RqhnMBby.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the pairing of geometric alignment with heterophily-aware propagation well motivated and the 14-dataset evaluation broad.
f2RqhnMBby.main_concern: Underspecified geometric details (how local frames and track subspaces are chosen) and unclear novelty over sheaf and connection-based GNNs.
