tDe5JRJmGH.one_liner: A2QA predicts final action-quality scores from partial video by scoring retrieved real endings weighted by a conditional-flow likelihood.
tDe5JRJmGH.problem: Action quality assessment normally predicts a score only after the full video, and predicting before an action ends requires handling uncertainty about the unseen future.
tDe5JRJmGH.method: A2QA retrieves real future segments from training videos with compatible declared content and appends them to the partial video in feature space. A conditional flow model estimates each completion's likelihood given the partial video, a frozen scorer evaluates each completed sequence, and the likelihood-weighted scores are aggregated.
tDe5JRJmGH.key_idea: Complete a partial video with retrieved real endings, weight each completion by a conditional-flow likelihood, and aggregate the frozen scorer's outputs.
tDe5JRJmGH.evidence: Experiments on four datasets spanning sports and surgical skill assessment (FineFS, FineDiving, and others; abstract cut off); reviewers cite eleven reused scorers and five observation ratios.
tDe5JRJmGH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the framework is model-agnostic, reusing pretrained AQA scorers without retraining, and shows consistent early-observation gains over scoring truncated videos in broad experiments.
tDe5JRJmGH.main_concern: The only baseline is a full-video scorer applied to truncated video, with no baseline trained for early prediction, and it is unclear what information (declared future content) is available at prediction time.

KUAlW7DbIh.one_liner: Structural causal framework tracing cross-turn error propagation in memory-augmented LLMs using four counterfactual trajectories.
KUAlW7DbIh.problem: Evaluations of memory-augmented LLMs check whether information is stored and retrieved correctly but not the causal pathways by which errors persist and re-emerge.
KUAlW7DbIh.method: The framework models user questions, responses, and memory states as a dynamic causal process, separates memory-update and question-feedback pathways, and estimates their downstream effects and interaction with four counterfactual trajectories, measured through memory retention, natural responses, diagnostic probes, and probability-level error preference.
KUAlW7DbIh.key_idea: Separate memory-update and question-feedback pathways with four counterfactual trajectories sharing a pre-intervention history, then measure error at four levels.
KUAlW7DbIh.evidence: Experiments across models, memory categories, injection positions, and memory mechanisms; reviews note 144 synthetic multi-turn interactions and two 7B models.
KUAlW7DbIh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the four-trajectory causal design and multi-level error measurement give a rigorous, systematic view of errors persisting in memory after vanishing from natural responses.
KUAlW7DbIh.main_concern: The validity filter makes the memory-path effect strong by construction, restoration is an oracle setting, and experiments use only synthetic data with two 7B models, limiting generalizability.

zAy99Hyyja.one_liner: Builds weighted action preferences from existing rollouts by matching decisions on state summary and rubric progress, added to GraphGPO.
zAy99Hyyja.problem: Long-horizon LLM agents must assign credit to intermediate decisions from sparse terminal feedback, and comparisons among sibling rollouts depend on context and evidence for each action.
zAy99Hyyja.method: MCGPO defines comparison contexts from pre-action state summaries and task-rule-annotated rubric progress, selects among ordered exact and coarse matching rules by two-action support, and uses fixed folds to separate candidate decisions from the terminal outcomes that orient preferences. Support-dependent evidence weights scale an auxiliary pairwise objective alongside GraphGPO, reusing rollout data and staying critic-free.
zAy99Hyyja.key_idea: Compare actions only across rollouts matched on state and rubric progress, orient preferences with opposite-fold outcomes, and weight them by evidence support.
zAy99Hyyja.evidence: Six environment-backbone settings (ALFWorld and WebShop with Qwen2.5-1.5B and 7B, WebShop with Qwen3-4B and 8B), three training seeds each, against matched GraphGPO.
zAy99Hyyja.claimed_gains: Improves mean success over matched GraphGPO by 0.47-1.46 percentage points on ALFWorld and WebShop with Qwen2.5-1.5B and 7B, and by 3.96 and 5.16 points on WebShop with Qwen3-4B and 8B.
zAy99Hyyja.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that conditioning action comparisons on state and rubric progress is a sensible extension of graph-based credit assignment, with careful controls and gains from existing rollouts without a critic.
zAy99Hyyja.main_concern: Local preference validity is weakly established: 90.7% of WebShop preferences come from coarse matching and 77.7% have a single supporting trajectory for the less-supported action, so gains may not reflect causal action value.

QMY6yLW6bY.one_liner: Penalizes drift from a frozen reference on random-token anchors with a Fisher-weighted MMD, mitigating forgetting in RL post-training of VLMs.
QMY6yLW6bY.problem: Single-domain RL post-training silently collapses held-out VLM capability, hidden by suite-wide averages, and existing defenses assume the anchor set must represent the capabilities being protected.
QMY6yLW6bY.method: CFA is a Fisher-weighted Maximum Mean Discrepancy penalty between current and reference next-token distributions, derived as a Gauss-Newton generalization of Elastic Weight Consolidation and applied to anchors of uniformly random tokens. The authors also introduce the worst-k curve and prove anchors affect retention only through a transfer coefficient (abstract truncated).
QMY6yLW6bY.key_idea: Constrain next-token distributions to a frozen reference on content-free random-token anchors, since anchor content affects retention only through a transfer coefficient.
QMY6yLW6bY.evidence: Qwen3-VL at 2B, 4B, and 8B scale under single-domain RL post-training, comparing random anchors against a curated real coreset spanning five capability dimensions and against existing defenses.
QMY6yLW6bY.claimed_gains: Random-token anchors match, and at modest budgets outperform, a curated real coreset; the abstract reports baseline worst-decile drops up to -67% hidden behind flat suite averages.
QMY6yLW6bY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that content-free random anchors mitigating forgetting is a useful, counterintuitive finding and that the worst-k curve exposes tail forgetting that suite averages hide.
QMY6yLW6bY.main_concern: The claim that anchor content is unnecessary is overstated: the concentration theory does not establish retention on real inputs, headline numbers conflict with appendix tables, and evaluation covers one model family.

FpuhBZxZzo.one_liner: Benchmark of hard, visually verifiable text-to-image prompts across nine capability axes, graded by grounded VLM question decomposition.
FpuhBZxZzo.problem: There is no benchmark that stress-tests where frontier text-to-image models fall short using objectively verifiable prompts such as counting, deep reasoning, physical consistency, and complex rules.
FpuhBZxZzo.method: Prompts span nine capability axes and are designed so alignment is visually verifiable. The automated evaluator decomposes each prompt into easy and hard questions and, for most hard questions, draws help lines to ground the evidence for grading.
FpuhBZxZzo.key_idea: Decompose prompts into easy and hard questions and ground the hard ones with drawn help lines, so the VLM verifies evidence rather than judging holistically.
FpuhBZxZzo.evidence: Evaluation of 20+ text-to-image models including Nano Banana Pro, GPT-Image-2.5, and Seedream-5.0, coding models such as GPT-6 Astra, and a grounding ablation and human-agreement check per reviews.
FpuhBZxZzo.claimed_gains: The best text-to-image model (Nano Banana Pro) achieves a strict score of only 23.9 out of 100, and coding models such as GPT-6 Astra have higher prompt alignment scores.
FpuhBZxZzo.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the grounded evaluation design is a substantive step beyond direct VLM judging and that the thorough multi-model evaluation delivers a clear message that frontier models score low.
FpuhBZxZzo.main_concern: The motivation and practical relevance of synthetic, pedantic tasks are questioned, and withheld tasks and heavy grounding cost make comparisons across models uneven.

IaUWuZHzoV.one_liner: Theory of when to add, subtract, or ignore earlier verifier scores in step-level error detection under correlated noise.
IaUWuZHzoV.problem: Step-level verifier scores are noisy, and earlier scores can either add evidence or repeat the same scoring error, so it is unclear how a detector should use history.
IaUWuZHzoV.method: They develop a theory of causal linear detectors under correlated noise that optimize a class-weighted SNR. In a stationary binary Markov model historical weights are positive when the state persists longer than the noise, negative when the noise persists longer, and zero when equal, while finite-trace initialization can reverse this.
IaUWuZHzoV.key_idea: The sign of the optimal historical weights is set by whether the state persists longer than the observation noise, so history is added, subtracted, or ignored.
IaUWuZHzoV.evidence: Theorems on the stationary and finite-trace cases and a study of 27 methods on 2,000 MATH and GSM8K problems across six settings.
IaUWuZHzoV.claimed_gains: The model-derived kernel improves within-position SNR over current-only scores in all six settings, with simultaneous intervals excluding zero (27 methods, 2,000 MATH and GSM8K problems).
IaUWuZHzoV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the theory is careful and informative (sign law, monotone total historical weight, initialization effects) and that the paper openly examines where assumptions fail on real data.
IaUWuZHzoV.main_concern: The distinctive noise-cancellation prediction is not seen on real data (all fitted settings are in the smoothing regime), and the kernel does not consistently beat tuned exponential smoothing.

gAbzu4hIqM.one_liner: Samples Gaussian anchors and offsets from learned probabilities, decoupling feed-forward 3D Gaussian splatting from the input pixel grid.
gAbzu4hIqM.problem: Pixel-aligned Gaussian allocation ties representation capacity to input resolution and view count, preventing adaptive allocation of the Gaussian budget by scene complexity.
gAbzu4hIqM.method: Builds 3D anchors from image features and estimated geometry; a sampling module jointly learns anchor selection and spatial offsets, trained end-to-end with reconstruction supervision only, to place Gaussians under a controllable shared budget.
gAbzu4hIqM.key_idea: Learn anchor-selection probabilities and offset distributions end to end from reconstruction loss alone, so Gaussians go where the scene needs them.
gAbzu4hIqM.evidence: Experiments on DL3DV-10K covering variable-view inputs including monocular, flexible input resolutions, and adaptive allocation under a Gaussian budget, with ablations such as a random sampling variant.
gAbzu4hIqM.claimed_gains: Claims 'state-of-the-art' novel view synthesis on DL3DV-10K, with monocular reconstruction taking 90.97 ms at the native 540x960 resolution.
gAbzu4hIqM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers like that allocation is learned from reconstruction loss without handcrafted complexity measures, and that the sampling visualizations and sharp novel views show the model focusing capacity sensibly.
gAbzu4hIqM.main_concern: Closely related adaptive-allocation methods (Off The Grid, F4Splat, SparseSplat, EcoSplat) are not compared, so the claim that learned sampling beats heuristic allocation is not directly tested.

hnRnDvEDEv.one_liner: Two-stage visual tool use: GRPO learns direct and tool modes, then on-policy self-distillation learns question-specific routing.
hnRnDvEDEv.problem: Jointly training mode capability and routing with RLVR causes tool overuse or tool collapse, because a mode can lose sampling probability while its capability still improves and rewards can favor tool use without an accuracy benefit.
hnRnDvEDEv.method: Stage one trains a shared expert with GRPO under explicit mode instructions. Stage two compares its performance across modes per question to guide an autonomous student through on-policy self-distillation, with no extra routing rewards or large supervised tool-use trajectories.
hnRnDvEDEv.key_idea: Decouple capability from routing: learn both modes first, then distill per-question mode preferences, derived from comparing mode performance, into the student by on-policy self-distillation.
hnRnDvEDEv.evidence: Analysis of GRPO advantages and training diagnostics, then experiments with Qwen2.5-VL-7B on high-resolution visual benchmarks (V*Bench per reviews).
hnRnDvEDEv.claimed_gains: Accuracy gains of up to 14.13 percentage points over Qwen2.5-VL-7B on high-resolution benchmarks (the abstract text is cut off after 'high-resolution').
hnRnDvEDEv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find separating capability learning from routing intuitive and well motivated, with accuracy gains across visual benchmarks and fewer tool calls.
hnRnDvEDEv.main_concern: Attribution is unclear: there are no direct-only or tool-only RL baselines and no end-to-end joint RL baseline under matched budgets, so capability gains cannot be separated from routing gains, and only one tool type (crop/zoom) is tested.

xAAO8QAOCC.one_liner: DSDyn-VLA pairs a slow optical-flow, future-aware VLA planner with a fast RL residual refiner for dynamic manipulation.
xAAO8QAOCC.problem: VLA models fail on moving objects because of a perception gap (static inputs lack motion cues), a latency gap (inference delay makes actions obsolete), and a control gap (open-loop action-chunk execution).
xAAO8QAOCC.method: The slow Flow-Planner augments the VLA with optical flow and a future-state awareness mechanism that offsets inference latency to produce motion-aware action chunks, and the fast Res-Refiner is a lightweight RL policy that injects high-frequency closed-loop residual corrections from real-time observations. It also introduces DynBench, a MuJoCo benchmark of nine dynamic manipulation tasks.
xAAO8QAOCC.key_idea: Slow-fast split: optical-flow input plus future-state conditioning to offset latency in the planner, and a lightweight RL residual policy correcting action chunks at high frequency.
xAAO8QAOCC.evidence: Simulation on DynBench and real-robot tasks, with ablations and external dynamic benchmarks, compared against baselines such as DynamicVLA.
xAAO8QAOCC.claimed_gains: The abstract says DSDyn-VLA reduces the failure rate by over a figure that is cut off; reviews cite average real-world success rising from 38.1% with DynamicVLA to 49.0%.
xAAO8QAOCC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the dynamic-manipulation problem is relevant, the three-module design is clear, and simulation and real-robot results with ablations show gains over the chosen baselines.
xAAO8QAOCC.main_concern: Novelty is not separated from close prior work (VLASH for future-state compensation and A2C2 for residual correction of action chunks, the latter not compared directly), and ablations do not isolate mechanisms such as polar flow mapping from encoder changes.

V74K09LmIh.one_liner: Controlled changes to subordinate material test whether senior LLM agents weigh, verify, and relay evidence according to their roles.
V74K09LmIh.problem: Final-answer correctness cannot reveal whether senior agents fulfill their responsibilities when using subordinate reports.
V74K09LmIh.method: The benchmark builds tasks from peer review, appellate adjudication, and parliamentary inquiry. It measures responses to controlled changes in subordinate material using rule-based checks and an LLM judge calibrated against human annotation.
V74K09LmIh.key_idea: Intervene on subordinate material while holding underlying records fixed to measure senior-agent duties beyond final-answer correctness.
V74K09LmIh.evidence: The study evaluates eight LLMs across three institutional settings and over 12,000 agentic episodes, with human calibration and case analyses.
V74K09LmIh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value evaluating role fulfillment beyond final decisions through realistic institutional duties and controlled input changes.
V74K09LmIh.main_concern: Reviewers question whether the endpoints establish actual use of subordinate evidence and fulfillment of the stated duties.

9CQAw08kMu.one_liner: Normal-referenced score normalization and a mixture link train graph anomaly detection with labeled and unlabeled nodes.
9CQAw08kMu.problem: Graph anomaly detectors trained on labeled anomaly types can misclassify unseen anomaly types as normal.
9CQAw08kMu.method: NoRD combines supervised anomaly detection with discrimination between unlabeled nodes and labeled normal nodes using one anomaly score. It normalizes scores against labeled normal nodes and applies a mixture link to reduce upward pressure on low-scoring unlabeled normals.
9CQAw08kMu.key_idea: Normalize anomaly scores against labeled normals and apply a mixture link when discriminating unlabeled nodes from normal references.
9CQAw08kMu.evidence: Experiments cover seven public graphs, twelve baselines, five runs, rotating seen anomaly classes, and an internal payment graph.
9CQAw08kMu.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the limited-label anomaly-detection problem useful and recognize effective use of unlabeled nodes with supporting graph evaluations.
9CQAw08kMu.main_concern: Reviewers question the assumption that labeled normal nodes provide a representative reference for the unlabeled normal population.

GIelavSPz1.one_liner: Annotated manuscript revision trajectories test whether AI reviewers reward improvements and retain those rewards under negative user framing.
GIelavSPz1.problem: It is unclear whether AI review scores reflect substantive manuscript improvements or remain stable under user framing.
GIelavSPz1.method: PaperTrajectory-2026 reconstructs paper revisions and annotates changes along 14 dimensions with separate overall-quality judgments. Eight AI reviewers independently assess versions, and negative user opinions test the stability of revision-related score gains.
GIelavSPz1.key_idea: Compare independent scores across annotated manuscript versions, then introduce negative user opinions to test whether revision-related score gains persist.
GIelavSPz1.evidence: The dataset contains 6,959 paper trajectories across five AI conferences, evaluated by eight AI reviewers with human checks of revision annotations.
GIelavSPz1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the real revision-trajectory dataset and the timely study of whether AI reviewers recognize manuscript improvements.
GIelavSPz1.main_concern: Reviewers question the reliability of major-improvement labels produced by a single model without sufficiently independent expert validation.

8Lvte2O8bp.one_liner: Learning conditioning prompts within a diffusion bridge steers frozen diffusion models from degraded inputs toward restored images and videos.
8Lvte2O8bp.problem: Frozen diffusion models do not reliably perform restoration through ordinary text prompts or text-token optimization.
8Lvte2O8bp.method: The method learns conditioning signals at the text-encoder output within a diffusion bridge that aligns training and sampling trajectories. Partial inversion supports sampling, and prompt composition handles mixed degradations.
8Lvte2O8bp.key_idea: Optimize text-encoder-output conditioning within a diffusion bridge that maps noisy degraded states along a coherent denoising path.
8Lvte2O8bp.evidence: FLUX and WAN experiments include image and video restoration, out-of-distribution datasets, backbone-matched LoRA comparisons, and bridge and inversion ablations.
8Lvte2O8bp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize competitive restoration from frozen backbones and useful evidence for conditioning-space optimization and trajectory alignment.
8Lvte2O8bp.main_concern: Reviewers question whether supervised learned prompts demonstrate intrinsic restoration capability rather than parameter-efficient adaptation.

cRg9l0vFCI.one_liner: Row, column, and subtable latent stages separate structure from content for multimodal table reasoning.
cRg9l0vFCI.problem: Existing latent visual reasoning does not explicitly organize computation around table structure.
cRg9l0vFCI.method: DLVR uses progressive row, column, and subtable latent stages with separate structural and semantic components. It trains with decoupled latent supervision on TableLVR-41K and Latent Intervention GRPO using a contribution-based reward.
cRg9l0vFCI.key_idea: Organize structure and content latents by table stages and reward their predictive contribution through counterfactual latent interventions.
cRg9l0vFCI.evidence: Experiments use Qwen2.5-VL and Qwen3-VL across seven benchmarks, with data-matched baselines and ablations of decoupling, supervision, and rewards.
cRg9l0vFCI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize competitive table-reasoning accuracy at lower inference cost and a sensible structure-guided latent design.
cRg9l0vFCI.main_concern: Reviewers find the incremental gains from the latent contribution reward small and insufficiently supported by variability estimates.

YZUgfvtqf9.one_liner: Page canonicalization and fixed-budget token routing bound sparse attention for parsing documents across many pages.
YZUgfvtqf9.problem: Page-wise parsing loses cross-page dependencies, while full-document attention becomes expensive and difficult to route over long visual contexts.
YZUgfvtqf9.method: LASA combines Page Canonicalization, which constrains visual search and stabilizes page positions, with Token Bounding, which selects a fixed budget of relevant visual blocks. This gives each query an attention scope independent of document length.
YZUgfvtqf9.key_idea: Restrict visual candidates using page structure and learn fixed-budget routing over query-relevant visual blocks.
YZUgfvtqf9.evidence: Evaluations on MPDocBench and MarathonDocBench include cross-page text and table parsing, controlled routing ablations, and decoding-time measurements.
YZUgfvtqf9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the page-aware sparse-attention design and improved cross-page parsing supported by long-document evaluations.
YZUgfvtqf9.main_concern: Reviewers identify missing comparisons needed to isolate LASA's advantage over simpler page-restricted attention or strong page-wise pipelines.

c8WN29giQe.one_liner: Fisher-based masking and projection against prior updates prevent sequential speaker unlearning from reviving previously removed identities.
c8WN29giQe.problem: Applying one-shot speaker unlearning sequentially can restore previously suppressed voice identities when their data are no longer retained.
c8WN29giQe.method: CORTIS localizes updates to speaker-relevant parameters using Fisher information. It projects updates against subspaces formed by earlier unlearning updates without accessing previously forgotten speaker data.
c8WN29giQe.key_idea: Mask speaker-relevant weights with Fisher information and orthogonally project new unlearning updates against prior update subspaces.
c8WN29giQe.evidence: Sequential zero-shot TTS evaluations compare CORTIS with prior unlearning methods and ablate projection and masking, while a reviewer identifies the experiments as Voicebox-only.
c8WN29giQe.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize a realistic sequential forgetting problem and effective suppression of previously removed speakers with lower computational cost.
c8WN29giQe.main_concern: Reviewers view the Fisher masking and orthogonal projection as adaptations of established methods with insufficient differentiation from prior continual unlearning.

z5fqixmqwU.one_liner: Distilling token-level log-probability differences between dense and sparse frame views of on-policy rollouts trains video reasoning MLLMs cheaply.
z5fqixmqwU.problem: Reinforcement learning for video reasoning MLLMs faces a trade-off between expensive dense-frame autoregressive rollouts and sparse-frame rollouts that miss fine-grained temporal events.
z5fqixmqwU.method: FD-OPSD generates on-policy RL rollouts under a sparse frame budget and scores the same sampled responses under dense frame views using the same model. Distilling the resulting token-level preference differential transfers dense visual evidence without an external teacher, dense rollouts, or inference-time changes.
z5fqixmqwU.key_idea: Sample on-policy RL responses from sparse video frames, re-score those token sequences under dense frames with the same policy, and self-distill the token-level log-probability differential.
z5fqixmqwU.evidence: Evaluated with Qwen2.5-VL-7B and Qwen3-VL-4B on six video reasoning benchmarks across 16-, 32-, and 64-frame evaluation settings against GRPO, T-GRPO, and Video-KTR.
z5fqixmqwU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that re-scoring sparse-frame rollouts under dense views is a clean, teacher-free mechanism that lowers RL training time by 40–47% while leaving inference unchanged.
z5fqixmqwU.main_concern: Reviewers note that average accuracy gains over the strongest RL baselines are small (0.8–1.3 points) without multi-seed variance reporting, alongside an 8-frame training versus 16/32/64-frame evaluation mismatch and Qwen-only testing.

lP8UNx2XRQ.one_liner: SHUGYO trains game agents with GRPO inside an action-conditioned video simulator rewarded by a rubric-guided vision-language judge.
lP8UNx2XRQ.problem: Imitation-trained game agents suffer compounding errors, while closed commercial games lack fast resets, dynamics access, and reward interfaces for reinforcement learning.
lP8UNx2XRQ.method: SHUGYO adapts a pretrained video diffusion model into a resettable simulator conditioned on rendered frames and native keyboard-and-mouse controls. A rubric-guided vision-language judge supplies rewards for GRPO post-training with a two-stage curriculum and parallel rollout generation.
lP8UNx2XRQ.key_idea: Generate action-conditioned game rollouts in a learned video environment and use visual rubric rewards to train an agent before real-game deployment.
lP8UNx2XRQ.evidence: Black Myth: Wukong experiments compare simulator and real-game task success, and adaptation to a second game uses three hours of data.
lP8UNx2XRQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the complete simulator-training-to-real-game evaluation and evidence of adaptation to a second commercial game.
lP8UNx2XRQ.main_concern: Reviewers find success measurement insufficiently specified and independently validated, particularly if the training reward judge also determines evaluation success.

ngwmV0yz3Y.one_liner: DA-WAM predicts a future latent for each driving trajectory and jointly learns latent dynamics and trajectory utility scores.
ngwmV0yz3Y.problem: Detailed scene reconstruction can emphasize planning-irrelevant information while missing distinctions between candidate actions with different safety outcomes.
ngwmV0yz3Y.method: DA-WAM combines a Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture with action-conditioned future latents and a multi-head trajectory scorer. Joint predictive and planning objectives align representations with observed dynamics and utility, followed by safety-focused post-training using hard negatives.
ngwmV0yz3Y.key_idea: Associate each candidate trajectory with its own predicted future latent and jointly train that representation for dynamics prediction and planning scores.
ngwmV0yz3Y.evidence: Experiments evaluate learned camera-based planning on NAVSIM-v1, NAVSIM-v2, and Bench2Drive with component, future-prediction, and horizon ablations.
ngwmV0yz3Y.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find candidate-specific future representations coupled to trajectory scoring a coherent and practical design for driving decisions.
ngwmV0yz3Y.main_concern: Reviewers find insufficient evidence that candidate-conditioned latents model future consequences rather than merely stronger scene-trajectory feature interactions.

olbdGYAplT.one_liner: SAFER uses text-only controls and controlled perturbation analyses to expose label leakage in radiology hallucination detection.
olbdGYAplT.problem: A radiology benchmark intended to measure visual hallucination detection can reveal its labels through textual construction artifacts.
olbdGYAplT.method: SAFER compares VLMs with text-only and constructed baselines, then removes candidate leakage sources through controlled retraining. Image ablations and counterfactual-pair controls separate swap-vocabulary effects, substring injection artifacts, and eligibility selection.
olbdGYAplT.key_idea: Test image-free label recovery and systematically eliminate textual perturbation artifacts to identify what a visual hallucination benchmark actually measures.
olbdGYAplT.evidence: The benchmark includes 8,294 chest radiograph-report pairs from 8,166 OpenI and MIMIC-CXR studies, seven VLMs, five baselines, and 30 re-trained attribution splits.
olbdGYAplT.claimed_gains: The text-only classifier reaches AUROC 0.918 versus MedGemma-27B's 0.707 on identical studies, with paired difference 0.212 and 95% CI [0.190, 0.234]; the closed 50-word vocabulary explains 57.9% ± 2.2% of the above-chance gap.
olbdGYAplT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find image-free label recovery a meaningful validity check and the analysis of textual leakage informative.
olbdGYAplT.main_concern: The supplied reviews question whether evaluation and attribution controls are adequate, citing unmatched test populations and incompletely specified leakage experiments.

lebFD9dgeX.one_liner: Controlled serialization changes separate extracted-answer correctness, grammar compliance, and strict interface accuracy to reveal format-driven model rankings.
lebFD9dgeX.problem: Language-model evaluations conflate semantic correctness with formatting requirements and parser recognition, potentially reversing model rankings.
lebFD9dgeX.method: The study varies final-answer serialization while preserving reasoning instructions and reports extracted-answer accuracy, terminal-grammar compliance, and strict accuracy separately. Paired comparisons, multiplicity correction, wrapper tolerance, and targeted template interventions test ranking sensitivity.
lebFD9dgeX.key_idea: Hold reasoning instructions fixed while changing answer serialization, then score semantic correctness and interface compliance independently.
lebFD9dgeX.evidence: Five models are tested on MATH-500 and a balanced 13-domain MMLU-Pro subset using 24,750 original generations, a 2,000-response intervention, and 3,000 held-out outputs.
lebFD9dgeX.claimed_gains: The study identifies 12 strict-accuracy and 5 compliance rank reversals but no reliable extracted-answer accuracy reversal, with nine original strict reversals persisting under wrapper tolerance.
lebFD9dgeX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the controlled, statistically careful evaluation and practical recommendation to report correctness, compliance, and strict accuracy separately.
lebFD9dgeX.main_concern: Reviewers view the scientific contribution and generality as limited by the scope of the formatting case study.

Urbr8CilRa.one_liner: FARMerge learns adapter-interference representations from probe activations and uses them to gate rank-one components before fixed-rank merging.
Urbr8CilRa.problem: Parameter-space adapter similarity does not reliably predict functional compatibility or downstream interference during multi-adapter merging.
Urbr8CilRa.method: An offline-trained, layer-aware set encoder maps probe activations into a metric space predictive of pairwise adapter interference. At merge time, domain-spanning probes supply interaction predictions to a linear gate over rank-one SVD components, followed by fixed-rank synthesis without merge-time training.
Urbr8CilRa.key_idea: Predict functional interference from multi-layer probe activations and use those predictions to weight SVD components before synthesizing a merged adapter.
Urbr8CilRa.evidence: Evaluation spans LLaMA-3-8B, Mistral-7B, Qwen3.5-4B, OLMo-2-7B, and 12 tasks, with fixed-rank comparisons and component ablations.
Urbr8CilRa.claimed_gains: FARMerge reports 98.69% single-task-oracle retention on LLaMA-3-8B and 98.39% across four families, with 18.4-second merging at K = 12 on LLaMA-3-8B after 32.8 GPU-hours of offline training per base architecture.
Urbr8CilRa.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value functional interference modeling and the broad adapter-merging evaluation across backbones and tasks.
Urbr8CilRa.main_concern: Reviewers question the reported sign-canonicalization ablation because simultaneous singular-vector sign flips should leave the formulated gated updates unchanged.

WNp9qjh5CF.one_liner: PAM jointly denoises a timing-free joint-space path sketch and an executable action chunk with directed sketch-to-action attention.
WNp9qjh5CF.problem: Short action chunks lack long-horizon guidance, while visual plans require motion translation and dense timed trajectories are costly or redundant.
WNp9qjh5CF.method: PAM jointly generates an arc-length-parameterized sketch of the remaining joint-space path and a dense action chunk within one transformer denoiser. Block-causal attention and staggered denoising make action tokens depend on a progressively cleaner sketch.
WNp9qjh5CF.key_idea: Represent remaining motion by arc length rather than time and direct denoising dependencies from the path sketch to executable action tokens.
WNp9qjh5CF.evidence: Simulation experiments use Push-T and LIBERO-Long, alongside four real-world bimanual tasks and component ablations.
WNp9qjh5CF.claimed_gains: PAM raises success on four real-world bimanual tasks from 47.5% to 75.0%.
WNp9qjh5CF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value compact timing-invariant motion guidance derived directly from demonstrations and the real-world bimanual results.
WNp9qjh5CF.main_concern: Reviewers question the strength of comparative evidence, citing missing uncertainty estimates and simulation baselines taken from other publications.

stjQyihyp6.one_liner: TextVerifier conditions character-crop verification on ideographic structure and learns from same-character pairs with different rendering quality.
stjQyihyp6.problem: OCR and recognition-focused VLMs overlook local Chinese character defects such as missing strokes or malformed components.
stjQyihyp6.method: TextVerifier feeds Ideographic Description Sequences into its text tower and trains on crop-IDS pairs plus label-free hard pairs mined from an inpainting model's training trajectory. Its character-level score also supplies a reward for Flow-GRPO text-generation post-training.
stjQyihyp6.key_idea: Condition verification on a character's compositional structure and contrast same-character crops with differing rendering quality.
stjQyihyp6.evidence: Training uses 12.7M crop-IDS pairs, and TextRenderBench-ZH annotates position, identity, and correctness for 7,358 characters, with training-stage ablations and Flow-GRPO experiments.
stjQyihyp6.claimed_gains: TextVerifier reaches F1 0.844 versus OCR confidence at 0.526, a general VLM at 0.329, and TextPecker at 0.590.
stjQyihyp6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value character-level structural-error evaluation and strong verifier performance supported by training-stage ablations.
stjQyihyp6.main_concern: Reviewers request independent validation of Flow-GRPO gains because TextVerifier serves as both training reward and evaluator.

NB4eU7IvuL.one_liner: Localized anatomical corruptions create preference pairs for region-aware, margin-bounded alignment of human image generators.
NB4eU7IvuL.problem: Preferences between independently generated images confound anatomical quality with unrelated visual differences.
NB4eU7IvuL.method: ASAP creates dispreferred examples by locally degrading verified anatomically plausible anchors, producing HAP pairs with masks and error metadata. Region-aware DPO weights edited areas and regresses the preference gap toward a finite margin.
NB4eU7IvuL.key_idea: Construct anatomy-specific preference pairs by locally corrupting verified anchors and optimize a spatially weighted preference gap toward a finite target.
NB4eU7IvuL.evidence: HAP contains over 10K curated pairs, with reviews describing FLUX and SDXL experiments, vanilla-DPO controls, human evaluation, and Human-Art evaluation.
NB4eU7IvuL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit localized preference data as useful anatomical supervision and report image-quality benefits from the objective.
NB4eU7IvuL.main_concern: Reviewers see limited methodological originality in the objective's combination of established regional weighting and finite-target preference regression.

T1DhlI7kLf.one_liner: Learned graph purification reduces track hypotheses before trajectory-level QUBO optimization for full-detector particle reconstruction.
T1DhlI7kLf.problem: Learning-based particle tracking can generate many fake trajectories, while global trajectory optimization incurs high computational cost.
T1DhlI7kLf.method: ML-QTrack uses learning-based graph purification to reduce the candidate hypothesis space before trajectory-level QUBO optimization. A subsequent refinement stage merges duplicate trajectories and reconnects fragments.
T1DhlI7kLf.key_idea: Prune candidate tracking hypotheses with learned graph purification before solving a trajectory-level quadratic binary optimization problem.
T1DhlI7kLf.evidence: Evaluation uses full-event, full-detector TrackML and an HGNN-based comparator with the same candidate graph, plus purification and optimization ablations.
T1DhlI7kLf.claimed_gains: The abstract reports 97.7% efficiency, a fake-rate reduction from 36.71% to 6.11%, and reconstruction in 2.68 s per event.
T1DhlI7kLf.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit the practical combination of learned hypothesis reduction with global tracking optimization.
T1DhlI7kLf.main_concern: The evaluation does not isolate QUBO's benefit from duplicate suppression and fragment recovery in post-processing.

k54NObHKuy.one_liner: Calibrated multi-source sequence probabilities set completion-specific baselines for pointwise preference updates.
k54NObHKuy.problem: Fusing heterogeneous language-model capabilities is difficult when parameter spaces differ and constructed preference pairs are unreliable.
k54NObHKuy.method: CGPO calibrates source-model sequence probabilities into a consensus baseline for each completion. Pointwise verifier labels determine desirable and undesirable responses, enabling alignment without paired preferences or parameter merging.
k54NObHKuy.key_idea: Use confidence-calibrated source consensus as a completion-specific optimization baseline while verifier feedback sets pointwise preference-update directions.
k54NObHKuy.evidence: Experiments compare fusion and preference-optimization baselines on seven mathematics, coding, reasoning, and instruction-following benchmarks.
k54NObHKuy.claimed_gains: For Phi-3.5, the abstract reports an increase in average benchmark performance from 58.1 to 63.3.
k54NObHKuy.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit the practical value of unpaired supervision for combining heterogeneous models' capabilities.
k54NObHKuy.main_concern: Inconsistent source-free ablations leave the size of the consensus mechanism's contribution unclear.

4NclmaSYhs.one_liner: Norm-dependent tangent filtering modifies momentum before Muon's Newton–Schulz orthogonalization during LLM pretraining.
4NclmaSYhs.problem: Muon momentum can contain weight-aligned components that the paper hypothesizes are locally redundant.
4NclmaSYhs.method: TMuon filters momentum using tangent projection before feeding it into Newton–Schulz orthogonalization. Its norm-dependent formulation changes the filtering according to local weight geometry.
4NclmaSYhs.key_idea: Apply norm-dependent tangent filtering to momentum before Newton–Schulz orthogonalization constructs the update direction.
4NclmaSYhs.evidence: Pretraining experiments cover LLaMA and Qwen3, dense and mixture-of-experts configurations, and runs with up to 150B tokens.
4NclmaSYhs.claimed_gains: On Qwen3-1.7B with a 150B-token budget, the abstract reports a 2.3 percentage-point average benchmark accuracy improvement over Muon.
4NclmaSYhs.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit the simple, inexpensive modification and improvements across architectures and training scales.
4NclmaSYhs.main_concern: The experiments do not directly validate that removing weight-aligned momentum explains the gains rather than normalization or effective learning-rate changes.

0hmFgwiM0E.one_liner: FID on decoded nearest-neighbor latent interpolations predicts downstream diffusion generation quality across autoencoders.
0hmFgwiM0E.problem: VAE reconstruction FID correlates poorly with the generation FID of latent diffusion models.
0hmFgwiM0E.method: iFID retrieves each sample's nearest latent neighbor, interpolates the pair, decodes the result, and computes FID against the original dataset. The paper relates this metric to diffusion generalization through theoretical intuition and examples.
0hmFgwiM0E.key_idea: Compute FID between original data and decoded interpolations of nearest-neighbor latent pairs.
0hmFgwiM0E.evidence: The benchmark includes 22 pretrained VAEs, 15 VAE metrics, and 44 class-conditional diffusion models trained on ImageNet.
0hmFgwiM0E.claimed_gains: The abstract reports Pearson and Spearman correlations with generation FID of approximately 0.85.
0hmFgwiM0E.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit the metric's simplicity, practical motivation, and broad empirical benchmark.
0hmFgwiM0E.main_concern: Aggregate correlations may reflect differences between VAE families and do not establish reliable within-family model selection.

A1usOfvvW4.one_liner: Counterfactual pruning previews calibrate Gaussian importance using the surviving representation's geometric response.
A1usOfvvW4.problem: Importance-based Gaussian pruning ignores how retained primitives adapt to removed information during subsequent optimization.
A1usOfvvW4.method: RAGP probes localized Gaussian removal and measures geometric responses in surviving primitives. It whitens these responses and combines them with the host importance prior using bounded relative calibration at a fixed pruning budget.
A1usOfvvW4.key_idea: Measure surviving Gaussians' geometric responses to localized removals and fuse whitened responses with existing importance scores through bounded calibration.
A1usOfvvW4.evidence: Controlled recovery and freezing interventions examine recoverability, while reviews report matched-count comparisons across five pruning budgets and seven importance criteria.
A1usOfvvW4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit the recoverability motivation and consistent rendering improvements across existing pruning criteria.
A1usOfvvW4.main_concern: The link between geometric gradient responses and post-pruning recoverability remains indirect and insufficiently separated from ordinary importance refinement.

TuKBgf6dZr.one_liner: Consensus-trained reranking selects repeated video events between candidate retrieval and temporal-boundary refinement.
TuKBgf6dZr.problem: Single-occurrence grounding methods and incomplete annotations miss repeated query-matching events in long videos.
TuKBgf6dZr.method: AO-Bench provides human-refined annotations for all matching temporal spans, and ReGround retrieves, reranks, and refines candidate clips. Its reranker trains on AOVTG-66K labels produced by iterative multi-agent assessment and filtered consensus.
TuKBgf6dZr.key_idea: Train a clip reranker on filtered multi-agent consensus labels, then refine boundaries for all query-matching candidates.
TuKBgf6dZr.evidence: Experiments on AO-Bench evaluate multi-occurrence grounding, single-occurrence performance, and inference cost relative to the multi-agent pipeline.
TuKBgf6dZr.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the repeated-occurrence grounding problem and AO-Bench's human-refined annotations.
TuKBgf6dZr.main_concern: Reviewers find limited technical originality in the established retrieve–rerank–refine pipeline.

rLCDWYf6Yu.one_liner: Calibration tokens and Jacobian-based attention bias combine fisheye and pinhole views for compact metric-depth estimation.
rLCDWYf6Yu.problem: Real-time depth estimation must reconcile different camera projections while retaining metric scale and limiting computation.
rLCDWYf6Yu.method: X-Lens uses calibration tokens for coarse projective alignment and a Jacobian-parameterized distortion bias in cross-attention. It predicts dense depth and a global metric scale from a variable number of views.
rLCDWYf6Yu.key_idea: Use calibration tokens for lens adaptation and Jacobian distortion bias in cross-attention to combine heterogeneous camera features.
rLCDWYf6Yu.evidence: Training uses public datasets and synthetic OmniScene, with evaluations on OmniScene, real fisheye and pinhole benchmarks, and deployment demonstrations.
rLCDWYf6Yu.claimed_gains: The abstract reports 0.04B parameters and up to 41 FPS, with 25.4% lower AbsRel on OmniScene-Full and 88.9% fewer parameters than the strongest baseline.
rLCDWYf6Yu.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit the geometry-aware camera formulation and the compact implementation supported by OmniScene.
rLCDWYf6Yu.main_concern: Cross-camera generalization is insufficiently established because training exposure differs across baselines and real mixed-camera depth accuracy is unreported.

3xENsJ0wQl.one_liner: Explicit 3D part extraction, isolated editing, and boundary refinement control local texture and shape changes.
3xENsJ0wQl.problem: Existing 3D editors select regions imprecisely and lack decoupled texture and geometry editing while preserving surrounding content.
3xENsJ0wQl.method: Inlay3D selects an explicit target part from 3D candidates using a lightweight 2D mask. It edits a part-isolated representation and refines the boundary to integrate the result with the remaining asset.
3xENsJ0wQl.key_idea: Extract a target 3D part from mask-guided candidates, edit it in isolation, and refine its boundary with the untouched asset.
3xENsJ0wQl.evidence: Reviews describe part-localization evaluation across eight categories and texture/geometry editing comparisons, including full-mesh inpainting controls.
3xENsJ0wQl.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit reported localization and editing performance, including boundary integration that preserves non-target regions.
3xENsJ0wQl.main_concern: Component-wise ablations do not sufficiently justify the pipeline's stages or quantitatively establish boundary-refinement benefits.

How3ivYLwf.one_liner: ROI-profile masking and low-rank subject regularization support functional-connectivity classification under label scarcity.
How3ivYLwf.problem: Small, heterogeneous functional-connectivity datasets limit diagnosis models, and the benefit of foundation-model transfer under label scarcity is unclear.
How3ivYLwf.method: The paper benchmarks language, vision, and neuroimaging foundation models under several adaptation protocols. BrainLRR combines ROI-profile masking with low-rank regularization of subject representations for task-specific classification.
How3ivYLwf.key_idea: Mask ROI connectivity profiles and impose low-rank regularization on subject representations during supervised learning.
How3ivYLwf.evidence: Evaluation spans four ASD, Parkinson's, and Alzheimer's classification tasks, with encoder-only controls, label-scarcity sweeps, and transfer to BrainNetCNN.
How3ivYLwf.claimed_gains: The abstract reports that learned alignment improves LLM-based classification mean AUROC from 53.3 to 70.8.
How3ivYLwf.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit the controlled comparisons and evaluation of sample efficiency across clinical tasks.
How3ivYLwf.main_concern: The masking and nuclear-norm regularization choices need stronger justification and clearer distinction from existing regularizers.

rKtKwQilp5.one_liner: Selects target-centric virtual views by Gaussian visibility gain and enforces object-centric semantic axes for multi-granularity 3DGS segmentation.
rKtKwQilp5.problem: Language-guided 3D Gaussian Splatting segmentation struggles across varying query granularities because fixed camera views under-observe fine parts and object-centric spatial relations become ambiguous across viewpoints.
rKtKwQilp5.method: AnyGranGS locates a coarse target proxy to construct target-centric virtual views, selects complementary views via Gaussian visibility gain, and establishes object-centric semantic axis constraints for consistent part localization across views. It then aggregates multi-view masks from an MLLM using visibility-weighted Gaussian evidence to refine the 3D target segmentation.
rKtKwQilp5.key_idea: Generates target-focused virtual cameras selected by marginal Gaussian visibility coverage and applies object-centric semantic coordinate axes to resolve cross-view spatial ambiguity before visibility-weighted mask aggregation.
rKtKwQilp5.evidence: Evaluated on Gran-LERF, Gran-3D-OVS, and Ref-LERF benchmarks.
rKtKwQilp5.claimed_gains: Improves average mIoU over the strongest baselines by 15.37, 21.61, and 12.58 points on Gran-LERF, Gran-3D-OVS, and Ref-LERF, respectively.
rKtKwQilp5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that adaptive target-centric view construction and object-centric spatial disambiguation address concrete failure modes in fine-grained and part-level 3DGS segmentation.
rKtKwQilp5.main_concern: Baseline comparisons do not control for the underlying MLLM backbone (using Gemini-3.6-Flash while baselines use weaker models), and ablations are limited to a single scene with unexplained table discrepancies.

d8YA40OtHW.one_liner: Benchmarks token-probability, numerical verbal, and linguistic verbal uncertainty estimation across 80 large language models on MMLU-Pro.
d8YA40OtHW.problem: Deploying large language models in high-stakes settings requires reliable uncertainty estimation, but the relative effectiveness of single-pass uncertainty expression methods across model scales, architectures, and reasoning modes remains poorly understood.
d8YA40OtHW.method: The authors evaluate 80 open- and closed-source LLMs (from 0.6B to 671B parameters, including dense, MoE, reasoning, non-reasoning, and quantized variants) on MMLU-Pro. They compare three black-box single-pass methods—token probability-based uncertainty (TPU), numerical verbal uncertainty (NVU), and linguistic verbal uncertainty (LVU)—on calibration and selective classification.
d8YA40OtHW.key_idea: Systematically compares single-pass token-probability, numerical verbal, and linguistic verbal uncertainty expressions across 80 LLMs varying in scale, architecture, quantization, and reasoning mode.
d8YA40OtHW.evidence: Evaluated across 80 LLMs spanning 0.6B to 671B parameters on the MMLU-Pro benchmark using an LLM judge for linguistic uncertainty.
d8YA40OtHW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that benchmarking uncertainty quantification across 80 models comparing linguistic, numerical, and token-probability methods provides a useful empirical reference.
d8YA40OtHW.main_concern: All experiments rely on a single multiple-choice benchmark (MMLU-Pro), and several analytical claims in the text—such as reasoning mode improving uncertainty independently of accuracy—are confounded or unsupported by the data.

IBHE5Nj61C.one_liner: Curates an 80K region-annotated artifact dataset and supervises MLLM region-level attention for explainable AI-generated image detection.
IBHE5Nj61C.problem: Existing AI-generated image detectors lack interpretability and generalize poorly to unseen generators, while standard MLLM fine-tuning can exploit off-region visual shortcuts and fabricate explanations for target regions.
IBHE5Nj61C.method: The authors build Fake-Reason, an 80K-sample dataset spanning early GANs, diffusion models, and modern generators with fine-grained artifact explanations and bounding boxes. They fine-tune a lightweight open-source MLLM using region-level attention supervision that aligns the attention of each explanation with its annotated bounding box.
IBHE5Nj61C.key_idea: Aligns MLLM explanation attention maps directly with ground-truth artifact bounding boxes during fine-tuning on an 80K multi-era synthetic image dataset to prevent off-region visual shortcuts.
IBHE5Nj61C.evidence: Evaluated on Fake-Reason and external detection benchmarks including Synthbuster and GenImage.
IBHE5Nj61C.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the Fake-Reason dataset design—including bounding boxes, real-image regional descriptions, and label-only supervision for subtle modern generators—and attention supervision are thoughtful contributions.
IBHE5Nj61C.main_concern: The paper quantitatively evaluates binary classification accuracy but lacks direct quantitative metrics, human audits, or causal verification for explanation accuracy and bounding-box localization.

qK9P3oMLVo.one_liner: Evaluates memory usage in vision-language-action models via counterfactual retrieval interventions and a history-dependent benchmark.
qK9P3oMLVo.problem: Aggregate success-rate ablations in vision-language-action systems conflate computation changes with information use and hide whether decisions actually rely on specific task-relevant stored facts.
qK9P3oMLVo.method: The Interventional Memory Evaluation Protocol (IMEP) intervenes at the retrieval interface by comparing target-fact substitutions against fact-preserving replacements, minimal one-unit-in-the-last-place numerical perturbations, and exact replicas while separating decision correctness from motor execution. The authors also introduce ChainBench to test decisions requiring historical information unavailable in current observations across within-episode, cross-episode, and agentic memory systems.
qK9P3oMLVo.key_idea: Applies paired retrieval-interface interventions—comparing target-fact edits against fact-preserving replacements and minimal numerical perturbations—to isolate factual attribution from behavioral sensitivity in robot memory.
qK9P3oMLVo.evidence: Evaluated on within-episode, cross-episode learned-bank, and agentic memory VLA systems across tasks including ChainBench and Remember Color.
qK9P3oMLVo.claimed_gains: In cross-episode learned-bank experiments, a one-unit-in-the-last-place intervention changes 11.9% of seed-paired outcomes, while changing key facts produces no clear additional effect over fact-preserving replacements.
qK9P3oMLVo.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that distinguishing aggregate performance improvement from paired behavioral sensitivity and specific factual reliance is a valuable conceptual refinement for evaluating robot memory.
qK9P3oMLVo.main_concern: In learned-memory experiments, incomplete semantic validation and task design issues (such as re-observing the target cue) make it difficult to separate memory failures from intervention delivery failures.

73gQwMKbQl.one_liner: Couples capacity-constrained optimal transport patch matching with transport-variance residual calibration for training-free few-shot industrial anomaly detection.
73gQwMKbQl.problem: Independent patch retrieval in few-shot industrial anomaly detection permits unrestricted reuse of normal reference patches and mixes defect residuals with association ambiguity and normal appearance drift.
73gQwMKbQl.method: GOMC-AD enforces prescribed normal reference capacities and a fixed rejection budget via optimal transport to obtain both a normal reference plan and its association variance. It adds association variance to predictive residual scoring, subtracts its modeled contribution during online historical second-moment updates, and uses reference-preserving feedback to refine rejection.
73gQwMKbQl.key_idea: Uses capacity-constrained optimal transport with a rejection budget to jointly allocate normal reference patches and derives transport association variance to calibrate both anomaly scoring and online moment updates.
73gQwMKbQl.evidence: Evaluated under causal online and static settings on MVTec AD, VisA, and Real-IAD across 1-, 2-, and 4-shot support.
73gQwMKbQl.claimed_gains: Achieves the highest reported mean image- and pixel-level AUROC across all 18 settings among listed online configurations, with gains reaching 3.8 and 0.9 percentage points, respectively.
73gQwMKbQl.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that constraining reference patch reuse via shared capacities and using a unified transport variance decomposition for scoring and online updates is well reasoned.
73gQwMKbQl.main_concern: Ablations bundle multiple modifications into OT-GMA without isolating the shared-capacity constraint or variance subtraction individually, and direct comparisons with closely related OT-based anomaly detectors like FGPT and FOCT are missing.

NTEyoXZUdw.one_liner: Optimizes nonsmooth, nonconvex functionals over probability measures on Hilbert spaces using gradient-free stochastic control particle feedback.
NTEyoXZUdw.problem: Optimizing nonconvex and nonsmooth functionals over probability measures on infinite-dimensional spaces using only objective evaluations is difficult when the optimal measure is non-Dirac or multimodal.
NTEyoXZUdw.method: SCMO formulates measure optimization via entropy-regularized stochastic control and applies finite-particle and Galerkin approximations with a Cole-Hopf transform to express optimal feedback as a Gibbs-weighted terminal displacement. It approximates this feedback by sampling context clouds, replacing single particles with candidate draws, scoring empirical measures, and applying exponential reweighting with matched or nonmatched proposal and update covariances.
NTEyoXZUdw.key_idea: Approximates Cole-Hopf optimal control feedback over empirical measures on Hilbert spaces by exponentially reweighting single-particle candidate replacements across sampled context clouds using only objective evaluations.
NTEyoXZUdw.evidence: Supported by convergence and error-bound theorems for matched and nonmatched covariances, and experiments on function-space, trajectory-law, and contact-rich manipulation tasks.
NTEyoXZUdw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that extending stochastic-control-based derivative-free measure optimization to infinite-dimensional function spaces is mathematically principled and supported by thorough theoretical analysis.
NTEyoXZUdw.main_concern: The paper is dense and difficult to read with weak practical motivation, closely follows Qiu (2026), and uses near-zero temperatures in experiments without comparing against simple random-replacement search baselines.

JduaNIDbtl.one_liner: Shows that sensory signal geometry rather than sensory modality determines the spatial reference frame learned by predictive recurrent networks.
JduaNIDbtl.problem: Predictive recurrent network models of hippocampal spatial representations typically test vision alone, leaving unclear how multiple senses with different dependencies on position and heading shape the learned reference frame.
JduaNIDbtl.method: The authors train recurrent networks receiving first-person vision, binaural audio from four speakers, or both, alongside self-motion, to predict sensory inputs one second ahead in a virtual arena. They measure unit spatial allocentricity across headings and perform causal interventions by rearranging speaker geometry, removing interaural level differences, and manipulating prediction targets while holding inputs fixed.
JduaNIDbtl.key_idea: Intervenes on spatial cue geometry and prediction targets across visual and binaural auditory predictive RNNs to test whether heading invariance depends on target signal geometry rather than sensory modality.
JduaNIDbtl.evidence: Evaluated on 400-unit recurrent networks trained across 5 seeds in a virtual arena with visual and four-speaker binaural auditory inputs under speaker rearrangement, ILD removal, and oracle target manipulations.
JduaNIDbtl.claimed_gains: Audition networks became far more allocentric than vision networks, with median allocentricity of 0.677 ± 0.010 versus 0.363 ± 0.033.
JduaNIDbtl.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the research question is clear and the interventions—such as rearranging speakers and manipulating prediction targets while fixing inputs—are cleanly designed.
JduaNIDbtl.main_concern: Because frozen sensory encoders feed into a single recurrent network without modality-specific structure, the distinction between signal geometry and sensory modality holds almost by construction, and experiments are limited to a single 400-unit sigmoid RNN trained with L1 loss.

JfRO7fRy3h.one_liner: Caps early classifier-free guidance residual strength when null and conditional branches are weakly aligned in masked diffusion language models.
JfRO7fRy3h.problem: During initial sampling in masked diffusion language models, limited response context causes the null-prompt prediction to align weakly with the conditional branch and produces elevated classifier-free guidance residuals that impair generation.
JfRO7fRy3h.method: The authors characterize early sampling via branch alignment and relative residual strength, and evaluate two training-free adaptive controls: Adaptive on/off, which disables early guidance residuals, and AdaptiveCap, which retains the residual direction while capping its magnitude using a prompt-specific reference. Both methods revert to standard classifier-free guidance once branch similarity crosses a threshold.
JfRO7fRy3h.key_idea: Rescales the classifier-free guidance residual magnitude during early masked diffusion decoding steps using a prompt-specific cap until conditional and unconditional branch similarity reaches a threshold.
JfRO7fRy3h.evidence: Evaluated across two masked diffusion language models, three benchmarks (including MMLU and MATH-500), and five guidance scales, alongside comparisons with image generators.
JfRO7fRy3h.claimed_gains: AdaptiveCap improves or matches Full CFG across two models, three benchmarks, and five guidance scales, with gains of up to 7.1 percentage points.
JfRO7fRy3h.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the empirical characterization of early-stage CFG instability in masked diffusion language models is clear and the proposed training-free guidance capping is easy to apply.
JfRO7fRy3h.main_concern: The adaptive controls closely mirror existing continuous-diffusion guidance rescaling methods, lack comparisons against simple non-adaptive ramp-up schedules, and rely on a logit-norm metric that is not invariant to softmax-preserving logit shifts.

SoGnGEnHN3.one_liner: Audits protein backbone generators via domain-level retrieval rates and a training-free domain-assembly baseline to separate combinatorial from structural novelty.
SoGnGEnHN3.problem: Evaluating generated protein backbones by low full-chain similarity to known proteins conflates genuinely new folds with recombined assemblies of existing structural domains.
SoGnGEnHN3.method: The authors introduce the Domain Retrieval Rate (DRR), measuring the fraction of generated backbones containing any constituent domain matching CATH S40, and evaluate eight diffusion and flow-matching protein generators. They also build RetFold, a zero-training baseline that retrieves CATH domains and connects them via geometry-based helix-linker optimization to calibrate standard designability and full-chain novelty metrics.
SoGnGEnHN3.key_idea: Measures constituent domain matches against CATH S40 via Domain Retrieval Rate and benchmarks against a zero-training domain-retrieval and helix-linker assembly pipeline.
SoGnGEnHN3.evidence: Evaluated across eight diffusion and flow-matching protein backbone generation models (including ProtPardelle and FrameDiff) against CATH S40.
SoGnGEnHN3.claimed_gains: RetFold matches the designability and full-chain novelty of learned generators while running over two orders of magnitude faster on CPU alone.
SoGnGEnHN3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that exposing the flaw of query-normalized full-chain TM-score searches against domain databases and calibrating novelty metrics with the simple RetFold retrieval baseline is a valuable critical contribution.
SoGnGEnHN3.main_concern: Table 6 exhibits a non-monotonicity error where stricter TM thresholds report higher retrieval rates, and DRR only requires a single matching domain without providing a comprehensive positive prescription for measuring useful structural novelty.

Ira9Ki6nJG.one_liner: Aggregates multi-view geometry via VGGT-Omega and predicts next-step wrist-view latent tokens conditioned on shared latent actions for VLA learning.
Ira9Ki6nJG.problem: Existing latent world models for Vision-Language-Action learning encode camera views independently and predict holistic scene dynamics without modeling cross-view geometric relationships, hurting robustness under visual shifts.
Ira9Ki6nJG.method: GWM-VLA uses VGGT-Omega to aggregate multi-view observations at each timestep into geometry-aware states and trains a latent world model to predict next-step wrist-view patch tokens from aggregated patch and register tokens. Shared latent-action representations condition both the latent world model and a flow-matching action head under joint latent-prediction and robot-action supervision.
Ira9Ki6nJG.key_idea: Uses multi-view geometry-aware tokens from VGGT-Omega to predict next-step wrist-camera latent tokens while sharing latent-action conditioning between the world model and the flow-matching action head.
Ira9Ki6nJG.evidence: Evaluated on LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus out-of-distribution settings, and real-world robotic manipulation tasks.
Ira9Ki6nJG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that integrating multi-view geometric foundation model representations into latent world modeling and targeting wrist-view prediction is a well-motivated approach for improving VLA robustness.
Ira9Ki6nJG.main_concern: Comparisons with VLA-JEPA are confounded by VGGT-Omega's large-scale multi-view pretraining, single-view wrist prediction underutilizes multi-view geometry supervision, and fixed wrist-view selection may not generalize across manipulation tasks.

tGtktyX28E.one_liner: Rectifies physically invalid driving trajectories before rendering multi-view driving videos using a heterogeneous real-and-simulated physics dataset.
tGtktyX28E.problem: Driving video world models trained on nominal real-world logs fail and generate severe physical artifacts when conditioned on counterfactual or physics-violating trajectories from imperfect planners or simulators.
tGtktyX28E.method: PhyGenesis combines a physical condition generator that rectifies potentially invalid trajectory inputs into physically plausible conditions with a physics-enhanced multi-view video generator. Both modules are trained on a heterogeneous dataset mixing real-world driving videos with challenging driving scenarios and physics supervision signals generated in the CARLA simulator.
tGtktyX28E.key_idea: Decouples trajectory rectification from multi-view video synthesis and trains both stages on combined real driving logs and extreme CARLA simulation scenarios.
tGtktyX28E.evidence: Evaluated on nuScenes and style-transferred CARLA challenging trajectory benchmarks against driving video generators including UniMLVG, MagicDrive-v2, and DiST-4D.
tGtktyX28E.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that handling physics-violating or imperfect trajectory inputs is an important practical bottleneck for driving world models and that decoupling trajectory correction from video generation is sensible.
tGtktyX28E.main_concern: Baselines are general-purpose driving video generators rather than safety-critical or physics-aware models (such as SafeMVDrive, Challenger, or GenieDrive), and style-transferring CARLA clips to nuScenes for FID/FVD introduces synthetic evaluation bias.

wNt5C5X58Y.one_liner: Identifies and benchmarks endogenous authorization laundering where an LLM agent's memory writer turns history into false permissions.
wNt5C5X58Y.problem: Long-running LLM agents that track evolving permissions in persistent memory can misinterpret or fail to update authorization state, creating false authority that leads executors to take unauthorized actions without any external attack.
wNt5C5X58Y.method: The authors formalize endogenous authorization laundering and construct EAL-Bench, a deterministic ledger-backed benchmark covering procurement, cybersecurity, and finance tasks. They evaluate seven LLM memory writers and two calibrated executors across incremental typed and free-text memory updates, and test exact-state memory repair and memory-level safeguards.
wNt5C5X58Y.key_idea: Evaluates persistent agent memory as an effective authorization surface by separating false-authority formation during incremental memory writing from unauthorized execution using a deterministic permission ledger.
wNt5C5X58Y.evidence: Evaluated across seven LLM memory writers and two LLM executors on EAL-Bench spanning 36 synthetic histories and 132 request pairs in procurement, cybersecurity, and finance.
wNt5C5X58Y.claimed_gains: Under incremental typed-memory updates, writers create false authority for up to 45.4% of unauthorized requests, and once present, calibrated executors act on it in 99.0% of matched memory-only trials.
wNt5C5X58Y.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating false-authority formation in memory from downstream execution and using a deterministic ledger with exact-state repair interventions cleanly isolates a practical agent safety risk.
wNt5C5X58Y.main_concern: The benchmark is small (36 synthetic histories) with pooled correlated trials and no uncertainty intervals, and high execution propagation is expected when executors only see corrupted memory without original history or independent permission checks.

Qf8pqpxUwV.one_liner: Constructs label-flipped image pairs with bit-identical fixed-point downscaled tensors via integer lattices to certify visual information loss in VLMs.
Qf8pqpxUwV.problem: Vision-language verifiers and test-time compute routers cannot easily distinguish reasoning errors from cases where required visual evidence was erased during image preprocessing.
Qf8pqpxUwV.method: AliasForge exploits the fact that fixed-point image resampling acts as an exact integer linear map before rounding, using integer lattice criteria to find 8-bit bounded perturbations in the resampler's null space that flip semantic step-correctness labels while producing bit-identical model input tensors. The authors screen 20 resize configurations to classify constructibility and test verifiers and compute routers on the resulting certified collision pairs.
Qf8pqpxUwV.key_idea: Embeds label-flipping visual perturbations into the integer lattice null space of fixed-point image downscalers to generate image pairs with opposite ground-truth labels but bit-identical VLM input tensors.
Qf8pqpxUwV.evidence: Supported by theoretical null-vector bounds across 20 resize configurations (17 constructible, 3 non-constructible), certified collision pairs across three VLM architectures, and router evaluations.
Qf8pqpxUwV.claimed_gains: Resolves all 20 screened resize configurations (17 constructible, 3 non-constructible) and proves that every verifier achieves an average accuracy of exactly one half on certified pairs.
Qf8pqpxUwV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the mathematical formulation using integer lattices and the data processing inequality provides a rigorous way to construct exact preprocessing collisions and certify information loss.
Qf8pqpxUwV.main_concern: Certified collisions only exist for integer downscale ratios under fixed-point bicubic resampling using synthetic stripe patterns, rarely apply to natural image resolutions, and fail to explain why routers with full item identity still underperform.

3dMNKs8ZSs.one_liner: Proves that a two-head transformer learns depth-generalizing depth-first tree search via policy-gradient RL under a depth-wise curriculum.
3dMNKs8ZSs.problem: We lack a theoretical understanding of how transformer policies acquire exploration, failure memory, and backtracking search behaviors from reinforcement learning training dynamics.
3dMNKs8ZSs.method: The authors study a stylized two-head transformer interacting with a stochastic k-ary tree environment with sparse terminal rewards, showing how one head tracks past actions while the second detects failures to trigger backtracking. They analyze policy-gradient training dynamics under a depth-1 to depth-2 curriculum and prove the staged emergence of randomized and return-discounted ranked depth-first search.
3dMNKs8ZSs.key_idea: Analyzes policy-gradient dynamics on a two-head attention architecture under a depth-1-to-2 curriculum to show one head learns action history tracking while the other learns failure-triggered backtracking.
3dMNKs8ZSs.evidence: Supported by theoretical construction and policy-gradient training dynamics proofs on stochastic k-ary trees.
3dMNKs8ZSs.claimed_gains: After training only on depth-1 and depth-2 trees, the policy generalizes to deeper full trees.
3dMNKs8ZSs.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the theoretical construction and staged policy-gradient dynamics analysis showing why depth-1 training fails and depth-2 training enables depth-generalizing DFS are clear and insightful.
3dMNKs8ZSs.main_concern: The model relies on a heavily stylized two-head transformer with predefined head roles (one restricted to actions, one to labels) and an environment that forbids repeated actions, leaving a large gap to real LLM reasoning post-training.

FgGtPDr18J.one_liner: Synthesizes executable high-level programs and minimal closed semantic state abstractions from neural systems using counterexample-guided verification.
FgGtPDr18J.problem: Semantic variables extracted from a neural network may predict outputs without retaining sufficient state information to close under transition updates and form an independently executable high-level program.
FgGtPDr18J.method: The authors formalize minimal auxiliary-state selection for transition closure, proving NP-completeness in general while giving a verifiable dependency-graph condition for a unique least admissible state. They use state-pair and single-state counterexamples to separate state insufficiency from program class inexpressibility and synthesize affine-template executable abstractions with bounded verification calls and certified finite-execution error bounds.
FgGtPDr18J.key_idea: Uses state-pair versus single-state counterexamples to distinguish state non-closure from template inexpressibility while selecting auxiliary variables that close transition updates for executable program synthesis.
FgGtPDr18J.evidence: Supported by complexity proofs (NP-completeness and p+1 verification call bounds) and experiments on 10 small hand-built and six-dimensional polynomial networks.
FgGtPDr18J.claimed_gains: For a fixed template affine in its p unknown coefficients, exact synthesis requires at most p+1 verification calls.
FgGtPDr18J.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating state insufficiency (closure under updates) from program formula inexpressibility is a sharp formal distinction supported by solid complexity results.
FgGtPDr18J.main_concern: The framework is only tested on tiny six-dimensional polynomial networks with fixed coordinate projections rather than real neural models or pretrained transformers, where required Lipschitz and verification certificates are unavailable.

T5pU0erow3.one_liner: Executes LLM attention directly over pair-packed reduced-precision KV blocks under GPU memory pressure before asynchronous restoration to target fidelity.
T5pU0erow3.problem: LLM serving runtimes typically require KV caches to reside at full target fidelity before execution, turning GPU memory shortages into request stalls and preemptions.
T5pU0erow3.method: ElasticKV decouples execution from target KV fidelity by introducing a compact intermediate KV state managed inside a paged serving runtime. It combines a pair-structured page layout that packs two reduced-precision base blocks to free physical GPU blocks, a dual-mode attention backend that directly consumes the compact state, and pressure-aware fidelity control.
T5pU0erow3.key_idea: Packs pairs of high-byte reduced-precision KV blocks to free physical GPU pages under memory pressure and executes attention directly on the compact state without waiting for full-precision restoration.
T5pU0erow3.evidence: Implemented in vLLM and evaluated across synthetic, ShareGPT, and production traces on Llama and Qwen models up to 70B across NVIDIA and AMD GPUs.
T5pU0erow3.claimed_gains: Under high concurrency, ElasticKV achieves 2.0-2.6x lower time-to-first-token (TTFT) and 2.5-4.7x lower P90 TTFT than vLLM with KV offloading while preserving generation quality.
T5pU0erow3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the vLLM system implementation—packing reduced-precision pages to reclaim allocator capacity and consuming them directly in attention—is well engineered and thoroughly evaluated across hardware platforms.
T5pU0erow3.main_concern: Static FP8 KV caching in vLLM achieves faster P90 TTFT and higher throughput than ElasticKV with only minor quality drop, and baselines appear configured in a heavy preemption thrashing regime.

2eriOT0qnW.one_liner: Builds a persistent provider-side graph memory of tool capabilities, failure boundaries, and compositions via execution-verified probing for LLM agents.
2eriOT0qnW.problem: Maintaining tool-use knowledge on the agent side via fine-tuning, prompt updates, or agent-private memory prevents sharing across heterogeneous agents and repeats costly tool exploration.
2eriOT0qnW.method: ToolAtlas constructs a persistent provider-side three-layer graph memory capturing tool capabilities, failure boundaries, and cross-tool compositions through capability-guided execution probing. At inference time, downstream LLM agents query this shared provider memory via adaptive graph traversal without retraining or task-time exploration.
2eriOT0qnW.key_idea: Shifts tool memory from individual agents to the tool provider by probing tool executions offline to populate a shared graph of capabilities, failure boundaries, and multi-tool compositions.
2eriOT0qnW.evidence: Evaluated on two MCP-based benchmarks (MCPMark and MCP-Universe) spanning eight tool services, including cross-environment and cross-framework transfer settings.
2eriOT0qnW.claimed_gains: Outperforms tool-side optimization and agent-side memory baselines by up to 21.61% in pass@1 and 18.61% in pass@4, with transfer gains of up to 24.16%/16.22% and 17.49%/14.27% relative pass@1/pass@4.
2eriOT0qnW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that centralizing reusable tool capabilities and failure modes at the tool provider is a practical paradigm for shared MCP tool servers and shows strong cross-agent transfer gains.
2eriOT0qnW.main_concern: Ablations do not isolate provider-side ownership from the three-layer graph design and unmatched offline probing rollouts, nor does the paper address how the static memory handles evolving APIs or permissions.

BnaJK6Bt2v.one_liner: Organizes out-of-order speculative draft tokens into a state-sharing verification lattice for masked diffusion language model decoding.
BnaJK6Bt2v.problem: In speculative decoding for masked diffusion language models, verifying candidates along a fixed draft chain halts at the first ordering mismatch, while verifying all alternative orderings separately incurs excessive compute overhead.
