h2DNkIovAf.method: EnergyDrive learns an explicit scene-conditioned trajectory energy landscape from expert demonstrations, explores diverse modes via repulsive sampling, and composes modular energies for target speed, drivable area, and collision avoidance at inference.
h2DNkIovAf.key_idea: Models driving planning as an explicit trajectory energy landscape so generation, scoring, and inference-time safety constraints share one composable objective.
h2DNkIovAf.evidence: Evaluated on NAVSIM v2 navhard and HUGSIM benchmarks alongside qualitative energy-landscape visualizations.
h2DNkIovAf.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the unified energy landscape intuitive and note strong closed-loop performance on NAVSIM v2 and HUGSIM.
h2DNkIovAf.main_concern: Reviewers note overlap with prior composable energy planning works, lack of ablations isolating the repulsive sampler, and weak validation of compositional constraint enforcement.

92PBBdTtX5.one_liner: Distills microscopic atomistic simulations into physically constrained macro-step transitions predicting sparse structural edits and elapsed time.
92PBBdTtX5.problem: Atomistic simulations waste compute on low-impact microscopic updates before reaching structurally consequential state transitions.
92PBBdTtX5.method: AtomWorld-Mirror distills short micro-event segments into latent macro-step dynamics that jointly predict sparse structural edits and continuous physical duration under reachability, inventory conservation, and time-consistency constraints.
92PBBdTtX5.key_idea: Replaces micro-event replay with a latent macro-step world model predicting constrained sparse atomic edits and accumulated physical time.
92PBBdTtX5.evidence: Evaluated across five atomic systems including Cu-rich RPV steel, Cu-Zr metallic glass, and Li3N solid electrolyte against MD/KMC teachers.
92PBBdTtX5.claimed_gains: Delivers a speedup of 10^3 to 10^4x (abstract truncated; 10^3-10^4x cited in review) over microscopic simulation.
92PBBdTtX5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the cross-domain application of macro-step world modeling with physical constraints to atomistic simulation well-motivated and promising.
92PBBdTtX5.main_concern: Reviewers highlight untested out-of-distribution generalization beyond fixed teacher regimes, insufficient validation of long-term transition statistics, and complex seven-term loss tuning.

CR7n3PKdwG.one_liner: Derives sub-Gaussian concentration bounds and worst-case error-accumulation lower bounds for the Gram-Schmidt Walk under finite-precision arithmetic.
CR7n3PKdwG.problem: Exact-arithmetic guarantees for the Gram-Schmidt Walk break down in finite precision because small numerical errors alter which coordinates freeze.
CR7n3PKdwG.method: The authors analyze perturbed Gram-Schmidt trajectories directly under bounded, history-dependent errors to derive a modified MGF concentration bound, construct a matching n^2 error-accumulation lower bound, and ablate precision and problem size.
CR7n3PKdwG.key_idea: Bounds sub-Gaussian concentration directly along the perturbed finite-precision trajectory rather than comparing pathwise to an exact execution.
CR7n3PKdwG.evidence: Theoretical upper and lower concentration bounds paired with finite-precision numerical ablations.
CR7n3PKdwG.claimed_gains: Constructs an instance where bounded update errors produce bias of order min{n^2 eps_iter, n}.
CR7n3PKdwG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers commend the direct trajectory-level concentration analysis and tight pairing of upper and lower finite-precision bounds.
CR7n3PKdwG.main_concern: Reviewers point out mismatches between the theoretical assumptions and the provided implementation, plus statement-level notation inconsistencies in key lemmas.

c0Lc7DGIpP.one_liner: Compresses omni-modal LLM tokens via pre-LLM coverage selection and depth-adaptive intra-modal-to-text pruning.
c0Lc7DGIpP.problem: Existing multimodal token compression methods rely on local redundancy or task relevance and make limited use of global cross-layer modality dependencies.
c0Lc7DGIpP.method: OmniRelay combines pre-LLM Saliency-Diversity and Coverage-Aware Compression (SDCC) with within-LLM Depth-Adaptive Relay Compression (DARC). DARC progressively shifts pruning guidance from intra-modal interactions in early layers to text guidance in middle layers before dropping remaining audiovisual tokens in late layers.
c0Lc7DGIpP.key_idea: Shifts token-compression guidance across LLM depth from intra-modal anchors to text attention before removing remaining audiovisual tokens in late layers.
c0Lc7DGIpP.evidence: Attention-knockout analyses and evaluations across 3 Omni-LLMs (including Qwen2.5-Omni-7B) and 5 audiovisual benchmarks support the framework.
c0Lc7DGIpP.claimed_gains: OmniRelay retains 99.51% of full-token performance on Qwen2.5-Omni-7B at 25% layer-averaged audiovisual token retention.
c0Lc7DGIpP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the layer-wise attention-knockout analysis provides a clear mechanistic motivation and that empirical retention across models and benchmarks is strong.
c0Lc7DGIpP.main_concern: Reviewers question novelty over SEATS, lack of ablations isolating gradual depth transitions from fixed switches, and discrepancies between the paper and public code.

qqwATQYvvA.one_liner: Trains latent world models with a shared action-token interface and horizon curriculum to predict variable-length future states.
qqwATQYvvA.problem: One-step latent world models accumulate prediction errors during recursive rollouts over long action sequences.
qqwATQYvvA.method: VLWM conditions a single predictor on variable-length action sequences via shared action tokens, trains with a progressive horizon curriculum, and enables fixed or adaptive chunked rollouts during planning.
qqwATQYvvA.key_idea: Predicts future latent endpoints directly over variable action-sequence horizons using shared action tokens and a cumulative horizon curriculum.
qqwATQYvvA.evidence: Experiments on PushT, OGBench-Cube, TwoRoom, and LIBERO instantiated on both LeWM and DINO-WM backbones across three seeds.
qqwATQYvvA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree variable-length latent prediction improves closed-loop planning across both jointly learned (LeWM) and frozen (DINO-WM) visual representations.
qqwATQYvvA.main_concern: Reviewers note that planning horizons in key controls remain fixed at five model steps and that gains from variable-length prediction are not fully disentangled from the curriculum and planning strategies.

WdGF6pQ0Gj.one_liner: Consolidates fragmented target sounds in an event-level memory and adaptively fuses it with long-term navigation memory.
WdGF6pQ0Gj.problem: Audio-visual navigation struggles when target sounds are brief, fragmented, and intermittent amid competing sounds over long navigation horizons.
WdGF6pQ0Gj.method: TraSNav maintains an event-level memory to accumulate and calibrate fragmented acoustic cues against conflicting sounds, and adaptively fuses this event memory with long-term navigation memory across temporal scales.
WdGF6pQ0Gj.key_idea: Maintains a dedicated event-level memory for transient acoustic evidence and adaptively fuses it with long-term navigation memory to bridge temporal-scale mismatches.
WdGF6pQ0Gj.evidence: Evaluated on multi-source audio-visual navigation benchmarks where target sounds are progressively shortened from 90% to 10% of original duration, with three-run statistics and ablations.
WdGF6pQ0Gj.claimed_gains: Achieves up to a 26.41% relative improvement in success rate when each target-sound event is shortened to 10% of its original duration.
WdGF6pQ0Gj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the well-controlled duration-truncation evaluation protocol and consistent SR/SPL improvements over baselines.
WdGF6pQ0Gj.main_concern: Reviewers question whether truncating sustained sounds models genuinely transient sounds (confounding duration with total signal loss) and note that ablations do not isolate conflict calibration or RTEM.

iRyFCL35zO.one_liner: Combines historical feature extrapolation with a projected current-observation displacement update for training-free diffusion caching.
iRyFCL35zO.problem: Training-free diffusion caching relies on historical residual directions that fail to represent current CFG-weighted residual motion.
iRyFCL35zO.method: MoorCache pairs historical feature prediction with current-observation completion, using an affordable current observation to supply missing directions via a projected displacement update.
iRyFCL35zO.key_idea: Augments historical diffusion caching with a projected displacement update computed from an affordable current-step observation.
iRyFCL35zO.evidence: Supported by secant-coverage and oracle reconstruction analyses plus latency-inclusive experiments across Wan2.1, HunyuanVideo, DiT-XL/2, and FLUX.1-dev against 14 baselines and same-cost ablations.
iRyFCL35zO.claimed_gains: Achieves 2.784x measured speedup with 38.506 dB reference PSNR on HunyuanVideo; on Wan2.1, historical input secants capture 98.9% of input displacement energy versus 2.7% for residual secants.
iRyFCL35zO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the secant-coverage analysis separating coefficient vs. basis error and the broad, latency-inclusive evaluation with same-cost controls.
iRyFCL35zO.main_concern: Reviewers point out that on Wan2.1 and DiT-XL/2 the projection cancels in Eq. (20) reducing to a FasterCache-like update without comparing to FasterCache/ResCa, and the 2.7% statistic is tied to one CFG weight.

WL7BFUUld0.one_liner: Refines natural-language hardware specs into audited Abstract Signal Transition Functions before generating and debugging RTL code.
WL7BFUUld0.problem: LLMs frequently generate incorrect RTL designs because they misinterpret ambiguous natural-language hardware specifications.
WL7BFUUld0.method: VeriRefine translates specifications into schema-constrained Abstract Signal Transition Functions (ASTFs), audits them for coverage, consistency, and design rules, and routes post-generation simulation failures to refine either the ASTF or the RTL.
WL7BFUUld0.key_idea: Enforces an audited, schema-constrained Abstract Signal Transition Function intermediate representation between specification parsing and RTL generation/repair.
WL7BFUUld0.evidence: Evaluations on RTLLM v2.0 and VerilogEval-Human v2 using Claude Sonnet 4.6.
WL7BFUUld0.claimed_gains: Using Claude Sonnet 4.6, VeriRefine achieves 96.0% functional correctness on RTLLM v2.0 and 95.5% on VerilogEval-Human v2, exceeding direct generation by 32.0 and 11.5 percentage points.
WL7BFUUld0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that ASTF is a useful intermediate representation for decoupling hardware semantics from Verilog syntax and yields strong RTLLM results.
WL7BFUUld0.main_concern: Ablations do not isolate individual audit or failure-routing components, VerilogEval uses reference-assisted testbenches, and no anonymous code repository was provided.

zzmLKM1RUb.one_liner: Combines a language-conditioned latent world model and flow-matching trajectory generator for belief-space UAV target search.
zzmLKM1RUb.problem: Semantic UAV exploration systems rely on heuristic frontier scoring rather than predicting future evidence and information gain along candidate trajectories.
zzmLKM1RUb.method: AirWorld maintains a belief over geometry, semantics, and task intention from RGB-D and UAV state, predicts future evidence via an action-conditioned latent world model, generates candidate controls via conditional flow matching, and executes geometrically verified segments.
zzmLKM1RUb.key_idea: Ranks flow-matching UAV control proposals through an action-conditioned latent world model using predicted discovery, coverage, information gain, and risk.
zzmLKM1RUb.evidence: Evaluated on a single-UAV open-vocabulary target search benchmark with component ablations and sampler comparisons.
zzmLKM1RUb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the belief-space predictive control formulation coherent and note that ablations separate language conditioning from predictive ranking (raising success from 84.0% to 92.5%).
zzmLKM1RUb.main_concern: Reviewers point out missing statistical uncertainty for the 3.5-point gain over AirHunt, conflation of world-model and multi-step lookahead benefits in Table 2, and missing architectural details.

4kWaRylmcv.one_liner: Trains LLM agents across multiple reasoning orchestrations using Discounted-UCB bandit routing to allocate rollouts dynamically during RL.
4kWaRylmcv.problem: Training RL agents under a single fixed orchestration (like ReAct) causes overfitting, tool atrophy, and brittle out-of-distribution generalization as policy capabilities evolve.
4kWaRylmcv.method: MORL maintains a fixed pool of structurally diverse orchestrations and uses Discounted-UCB routing (D-MORL) on the policy's reward stream to dynamically allocate rollout budgets across orchestrations during GRPO training.
4kWaRylmcv.key_idea: Treats diverse agent orchestrations as a dynamic RL curriculum, using Discounted-UCB bandit routing over live rewards to reweight rollout allocation as policy skill evolves.
4kWaRylmcv.evidence: Evaluated on seven Search QA benchmarks, embodied planning, and web navigation across multiple model scales (including Qwen2.5-3B-Ins) under matched rollout budgets.
4kWaRylmcv.claimed_gains: Outperforms a rollout-matched single-orchestration baseline by 5.3 exact-match points on average across seven Search QA benchmarks (43.3% vs. 38.0% with Qwen2.5-3B-Ins) and +7.8 on Bamboogle.
4kWaRylmcv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that training across multiple orchestrations rather than a single fixed scaffold addresses a practical limitation and reveals useful failure modes like tool atrophy.
4kWaRylmcv.main_concern: Reviewers note limited algorithmic novelty over standard GRPO + Discounted-UCB, unclear gains of D-UCB over uniform MORL or other bandits, and missing orchestration implementation details.

1At4h6NTZ2.one_liner: Learns lexicographic multi-objective generalized linear bandits with unknown reward variances via layered weighted MLE and elimination.
1At4h6NTZ2.problem: Variance-aware generalized linear bandits typically assume known variances and incur a suboptimal sqrt(dT) variance-independent regret term.
1At4h6NTZ2.method: They propose a layered weighted-MLE variance-aware algorithm with hierarchical objective elimination that avoids prior variance knowledge, plus a computationally efficient online alternative.
1At4h6NTZ2.key_idea: Combines staged weighted-MLE variance estimation with hierarchical cross-objective confidence-radius elimination for lexicographic bandits.
1At4h6NTZ2.evidence: Theoretical regret bounds, synthetic simulations with ten arms and three objectives, and a semi-synthetic real-world experiment.
1At4h6NTZ2.claimed_gains: The MLE-based algorithm achieves a regret bound of O~(d sqrt(sum_{t=1}^T (sigma_t^i)^2) + d) for any objective i in [m], while the online alternative achieves O~(d sqrt(T)).
1At4h6NTZ2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the variance-adaptive regret improvement without prior variance knowledge and the hierarchical elimination design.
1At4h6NTZ2.main_concern: Empirical validation is very limited (small synthetic/semi-synthetic setups, missing baselines), and reviewers note technical issues or heavy assembly of existing components.

jFQZrrDREJ.one_liner: Decomposes two-layer nonlinear test-time training memories into coupled layerwise delta-rule updates for chunkwise parallel execution.
jFQZrrDREJ.problem: Two-layer nonlinear recurrent memories are hard to optimize in a single sequential pass, often underperforming fixed-base parallel test-time training.
jFQZrrDREJ.method: DeltaTTT replaces joint inner-loop optimization of a two-layer memory with layerwise learning, assigning each layer a local prediction target and updating it via a state-dependent delta rule. Constructing the second layer's write address from the first layer's prediction preserves nonlinear readout while enabling chunkwise parallel scans.
jFQZrrDREJ.key_idea: Replaces joint two-layer MLP inner-loop updates with two stacked state-dependent delta-rule regressions for chunkwise parallel execution.
jFQZrrDREJ.evidence: Trained on 92.5B tokens using DeltaNet and LaCT backbones and evaluated on language modeling loss, needle-in-a-haystack retrieval, and training throughput.
jFQZrrDREJ.claimed_gains: Training throughput is 1.37x full attention, and single-needle retrieval improves from 37.87/40.52 to 50.47 on LaCT and 47.60 to 48.78 on DeltaNet (from reviews).
jFQZrrDREJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the layerwise delta-rule decomposition is simple, reuses efficient chunkwise parallel kernels, and improves retrieval on both backbones.
jFQZrrDREJ.main_concern: Reviewers note missing ablations isolating nonlinearity from extra state capacity, unrobust S1-driven motivating evidence, and missed comparison to Trellis.

ERDuxXKUdv.one_liner: Restores single-photon point clouds via reliability-aware local anchor repair and global-local latent flow matching on the SPORE benchmark.
ERDuxXKUdv.problem: Single-photon 3D point clouds suffer from spatially uneven sampling, missing surfaces, and spurious detections, while existing benchmarks lack diverse paired reference geometry.
ERDuxXKUdv.method: The authors introduce SPORE, a ray-based Poisson-photon simulated benchmark across 55 ShapeNet categories and three corruption regimes. They propose PRISM, a hierarchical latent flow-matching framework that selectively repairs unreliable local anchors and conditions global-local restoration on anchor reliability and repair states.
ERDuxXKUdv.key_idea: Selectively repairs unreliable local anchors and propagates their reliability and correction states to condition hierarchical global-local latent point flow matching.
ERDuxXKUdv.evidence: Evaluated on SPORE across Low, Mid, and High corruption regimes with component ablations and a qualitative real-capture demonstration.
ERDuxXKUdv.claimed_gains: On SPORE High corruption, PRISM outperforms the strongest competing metric results by reducing HD95 by 27.6% and improving F@0.01 by 22.9%.
ERDuxXKUdv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the physics-grounded SPORE benchmark fills a real resource gap and PRISM shows strong results under severe simulated corruption.
ERDuxXKUdv.main_concern: Reviewers note PRISM underperforms baselines under mild corruption, relies primarily on synthetic SPORE data without quantitative real-world validation, and shows anomalous F@0.01 behavior.

9ruFBv5tFF.one_liner: Creates free teacher-student asymmetry for visual on-policy distillation by conditioning the student on strongly augmented views of the image.
9ruFBv5tFF.problem: Visual on-policy distillation typically requires a stronger teacher model or privileged annotations like ground-truth answers or bounding boxes.
9ruFBv5tFF.method: S^2VOPD inverts teacher-student asymmetry by conditioning the teacher on the clean original image while training the student on-policy conditioned on a strongly augmented view. The authors systematically evaluate augmentation families, strengths, and compositions without labels or external teachers.
9ruFBv5tFF.key_idea: Generates free on-policy distillation signals by distilling the same model's clean-image distribution into a student conditioned on strongly augmented image views.
9ruFBv5tFF.evidence: Evaluated at 4B and 9B VLM scales across six fine-grained perception benchmarks and three math reasoning benchmarks, with augmentation strength/composition ablations.
9ruFBv5tFF.claimed_gains: S^2VOPD improves average perception accuracy from 70.67 to 77.76 at 4B and from 73.37 to 78.85 at 9B without privileged annotations (from review).
9ruFBv5tFF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the clean-vs-augmented asymmetry is simple, requires no extra labels or larger teachers, and delivers strong empirical gains on perception benchmarks.
9ruFBv5tFF.main_concern: Reviewers flag numerical inconsistencies in reported tables/figures, missing validation-set/seed details, and lack of offline-distillation controls to isolate on-policy benefits.

572c7xu4Mm.one_liner: Introduces the moving-target DANCE navigation task and DyGMap, which decays outdated acoustic-visual goal maps over time.
572c7xu4Mm.problem: Continuous audio-visual navigation assumes stationary targets, causing spatial goal maps to become outdated when sound-emitting targets move or fall silent.
572c7xu4Mm.method: DANCE tasks embodied agents with navigating to moving or stationary targets with intermittent sound in continuous environments. DyGMap couples audio-visual semantic/location estimation with category-specific spatial goal maps that temporally decay outdated or spurious target evidence.
572c7xu4Mm.key_idea: Projects audio-visual target estimates onto category-specific goal maps with temporal decay to suppress outdated evidence from moving targets.
572c7xu4Mm.evidence: Evaluated in clean and noisy continuous environments with unseen scenes, assets, and sound recordings.
572c7xu4Mm.claimed_gains: Outperforms the strongest evaluated baseline by approximately 11.6 percentage points in success rate across clean and noisy settings.
572c7xu4Mm.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the practical DANCE moving-target task formulation and strong overall navigation success rates.
572c7xu4Mm.main_concern: Reviewers point out that ablating the dynamic map decay/timestamp mechanism only drops SR by 1.17-2.31 pp, leaving the core dynamic contribution weakly isolated.

oBb0uicpGo.one_liner: Tests AI peer-review vulnerability by bidirectionally rewriting six rhetorical dimensions of manuscripts while preserving scientific content.
oBb0uicpGo.problem: LLM-based peer reviewers may be vulnerable to rhetorical manipulation even when the underlying scientific content is unchanged.
oBb0uicpGo.method: Constructs 4,200 manuscripts from 120 ICLR 2026 submissions by rewriting six rhetorical dimensions positively and negatively with two LLM rewriters under content-preservation constraints, then evaluates five LLM reviewers under standard and strict protocols.
oBb0uicpGo.key_idea: Applies bidirectional, content-preserving rhetorical rewrites across six dimensions to measure score shifts across multiple LLM reviewers and review protocols.
oBb0uicpGo.evidence: Evaluates 4,200 rewritten manuscripts across five LLM reviewers, human-rating strata, length controls, and a human fidelity audit.
oBb0uicpGo.claimed_gains: Strict review lowers mean overall assessment by 1.36 points, while positive-negative rhetorical contrasts persist.
oBb0uicpGo.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the clean bidirectional experimental design and systematic scale of the study.
oBb0uicpGo.main_concern: Reviewers argue that without human quality ratings of rewrites or a neutral-rewrite control, legitimate writing improvements cannot be separated from reward hacking.

H0IfEcElnx.one_liner: Benchmarks personal AI agent security against adaptive multimodal social engineering attacks across 608 tool-grounded tasks.
H0IfEcElnx.problem: Existing agent security benchmarks focus on text dialogue and overlook social engineering attacks reinforced by forged multimodal artifacts.
H0IfEcElnx.method: Multimodal-SEA provides 608 tasks across 14 domains and 152 Chinese/English attack scenarios in simulated apps where an adaptive attack harness tests agents and scores compromise from verifiable tool execution logs.
H0IfEcElnx.key_idea: Evaluates personal AI agents against adaptive multimodal social engineering in simulated applications with outcomes grounded in verifiable tool execution logs.
H0IfEcElnx.evidence: Evaluation of seven multimodal models across six dimensions and four difficulty levels, plus multimodal artifact ablation.
H0IfEcElnx.claimed_gains: Evaluated models show 7.1% to 34.5% attack success rates, and adding multimodal content raises attack success from 19.9% to 29.2%.
H0IfEcElnx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that evaluating multimodal social engineering grounded in consequential tool-execution logs is timely, comprehensive, and distinct from standard jailbreaks.
H0IfEcElnx.main_concern: Reviewers note that removing multimodal artifacts in the ablation may also remove actionable interfaces or information, confounding the claimed modality effect, alongside missing human realism validation.

sEvSKTZsnZ.one_liner: Computes horizon-specific input importance maps for differentiable time-series forecasters without backbone modification, plus a step-removal evaluation protocol.
sEvSKTZsnZ.problem: Time-series explanation methods typically output a single importance vector, overlooking that different forecast horizons depend on different past lookback positions.
sEvSKTZsnZ.method: HRX adds a horizon axis to explanations via a plug-in estimator that extracts per-step importance maps from shared low-dimensional basis maps, paired with a single-step removal faithfulness protocol and a rank criterion predicting when horizon resolution is needed.
sEvSKTZsnZ.key_idea: Extracts horizon-resolved attribution maps for each forecast step from a few shared basis maps without modifying differentiable forecasting backbones.
sEvSKTZsnZ.evidence: Experiments across multiple forecasting backbones, real datasets, and synthetic datasets with known ground-truth dependencies.
sEvSKTZsnZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the paper well written and appreciate the simple, retraining-free formulation and synthetic-to-real experimental evaluation.
sEvSKTZsnZ.main_concern: Reviewers question the novelty and practical utility of per-step attributions over whole-horizon summaries, noting unaddressed overlap with ChronoSHAP.

17GkLSLtK1.one_liner: Maximizes partial AUC from positive and unlabeled data by rewriting FPR-dependent thresholds and risk using positive and marginal densities.
17GkLSLtK1.problem: Partial AUC maximization methods normally require labeled negative examples, which are often unavailable or costly to annotate in practice.
17GkLSLtK1.method: Within empirical risk minimization, the method expresses pAUC and its FPR-dependent thresholds solely via positive and marginal densities, derives an empirical estimator from positive-unlabeled data, and trains a classifier by maximizing the smoothed estimator.
17GkLSLtK1.key_idea: Rewrites partial AUC and its FPR-dependent thresholds purely in terms of positive and marginal densities for smoothed PU optimization.
17GkLSLtK1.evidence: Finite-sample estimation error analysis and experiments on ten real-world image and tabular datasets.
17GkLSLtK1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the formulation is principled, avoids heuristic pseudo-negative selection, and is backed by finite-sample error bounds and clear presentation.
17GkLSLtK1.main_concern: Reviewers view the extension of standard PU risk rewriting to pAUC as straightforward with limited methodological novelty and mixed gains across settings.

iWAXe16sLv.one_liner: Separates teacher privileged-information gain from student retention in multimodal on-policy self-distillation, showing hints outperform answers.
iWAXe16sLv.problem: It is unclear whether privileged information (PI) that boosts teacher performance most in multimodal on-policy self-distillation also yields the largest gains in PI-free students.
iWAXe16sLv.method: The authors define PI access gain (direct teacher boost) and PI effectiveness (retained student boost over matched No-PI OPSD), comparing Answer, Hint, and other PI conditions across multimodal tasks and analyzing student visual localization under target-region corruption.
iWAXe16sLv.key_idea: Disentangles direct teacher PI access gain from retained PI-free student effectiveness using matched No-PI on-policy self-distillation controls.
iWAXe16sLv.evidence: Controlled experiments across four multimodal task families and external benchmarks, plus target-region corruption analyses.
iWAXe16sLv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating teacher PI access gain from student PI effectiveness with matched No-PI OPSD controls is a clear, meaningful lens.
iWAXe16sLv.main_concern: Reviewers note limited conceptual novelty beyond prior work like ViCuR and reliance on a single base model (Qwen3.5-4B) without prescriptive PI selection rules.

tN4FNZO748.one_liner: Jointly forecasts driver kinematics, vehicle dynamics, and road demands via directed residual connections for real-time driver monitoring.
tN4FNZO748.problem: Existing driver-monitoring models predict in-cabin activity or traffic-conditioned driver motion in isolation without jointly forecasting driver, vehicle, and road states in real time.
tN4FNZO748.method: TriDrive connects modality-specific encoders (kinematic driver pose, causal CAN-bus dynamics, and frozen V-JEPA 2 road latents with road margins) via directed residual connections in an automation-conditioned transition model, then distills road encoders for 5 Hz on-vehicle warning deployment.
tN4FNZO748.key_idea: Connects driver kinematic, CAN-bus vehicle, and V-JEPA 2 road encoders through directed residual transitions for joint forecasting and distilled real-time warnings.
tN4FNZO748.evidence: Evaluations on AIDE, 197.2 hours of naturalistic BATON driving, on-vehicle comma four deployment (8 GB GPU), and a 14-driver study.
tN4FNZO748.claimed_gains: Achieves 48.05 vs 71.47 All-MPJPE on AIDE, raises BATON PR-AUC by +0.084 (steering onset) and +0.286 (TTC drops), and runs at 5 Hz with 177 ms p95 latency.
tN4FNZO748.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the comprehensive evaluation, including driver-disjoint splits, real-time on-vehicle deployment, and the 14-participant user study.
tN4FNZO748.main_concern: Reviewers question the necessity of the joint forecasting architecture because the deployed warning probe uses only current-state features and all-to-all fusion matches directed connections.

tRQ6E6Zu6s.one_liner: Decomposes GNN accuracy changes under topology perturbations into Break and Repair transitions explained by clean margin and signed structural response.
tRQ6E6Zu6s.problem: Aggregate accuracy under graph topology perturbations hides prediction instability because Broken correct predictions and Repaired incorrect predictions cancel out in the net score.
tRQ6E6Zu6s.method: The authors formulate Break and Repair transitions via a margin-crossing model combining clean margin thresholds, signed perturbation-induced structural displacement measured on a disjoint perturbation bank, and clean-state opportunity weighting.
tRQ6E6Zu6s.key_idea: Models node-level Break and Repair transitions as margin crossings driven by clean boundary distance and signed structural displacement measured on realization-disjoint perturbation banks.
tRQ6E6Zu6s.evidence: Evaluated across development and external node-classification graphs, multiple GNN architectures, perturbation operators, and graph scales.
tRQ6E6Zu6s.claimed_gains: An independently measured structural response signal improves held-out Break/Repair susceptibility AUC beyond clean margin by 0.058–0.113 on development graphs.
tRQ6E6Zu6s.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the intuitive Break/Repair decomposition, the coherent margin-crossing account, and the non-circular disjoint-bank evaluation protocol.
tRQ6E6Zu6s.main_concern: Reviewers question the practical utility and novelty beyond prior prediction-churn literature, noting narrow evidence for the signed response signal and disorganized presentation.

fQ8lsjKggM.one_liner: Benchmarks AI reviewer rhetorical robustness across content-preserving rewrites and proposes SciCore dual-branch content-normalized reviewing.
fQ8lsjKggM.problem: AI reviewers can assign different scores to manuscripts presenting the same science in different wording, and low rewrite variance can mask score collapse across distinct papers.
fQ8lsjKggM.method: The authors define Rhetorical Robustness jointly via rewrite stability and cross-paper discrimination, build the RobustReview benchmark of 1,260 full-manuscript versions, and propose SciCore, which averages a full-manuscript review with a review of an extracted structured science core.
fQ8lsjKggM.key_idea: Averages a full-manuscript AI review with a judgment over an extracted structured science core to balance rewrite stability against cross-paper discrimination.
fQ8lsjKggM.evidence: Evaluated 30 reviewer configurations on RobustReview (1,260 manuscript versions) and compared SciCore primarily on GPT-5.5 with human-alignment and ensemble controls.
fQ8lsjKggM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that jointly measuring rewrite stability and cross-paper discrimination avoids false robustness and that RobustReview provides broad full-manuscript coverage.
fQ8lsjKggM.main_concern: Reviewers question whether rewritten manuscripts preserve exact scientific content and whether the extracted science core omits critical information, alongside limited cross-backbone testing of full SciCore.

kKGYeWp9xH.one_liner: Eliminates quadratic intermediate heatmaps and CPU launch overhead in VRP neural solvers via sparse pair scoring and fused GPU decoding.
kKGYeWp9xH.problem: Heatmap-based neural vehicle routing solvers fail to scale due to quadratic intermediate candidate-graph/heatmap storage and CPU-side kernel-launch overhead during autoregressive decoding.
kKGYeWp9xH.method: SIF constructs candidate graphs using criterion-specific sparse search, stores heatmap scores directly on sparse candidate pairs, fuses the entire autoregressive decoding loop into a single GPU-resident persistent kernel, and adds a low-overhead rescue fallback without altering learned model weights.
kKGYeWp9xH.key_idea: Scores sparse candidate pairs directly to avoid quadratic heatmaps and fuses autoregressive tour decoding into a single persistent GPU kernel with a fallback rescue mechanism.
kKGYeWp9xH.evidence: Evaluated on four representative heatmap-based VRP solvers with stage-wise profiling and component ablations.
kKGYeWp9xH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree SIF targets a real systems bottleneck in heatmap-based VRP inference without retraining and supports its runtime and memory reductions with helpful ablations.
kKGYeWp9xH.main_concern: Reviewers note that individual components (sparse kNN heatmaps, persistent GPU kernels, geometric fallbacks) have precedents in prior routing and LLM systems and that the claimed bottlenecks are specific to certain baseline codebases.

DSJoxz1Vh5.one_liner: Cuts ViT fine-tuning memory and time by caching full-sequence KV states gradient-free and backpropagating only through selected tokens.
DSJoxz1Vh5.problem: PEFT still backpropagates through all input tokens with high activation memory, while token pruning or merging alters forward-pass context.
DSJoxz1Vh5.method: Two-Phase Caching and Activation (TCA) runs a gradient-free full forward pass to cache global keys and values, then selects tokens using the completed forward pass and recomputes only those tokens against the cached KV context to restrict backpropagation while reproducing full-sequence forward outputs.
DSJoxz1Vh5.key_idea: Caches full-sequence keys and values in a gradient-free forward pass, then replays and backpropagates only through selected tokens against that cached context.
DSJoxz1Vh5.evidence: Evaluated across 13 image recognition tasks on multiple ViT scales, plus extensions to multimodal and generative backbones.
DSJoxz1Vh5.claimed_gains: Demonstrates over 60% peak-memory reduction and approximately 45% training-time reduction with minimal accuracy degradation across 13 recognition tasks.
DSJoxz1Vh5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the two-phase KV-caching and selective-backpropagation mechanism intuitive, composable with PEFT methods like LoRA, and effective for reducing memory and training time.
DSJoxz1Vh5.main_concern: Reviewers criticize uncontrolled cross-protocol comparisons against prior selective-backpropagation baselines (TokenTune, TokenSeek) and insufficiently explained token-ranking criteria for multimodal and generative models.

hI2fAYvROC.one_liner: Models cross-component safety interactions in self-evolving agent harnesses with an incrementally updated typed hypergraph for runtime monitoring.
hI2fAYvROC.problem: Individually safe updates to persistent agent harness components (memory, prompts, skills, tools) can interact to cause compositional safety failures, while exhaustive validation is combinatorially intractable.
hI2fAYvROC.method: The authors identify pairwise and 3-way compositional safety failures across agent benchmarks, represent component states as nodes and higher-order safety interactions as hyperedges in a typed hypergraph updated locally on harness changes, and build a hypergraph-guided runtime monitor.
hI2fAYvROC.key_idea: Encodes component states and higher-order safety interactions in a typed hypergraph that updates only local neighborhoods of changed states to guide runtime monitoring.
hI2fAYvROC.evidence: Empirical study of compositional safety failures and runtime monitoring across three safety-related benchmarks.
hI2fAYvROC.claimed_gains: Identifies 43 pairwise and 18 irreducible 3-way compositional safety failures across three safety-related benchmarks; runtime monitoring gains are not stated.
hI2fAYvROC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that compositional safety failures from individually safe harness updates are a practical, overlooked risk for self-evolving agents.
hI2fAYvROC.main_concern: Reviewers question how local neighborhood updates detect newly introduced cross-component interactions not in the historical hypergraph, as well as unclear state granularity and missing repeated-run stability evidence.

al7fSIJ6OI.one_liner: Switches LLM attention parallelism layouts online without halting requests by decoupling attention weight sharding from per-request KV ownership.
al7fSIJ6OI.problem: LLM serving workloads shift mid-execution from high concurrency to a few long generations, but existing engines fix one attention parallel layout at launch because switching requires draining requests.
al7fSIJ6OI.method: SPLASH exploits compact KV caches in MQA/GQA/MLA to decouple weight sharding from KV-cache residency, reusing resident shards and KV blocks in place while overlapping per-layer state transfers with inference, and introduces Decoupled Ownership Parallelism (DOP).
al7fSIJ6OI.key_idea: Decouples attention weight sharding from per-request KV-cache ownership, overlapping per-layer transfers of missing state with inference to switch parallel layouts at step boundaries.
al7fSIJ6OI.evidence: Formulation of layout-switching overhead and empirical evaluations across parallelism layouts, batch sizes, and sequence lengths.
al7fSIJ6OI.claimed_gains: Switches attention parallel layouts at a step boundary with under 0.51% median step overhead.
al7fSIJ6OI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the unified decoupling of weight sharding from KV ownership and the low-overhead online switching design.
al7fSIJ6OI.main_concern: Reviewers highlight missing end-to-end evaluations on realistic changing workloads, missing comparisons to hybrid parallelism or other switching systems, and poor writing quality.

1r4WMgl5iC.one_liner: Aligns variable-rate, multi-channel health sensors with a pretrained LM via a flexible patch embedder, cross-attention, contrastive, and captioning objectives.
1r4WMgl5iC.problem: Existing sensor-language models require fixed channel counts and sampling rates, preventing transfer across heterogeneous wearable and clinical health sensors.
1r4WMgl5iC.method: SLIP combines a flexible patch embedder (FlexMLP) with a repurposed pretrained decoder-only language model connected via cross-attention, trained jointly with contrastive alignment and sensor-conditioned captioning to handle arbitrary sampling rates and input lengths without retraining.
1r4WMgl5iC.key_idea: A flexible weight-resizing patch embedder paired with cross-attention into a pretrained decoder-only LM trained with contrastive and captioning objectives enables transfer across heterogeneous sensor configurations.
1r4WMgl5iC.evidence: Evaluated across 11 healthcare and wearable sensor datasets on retrieval, signal captioning, linear probing, and question answering.
1r4WMgl5iC.claimed_gains: Achieves 77.14% average linear-probing accuracy across 11 datasets, a 3.56% improvement over baselines.
1r4WMgl5iC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that handling heterogeneous sensor channel counts, sampling rates, and sequence lengths within a unified language-aligned framework addresses an important practical problem.
1r4WMgl5iC.main_concern: Reviewers flag large unexplained score discrepancies between main and repeated-run tables (e.g., WISDM and WESAD), underspecified FlexMLP resizing details, and limited justification over simpler pooling or prior SensorLM.

nZURBm0XYQ.one_liner: Diagnoses shortcut correlations and long-CoT sensitivity behind irrelevant-context math distraction, and improves robustness via out-of-domain IC fine-tuning.
nZURBm0XYQ.problem: LLMs are easily distracted by irrelevant context in math reasoning, yet the training-data factors driving this vulnerability are poorly understood.
nZURBm0XYQ.method: Through ablations on irrelevant context and chain-of-thought length during fine-tuning, the authors show that models rely on artifact-operation shortcuts exacerbated by long CoT supervision, and demonstrate that adding even out-of-domain irrelevant context to fine-tuning data improves robustness without harming clean accuracy.
nZURBm0XYQ.key_idea: Controlled fine-tuning ablations link irrelevant-context distraction to long-CoT supervision and shortcut correlations, and show that adding out-of-domain irrelevant context during fine-tuning builds robustness.
nZURBm0XYQ.evidence: Multi-seed experiments on two LLM families across extended GSM-IC (1,319 problems), multiple pruning ratios, and realistic/out-of-domain distractors.
nZURBm0XYQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the systematic empirical investigation of how CoT length and irrelevant-context fine-tuning affect math distraction across two model families and multiple seeds.
nZURBm0XYQ.main_concern: Reviewers point out that pruning by CoT length confounds solution length with problem type and difficulty, the shortcut claim lacks pre-SFT controls, and overlap with prior IC work and out-of-domain numeric IC settings needs clearer separation.

flWYXUxc42.one_liner: Evaluates clinical LMs in 333 clinician-authored sandbox encounters with virtual patients, clinical tools, and step-level scoring.
flWYXUxc42.problem: Most clinical benchmarks evaluate diagnosis on complete case descriptions without testing history-taking, examination ordering, or clinician-verified assessment processes.
flWYXUxc42.method: KlinikeBench provides 333 clinician-authored tasks in isolated sandbox environments with virtual patients, clinical tools, fixed turn budgets, and action constraints. It scores history gathering, examination requests, constraint adherence, and final diagnosis both separately and jointly.
flWYXUxc42.key_idea: Evaluates clinical agents inside clinician-authored sandboxes by scoring multi-turn history taking, tool use, action constraints, and diagnosis separately and jointly.
flWYXUxc42.evidence: Over 35 clinicians authored and evaluated cases, and 31 models across seven model families were tested alongside a clinician dialogue-quality study.
flWYXUxc42.claimed_gains: Across 31 models and seven model families, the best-performing models (e.g., GPT-6-astra and Claude Opus 5) succeed on <30% of tasks.
flWYXUxc42.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the process-level evaluation beyond diagnostic accuracy, clinician authoring, negative-symptom cases, and SFT/RL training-environment exploration.
flWYXUxc42.main_concern: Reviewers question inter-clinician agreement on mandatory tools and must-ask topics, and note insufficient penalization of unnecessary or harmful actions.

1QgEJOThOW.one_liner: Combines coarse-bias reward shaping, space-efficient linear programming, and on-demand transition reconstruction for average-reward MDPs.
1QgEJOThOW.problem: Model-free reinforcement learning in weakly communicating average-reward MDPs under near-linear working space lacks asymptotically optimal span-dependent sample complexity without prior span knowledge.
1QgEJOThOW.method: The algorithm uses reward shaping from a coarse reference bias to shrink the planning value scale, paired with space-efficient linear programming and a randomized square-grid decoder that reconstructs transition probabilities on demand under O(SA) working space. It terminates almost surely without requiring a prior bound on the optimal bias span H.
1QgEJOThOW.key_idea: Applies reference-bias reward shaping and a randomized square-grid decoder for on-demand transition reconstruction within space-efficient linear programming.
1QgEJOThOW.evidence: Theoretical sample-complexity and almost-sure termination guarantees for finite weakly communicating MDPs with a generative model under O(SA) working space.
1QgEJOThOW.claimed_gains: Returns an epsilon-optimal stationary deterministic policy using O~(SAH/epsilon^2 + S^(14/3)A^(4/3)H^(4/3)/epsilon^(4/3)) samples, matching the span-based lower bound as epsilon approaches 0.
1QgEJOThOW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the theoretical advance achieving optimal linear H dependence in near-linear working space without prior knowledge of H.
1QgEJOThOW.main_concern: The lower-order sample complexity term has steep S and A dependence, making the optimal leading term dominate only at extremely small epsilon.

L7FhES3m6f.one_liner: 3D RL courier-shift environment with persistent resource dynamics, event-based trajectory rewards, and weakness-driven curriculum adaptation.
L7FhES3m6f.problem: Embodied agents need executable environments that preserve cross-task resource dependencies like time, energy, and money across long trajectories rather than isolated tasks.
L7FhES3m6f.method: DeliveryGym is a 3D continuous courier-shift environment coupling multimodal tool interaction with persistent world dynamics and simulator-event trajectory rewards. It adapts future training shifts to diagnosed policy weaknesses while holding evaluation fixed.
L7FhES3m6f.key_idea: Couples persistent 3D courier-shift resource dynamics with trajectory rewards and an adaptive curriculum targeting observed policy weaknesses.
L7FhES3m6f.evidence: Evaluated across six models and 13 city maps, including RL training of Qwen3-VL-4B on unseen-city test sets and adaptive-curriculum comparisons at 100 updates.
L7FhES3m6f.claimed_gains: RL improves Qwen3-VL-4B's net income by 54.3% on the unseen-city test set, and adaptive training improves evaluation income by 18% over uniform sampling at 100 updates.
L7FhES3m6f.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the realistic long-horizon resource-constrained problem setting, complete RL harness, and controlled adaptive-curriculum results.
L7FhES3m6f.main_concern: Reviewers ask for clearer delineation of what DeliveryGym adds beyond the underlying DeliveryBench environment and question generality of domain-specific weakness diagnosis.

yY5TDfUS8V.one_liner: Quantizes video deepfake detectors via decision-gradient-constrained orthogonal rotations and perturbation-consistent calibration to preserve forgery cues.
yY5TDfUS8V.problem: Standard post-training quantization distorts subtle spatial artifacts and temporal inconsistencies required for accurate video deepfake detection on edge devices.
yY5TDfUS8V.method: ViGuardQ introduces Dual-Evidence-Constrained (DEC) Rotation, which identifies a sensitive channel subspace via within-frame and cross-frame differential decision gradients and optimizes orthogonal rotations to protect it. It pairs this with Evidence-guided Consistent Response (ECR) Calibration to align quantized responses under aligned and opposite perturbations.
yY5TDfUS8V.key_idea: Protect forgery-sensitive channel subspaces with decision-gradient-guided orthogonal rotations and calibrate quantizers for consistent signed perturbation responses.
yY5TDfUS8V.evidence: Evaluated across six benchmark datasets and eleven detectors/backbones (including DeiT, ViT, and Swin) in cross-dataset settings with component ablations.
yY5TDfUS8V.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree edge deployment of video deepfake detectors is practical and that DEC and ECR are complementary, decision-aware post-training quantization designs.
yY5TDfUS8V.main_concern: Reviewers note insufficient specification of bit-widths and temporal processing for image-based detectors, weakening the video-specific claim, and unclear novelty over prior deepfake quantization work (Tao et al., IJCAI 2025).

3Fq8NvlSTg.one_liner: Proves training-set memorization reverses post-hoc long-tailed classifier corrections and fixes it by refitting on out-of-fold logits.
3Fq8NvlSTg.problem: Two-stage long-tailed recognition methods refit classifiers on training images where tail-class memorization underestimates or reverses head-class bias.
3Fq8NvlSTg.method: The authors theoretically analyze how inflated ground-truth logits on memorized training examples cause post-hoc corrections to under-correct or move toward head classes when the first stage is class-balanced. They restore the correct tailward adjustment by fitting second-stage corrections on memorization-free out-of-fold logits.
3Fq8NvlSTg.key_idea: Fit second-stage long-tailed post-hoc corrections on out-of-fold logits rather than training-set logits to eliminate memorization-induced bias reversal.
3Fq8NvlSTg.evidence: Supported by theoretical analysis and experiments applying out-of-fold refitting to five second-stage methods across CIFAR-LT, ImageNet-LT, and iNaturalist2018.
3Fq8NvlSTg.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the diagnosis of memorization-induced reversal in second-stage long-tailed correction meaningful and backed by theory and consistent empirical improvements.
3Fq8NvlSTg.main_concern: Reviewers cite limited methodological novelty (standard cross-fitting), high training overhead for modest gains on large benchmarks (+1.59% ImageNet-LT, +0.78% iNaturalist2018), unclear writing, and gaps between binary theory and multiclass metrics.

YgMYjM8HkK.one_liner: Derives excess-risk bounds for group-robust continual learning and allocates replay memory via group-balanced or difficulty-adaptive buffers with group identification.
YgMYjM8HkK.problem: Rehearsal-based continual learning treats past tasks equally, causing severe forgetting and large excess risk on rare or difficult latent task groups.
YgMYjM8HkK.method: The authors propose Group-Robust Continual Learning (GRCL) with two bound-guided replay strategies: group-balanced replay and difficulty-adaptive replay. When group identities are unknown, they introduce MMD-based and online-EM group identification methods with theoretical guarantees.
YgMYjM8HkK.key_idea: Allocate continual-learning replay buffers across latent groups according to group-balanced or difficulty-aware excess-risk bounds, paired with MMD or online-EM group identification.
YgMYjM8HkK.evidence: Backed by excess-risk and identification bounds plus experiments on Waterbirds and CelebA.
YgMYjM8HkK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree heterogeneous forgetting across latent groups is an important, underexplored problem and value the theoretical excess-risk framing.
YgMYjM8HkK.main_concern: Reviewers highlight a gap between theory and heuristic experimental allocations, little empirical advantage of difficulty-adaptive over group-balanced replay, and limited dataset/backbone evaluation.

ZyLpUXvg8j.one_liner: Characterizes exact policy-certificate loss from coarsening inverse-propensity normalization into groups and constructs finite-sample rectangular augmented certificates.
ZyLpUXvg8j.problem: Grouping histories to share reward thresholds in confounded off-policy evaluation reduces statistical variance but can weaken the population policy-improvement bound.
ZyLpUXvg8j.method: In a one-step binary-action model under hidden confounding, the authors prove that normalization-coarsening loss equals excess weighted quantile (pinball) loss and give an exact lossless preservation criterion. For finite data with binary rewards, they develop Rectangular Augmented Certification (RAC) providing non-asymptotic coverage under nuisance confidence envelopes.
ZyLpUXvg8j.key_idea: Equate normalization-coarsening certificate loss to excess weighted quantile loss and certify binary-reward policies in finite samples via simultaneous nuisance confidence envelopes.
ZyLpUXvg8j.evidence: Supported by population/finite-sample theorems on standard-Borel spaces and synthetic experiments with ablations.
ZyLpUXvg8j.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the clean exact loss identity handling discrete outcomes, the finite-sample RAC coverage guarantee, and transparent reporting of ablations.
ZyLpUXvg8j.main_concern: Reviewers view the theory as incremental over Tan (2024), note that RAC still requires hard-to-obtain full-history simultaneous nuisance envelopes, and observe that simple fixed thresholds slightly outperform adaptive threshold fitting.

XxzeuVdYtb.one_liner: Adapts remote sensing models to substituted, added, or reduced sensor modalities using a masking-transformer architecture with missing-modality feature hallucination.
XxzeuVdYtb.problem: Remote sensing models trained on fixed sensor suites struggle to adapt when satellites add new sensors, replace modalities, or retire old ones without costly relabeling.
XxzeuVdYtb.method: The authors categorize changing-modality adaptation into Modality Transfer, Addition, and Peeking, and propose DeluluNet. Trained end-to-end from a unimodal teacher and unlabeled multimodal data, DeluluNet uses masking transformers to hallucinate missing modality representations from present ones.
XxzeuVdYtb.key_idea: Predict missing sensor-modality representations from available modalities using masking transformers trained via unimodal-teacher distillation and unlabeled multimodal data.
XxzeuVdYtb.evidence: Evaluated across three remote sensing datasets (including EuroSAT and reBEN) on Transfer, Addition, and Peeking scenarios against baselines like MixMatch, DINOv3, and Panopticon.
XxzeuVdYtb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find adapting remote sensing models to evolving sensor suites practically relevant and the unified feature-hallucination design coherent.
XxzeuVdYtb.main_concern: Reviewers flag irreconcilable inconsistencies across result tables (e.g., EuroSAT and reBEN numbers reversing rankings), limited novelty, few recent baselines, and reliance on correlated Sentinel-2 band subsets rather than distinct sensors.

3tUPFoi80o.one_liner: Measures visuomotor sensitivity in World-Action Models and attacks them by suppressing visual-to-action attention and paired-observation action differences.
3tUPFoi80o.problem: Task success rates do not reveal how strongly World-Action Models couple visual observations to action generation or how vulnerable this coupling is to adversarial attacks.
3tUPFoi80o.method: The authors introduce Visuomotor Sensitivity (VMS) to quantify action-prediction responses to controlled semantic visual changes and identify visual-to-action attention as a key pathway. They propose World-Action Disintegration (WAD), a white-box attack combining visual-to-action attention suppression with a surrogate minimizing action differences across consecutive observations.
3tUPFoi80o.key_idea: Suppress visual-to-action attention while minimizing predicted action differences across consecutive training observations to disintegrate visuomotor coupling in World-Action Models.
3tUPFoi80o.evidence: Evaluated across four WAM architectures on LIBERO, RoboTwin, and a real robot, with seed reproducibility and attention analyses.
3tUPFoi80o.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree probing visuomotor coupling and robustness in World-Action Models is important and that WAD consistently degrades success across multiple architectures and benchmarks.
3tUPFoi80o.main_concern: Reviewers note WAD is a white-box attack, consecutive observations confound visual changes with differing proprioceptive robot states, and VMS does not clearly separate harmful unresponsiveness from appropriate invariance.

xGaSpGMQ4O.one_liner: Mitigates negative transfer in cross-city spatio-temporal forecasting via invariant-environment separation and reliability-weighted fusion.
xGaSpGMQ4O.problem: Aligning full source and target distributions in cross-city spatio-temporal forecasting transfers source-specific spurious correlations and causes negative transfer under domain mismatch.
xGaSpGMQ4O.method: CauCrossNet separates representations into stable invariant predictive features and transient environment-specific variations, enforces consistency across stable-space summaries, applies stable-conditioned target augmentation, and fuses source knowledge weighted by representation compatibility and predictive uncertainty.
xGaSpGMQ4O.key_idea: Separates stable invariant features from transient city-specific variation and gates source-target fusion by representation compatibility and predictive uncertainty.
xGaSpGMQ4O.evidence: Evaluated across five city datasets (e.g., PeMS03->PeMS08) in standard transfer, few-shot, cross-region OOD, temporal-shift, and long-horizon settings against 19 baselines.
xGaSpGMQ4O.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the negative-transfer framing is well-motivated and the evaluation spans diverse transfer regimes with strong results against older baselines.
xGaSpGMQ4O.main_concern: Reviewers point out the lack of a same-backbone full-alignment control to verify the invariant-branch claim, small dataset scale, unvalidated invariance/uncertainty assumptions, and missing recent spatio-temporal foundation baselines.

llCtjFLimR.one_liner: Co-evolves multi-agent prompts and communication topologies as a unified genome via multi-objective Pareto evolutionary search.
llCtjFLimR.problem: Optimizing multi-agent prompts and communication graphs separately misses their coupling, since edge utility depends on how receiving agents are prompted.
llCtjFLimR.method: TCP-MCP encodes agent prompts and communication topologies into a unified executable genome and optimizes accuracy, token cost, and structural complexity via evolutionary search combining FDC-guided initialization with runtime adaptive control from landscape and Pareto-front diagnostics.
llCtjFLimR.key_idea: Jointly optimizes agent prompts and communication graphs as a unified genome using FDC-initialized multi-objective Pareto evolutionary search over accuracy, token cost, and structure.
llCtjFLimR.evidence: Evaluated using DeepSeek-V3.2 on MMLU-Pro, MMLU, GSM8K, and WorkBench against automated graph-generation and debate-style baselines, with staged-optimization ablations and search-cost reporting.
llCtjFLimR.claimed_gains: Achieves 82.66% on MMLU-Pro, 89.96% on MMLU, 96.61% on GSM8K, and 77.31% task success on WorkBench using up to 5.71x fewer deployment tokens than debate-style systems.
llCtjFLimR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the prompt-topology coupling motivation, multi-objective formulation, staged-optimization comparison, and transparent search-cost reporting.
llCtjFLimR.main_concern: Reviewers question the limited novelty of combining standard evolutionary heuristics, weak full-run evidence that one-time FDC guidance improves final genomes, and narrow efficiency gains over simpler baselines like Self-Consistency.

W3EItuYiJM.one_liner: Feeds pretrained vision tokens into later diffusion layers during training and reuses the REPA MLP head as a proxy at inference.
W3EItuYiJM.problem: Representation alignment methods like REPA supervise early diffusion layers and discard the projection head, leaving later velocity-supervised layers without direct semantic access.
W3EItuYiJM.method: RECON injects pretrained vision encoder tokens directly into later diffusion transformer layers during training, and at inference reuses the otherwise discarded REPA MLP projection head to project intermediate backbone features into later layers with zero added parameters.
W3EItuYiJM.key_idea: Conditions later diffusion layers on pretrained vision tokens during training and reuses the alignment MLP projection head as an inference-time semantic proxy.
W3EItuYiJM.evidence: Evaluated across SiT B/L/XL scales, multiple VAEs and vision encoders on ImageNet-256 (unguided and CFG) and text-to-image generation against SiT, REPA, and REG.
W3EItuYiJM.claimed_gains: RECON converges 63x faster than SiT and 25x faster than REPA with no added parameters.
W3EItuYiJM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find reusing the discarded REPA projection head simple and practical, noting consistent unguided convergence speedups across scales and encoders.
W3EItuYiJM.main_concern: Reviewers note weaker CFG performance than REG, limited novelty relative to joint representation generation (REG), recall drops, missing inference-overhead analysis, and shallow mechanistic explanation.

qjcMLfBRLF.one_liner: Diagnoses control-token structural collapse in tool-use RL, mitigates it via policy-gradient masking, and compares supervisory signals.
qjcMLfBRLF.problem: Agentic reinforcement learning for multi-step tool use frequently suffers structural collapse where valid tool calls degenerate into malformed control-token sequences.
qjcMLfBRLF.method: The authors analyze token-level advantage accumulation on repeated control tokens, mask direct policy-gradient terms at control-token positions to stabilize training, and systematically compare off-policy, hint-based, erroneous-trajectory, and teacher-generated process-reflection supervision.
qjcMLfBRLF.key_idea: Identifies advantage concentration on repeated control tokens as a driver of tool-use RL collapse and stabilizes training by masking direct policy gradients at control-token positions.
qjcMLfBRLF.evidence: Token-level diagnostics, control-token masking, and supervisory-signal comparisons under vanilla RL and SFT+RL, primarily using Qwen models on 300 BFCL questions.
qjcMLfBRLF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the detailed empirical diagnosis of structural collapse, the control-token masking mitigation, and honest reporting of both positive and negative supervision results.
qjcMLfBRLF.main_concern: Reviewers find causal evidence for the control-token collapse mechanism insufficient and note narrow empirical scope (small Qwen models, 300 BFCL questions, weak OOD generalization, and inconsistent controls).
